## 2026-10-03 [Detroit Pistons Fantasy Basketball Preview [26/27 NBA Season]](videos/2026-10-03-_O9pc_u5vH0.md)

- [7:10](https://youtu.be/_O9pc_u5vH0?t=430) The speaker never uses straight 9-category rankings to value players. He thinks they are inaccurate and often quoted in bad faith.
  > "I will never ever in a million years refer to a straight nine cat ranking of a player"
- [7:43](https://youtu.be/_O9pc_u5vH0?t=463) If you trust one set of 9-category rankings, you have to trust all of it. You cannot pick and choose which parts are right.
  > "if you believe one set of NAT rankings, you must believe all of them because otherwise a ranking system doesn't work"
- [8:19](https://youtu.be/_O9pc_u5vH0?t=499) First round picks among the big names are generally safe. The exact order does not cause huge swings.
  > "We love the first round. We love the big names. We love the best players."
- [14:23](https://youtu.be/_O9pc_u5vH0?t=863) Steals are very variable from game to game and season to season. Players whose value depends on steals carry extra risk.
  > "we know that on a game byame and season by season basis, these are incredibly variable stats"
- [15:39](https://youtu.be/_O9pc_u5vH0?t=939) Drafting a defense-only, poor-shooting player early can leave your team far behind in points and threes. That build is not for everyone.
  > "you are going to put yourself in a significant points and threes hole. So, it is not for everybody."
- [20:14](https://youtu.be/_O9pc_u5vH0?t=1214) Do not overvalue threes in the draft. Three-point specialists are easy to find on waivers.
  > "It's also one of those reasons why don't overindex on threes because you can find them everywhere on the waiver."
- [19:10](https://youtu.be/_O9pc_u5vH0?t=1150) A Yahoo ADP based on very few drafts can be inflated and misleading.
  > "that's one of those ones where he was drafted in three leagues and it pushes it up."
- [4:05](https://youtu.be/_O9pc_u5vH0?t=245) Minutes tiers: starters play about 29 to 35 minutes and bench players 17 to 20. A '.5 starter' plays about 24 to 25.
  > "we we go starter minutes is 30 29 to 35 regularly. bench players 17 to 20."
- [5:59](https://youtu.be/_O9pc_u5vH0?t=359) Coaches may mislead about player minutes. Be skeptical of coach statements, especially from coaches with a track record of doing it.
  > "prerogative to mislead as a coach. Good for him. But just know that I'm not believing him."
- [30:08](https://youtu.be/_O9pc_u5vH0?t=1808) Stash candidates are most useful in draft-only, best ball, weekly, games-cap, deep-bench and low-transaction leagues.
  > "Draft onlyies, best balls, weeklies, games caps, deep benches, low low transaction leagues."
- [31:17](https://youtu.be/_O9pc_u5vH0?t=1877) The speaker recommends ending the fantasy season on March 28. Yahoo's default end date is April 4.
  > "if you end your leagues on March the 28th, which is my recommended end date, it's not bad."
- [31:42](https://youtu.be/_O9pc_u5vH0?t=1902) Back-to-back counts only range from 13 to 16 across teams, so differences in back-to-backs are not a big deal.
  > "It's only two more than the lowest amount though. The range is 13 to 16. Not that many."

## 2026-10-02 [Would You Take a Flier On a Starting Center at Pick 120?](videos/2026-10-02-ZYllcj4o6_A.md)

- [1:21](https://youtu.be/ZYllcj4o6_A?t=81) Once your starting slots are filled, use bench picks on upside fliers. Round 10 can already be a flier zone.
  > "I'm talking about at least all of your bench slots. Once you start filling once you've filled up all your starters"
- [1:33](https://youtu.be/ZYllcj4o6_A?t=93) Do not draft a player at pick 110 who projects to finish 110th. You can find that kind of value on the waiver wire.
  > "there's no point grabbing a guy at 110 who's going to be 110th. There's no point in that."
- [18:48](https://youtu.be/ZYllcj4o6_A?t=1128) Take upside players in round 10 instead of waiting for their ADP. You usually drop and stream your round 10 to 13 picks anyway.
  > "for most of your teams, you're going to drop your round 10, 11, 12, 13 players nearly all the time."
- [16:34](https://youtu.be/ZYllcj4o6_A?t=994) Projections are a median outcome. When two players have the same projection, prefer the one with the wider range of outcomes. Veterans like Harrison Barnes or Tobias Harris have no realistic path above their projection.
  > "But the band of what he can do is a lot wider than what others can do."
- [8:20](https://youtu.be/ZYllcj4o6_A?t=500) Take a flier on a player only if there is a real chance he starts or gets a role. If reports say he will not start, pass.
  > "So if he might start, I will take the chance on. If we know that he won't, then I won't take it."
- [5:22](https://youtu.be/ZYllcj4o6_A?t=322) Value players against consensus, not on personal bias. Draft a player you don't like when his price and your team's needs make sense.
  > "It's more about how do I value them versus consensus? How do I value their game versus how other people do?"
- [42:27](https://youtu.be/ZYllcj4o6_A?t=2547) Don't draft for the week one schedule or stream just to get extra games early. Accept losses in weeks one and two to hold fliers with longer-term value.
  > "I'm okay to do that and take L's in week one because if I draft Gillespie or use him"
- [29:02](https://youtu.be/ZYllcj4o6_A?t=1742) Injury-prone stashes like Kristaps Porzingis are hard to use in daily-change leagues with small benches. Fit the pick to your format.
  > "If you're in a daily changes league with small benches, it's almost impossible to deal with that."
- [46:22](https://youtu.be/ZYllcj4o6_A?t=2782) Ignore what players say about each other. Players are poor evaluators of talent.
  > "I do not care. players who are the worst evaluators of talent. What they say, not in a million years."
- [37:33](https://youtu.be/ZYllcj4o6_A?t=2253) Avoid single-season myopia. One bad season does not make a player bad.
  > "Miles was pretty bad last season, but people again single season myopia."
- [41:52](https://youtu.be/ZYllcj4o6_A?t=2512) Backups who are one injury away from starting are valid late fliers.
  > "if one of Green, Booker, and Brooks gets hurt, Gillespie will start. He'll play 30 minutes and he'll be worth it."

## 2026-10-01 [Indiana Pacers Fantasy Basketball Preview [26/27 NBA Season]](videos/2026-10-01-EGdhmUgPAWY.md)

  > "there's always concern for me with guys coming back off Achilles injuries that you just lose some efficiency"

  > "I just don't want new players not understanding differences, looking at a rank that explains nothing"
- [10:16](https://youtu.be/EGdhmUgPAWY?t=616) Some players are much better in points leagues than in category leagues. Do not be afraid to take them early in the right format.

- [14:15](https://youtu.be/EGdhmUgPAWY?t=855) If centers are scarce in your draft, it is fine to reach for a center at the top of his range.

- [18:49](https://youtu.be/EGdhmUgPAWY?t=1129) Late round picks should have top 70 upside. Players whose ceiling is their draft slot are droppable.
  > "I don't want my 110th guy to finish 110th. I want him to have top 70 upside or he just becomes droppable."
- [19:07](https://youtu.be/EGdhmUgPAWY?t=1147) A streaming slot is worth about a top 100 player. Drop a low upside player around 115 and stream that spot or take fliers instead.
  > "The value of a streaming slot is a top 100 player. So, this guy that sits there at 115"
- [25:27](https://youtu.be/EGdhmUgPAWY?t=1527) One category specialists look like top 100 players when you punt their weak categories in rankings. That does not make them draftable in standard leagues.

- [29:12](https://youtu.be/EGdhmUgPAWY?t=1752) Bad players on bad teams can still pile up stats because someone has to take the shots and get the rebounds. Those numbers are mostly a product of the team context.
  > "So most of what he did was just a function of the team being really bad."
- [31:55](https://youtu.be/EGdhmUgPAWY?t=1915) Stashing backup players for injury upside makes more sense in weekly leagues, deep bench leagues and games cap leagues.
  > "weekly leagues deep bench leagues games cap leagues maybe we look at uh the Huffster there"
- [34:00](https://youtu.be/EGdhmUgPAWY?t=2040) A team's number of back-to-backs is not a big worry.

## 2026-09-30 [Fantasy Basketball Mock Draft - 9 Cat 10 Team Pick 4](videos/2026-09-30-BjXP9JODDSg.md)

- [7:16](https://youtu.be/BjXP9JODDSg?t=436) Mock drafts have some use, but every draft is very different. Don't fixate on mock trends, or you will be thrown off when your real draft goes differently.
  > "we have to make sure we're not narrow focusing and thinking that that is the only way that a draft can run"
- [6:25](https://youtu.be/BjXP9JODDSg?t=385) In a 10-team league teams are much more stacked than in a 12-team league, so players fall further than usual.
  > "It is a 10-man league so teams are going to be a little bit more stacked"
- [14:55](https://youtu.be/BjXP9JODDSg?t=895) The gap between 10-team and 12-team leagues is big. Some teams get a player like LeBron James with their sixth pick.
  > "The difference in a 10 and 12 man league, it is it is pretty stark, honestly in terms of just how stacked"
- [29:50](https://youtu.be/BjXP9JODDSg?t=1790) In a 10-team league, be more aggressive with upside picks late. The waiver wire is full all season, so failed picks are easy to replace.
  > "this a 10-man league be more aggressive. Your in a in a 10-man league, your waiverwire is brimming."
- [30:19](https://youtu.be/BjXP9JODDSg?t=1819) Late picks with no upside, like a low-ceiling backup, are pointless when better-value options are available.
  > "There's just so many other options who are better value at that spot."
- [28:34](https://youtu.be/BjXP9JODDSg?t=1714) Once you are in flyer territory late in the draft, just take your upside flyers. Don't try to game ADP to wait on them.
  > "it is flyer territory so just take my flyers."
- [15:25](https://youtu.be/BjXP9JODDSg?t=925) Check your team's category strengths and weaknesses during the draft and pick to fill needs, such as adding a big man for rebounds or reaching for assists.
  > "My rebounds need to be improved. So, I probably do need a big man coming up soon."
- [23:11](https://youtu.be/BjXP9JODDSg?t=1391) Sometimes you have to reach to fill a category need, like taking a player a bit early just to get assists.
  > "I think I am desperate for assists. I'm just going to take Dylan Harper. I don't love it."
- [12:48](https://youtu.be/BjXP9JODDSg?t=768) Pairing several injury-risk players is risky. He thinks the market is overindexing on risk for some veterans, which creates value.
  > "It's risky to have this combination of players, but I think we're also a little bit overindexing on the risk"
- [31:21](https://youtu.be/BjXP9JODDSg?t=1881) Panicking when your targets get sniped leads to bad picks. Have a clear backup in your queue.
  > "that's a mistake for me cuz I panicked and which can happen in drafts."
- [20:49](https://youtu.be/BjXP9JODDSg?t=1249) Check positional eligibility as the draft goes so your roster positions are covered, leaving only flex spots at the end.
  > "Got to make sure that my positions look okay. I've just got I need a small forward."
- [34:30](https://youtu.be/BjXP9JODDSg?t=2070) A late pick can serve as insurance on a star by taking a teammate who should start.
  > "I'm just going to take Grimes just as a sort of Luca somewhat insurance."
- [21:17](https://youtu.be/BjXP9JODDSg?t=1277) Role players with upside like McDaniels gain value when a teammate misses time, because they get a usage spike.
  > "If somebody misses time, he just gets a usage spike."

## 2026-09-29 [LEVEL UP: How Fantasy Basketball Auction Drafts TRANSFORM Your Draft Experience](videos/2026-09-29-XnIWJyBB0EM.md)

- [2:59](https://youtu.be/XnIWJyBB0EM?t=179) Auction drafts separate good managers from bad ones much more than snake drafts. It is easy to go off the rails.
  > "It does separate good from bad a lot more than a snake draft."
- [5:00](https://youtu.be/XnIWJyBB0EM?t=300) Auction prices change with any settings change: roster size, number of teams, categories, or the split of starters and bench. Mock draft prices do not carry over between drafts.
  > "Any deviation from setting, you go to a 13-man roster to 14, the auction prices change."
- [6:48](https://youtu.be/XnIWJyBB0EM?t=408) Do not budget for every roster spot. Keep at least one streaming spot. A streaming player is worth about a top 100 to 110 player.
  > "Anyway, don't budget for 13 roster spots because we want a streamer."
- [8:08](https://youtu.be/XnIWJyBB0EM?t=488) Plan with a buffer. For example, plan $185 for 11 core players and keep about $13 of wiggle room, plus $1 players for the last slots.
  > "like $185 for 11 spots. Giving me $13 of wiggle room on some of these players."
- [9:33](https://youtu.be/XnIWJyBB0EM?t=573) Have alternatives ready based on player shapes. Use decision trees: if you miss a target or save money on one, move that money to another slot.
  > "It's about decision trees and lists. So, if I get an extra 10 bucks to play with now,"
- [9:49](https://youtu.be/XnIWJyBB0EM?t=589) Keep some money for late in the draft. If you spend everything early, you cannot compete for late bargains.
  > "It is important, I think, also to reserve some money for later in an auction draft."
- [15:13](https://youtu.be/XnIWJyBB0EM?t=913) Do not just flip a punt toggle and pay the inflated punt value. Overpaying for a player because he fits your build is not value. The goal is to extract value.
  > "Taking a guy that's probably a $10 player and spending 25 cuz he fits your build is not value."
- [16:50](https://youtu.be/XnIWJyBB0EM?t=1010) Read the room. Money spent above projections on some players has to come out of other players' prices, so in a hot room, other prices will dip.
  > "If it's a hot room, where everyone's going well above budget, then you you understand that prices of other guys are going to have to dip."
- [17:06](https://youtu.be/XnIWJyBB0EM?t=1026) If top-end players go below expected prices, mid-round prices will rise because managers still have money to spend.
  > "then the mid-rounds are going to push up because people are going to be sitting there with money"
- [17:16](https://youtu.be/XnIWJyBB0EM?t=1036) Yahoo average and projected prices are only guides. Plans will get disrupted during the draft.
  > "On Yahoo, the average prices and the projected prices, they're just guides."
- [17:59](https://youtu.be/XnIWJyBB0EM?t=1079) Aim to get at least $250 of value from a $200 budget, and up to $300 in an easier league.
  > "You want to get $250 at least of value from a $200 budget."
- [19:41](https://youtu.be/XnIWJyBB0EM?t=1181) Mix up your nominations. In nearly every draft, one of the first 10 or so players nominated goes well under value, and then the room pushes up later prices.
  > "is that nearly every draft, one of the first 10 players or so will be very undervalued."
- [20:30](https://youtu.be/XnIWJyBB0EM?t=1230) Nominate players you do not want, so other teams spend money that could have gone toward your targets.
  > "So generally, if you are nominating, throw someone out there that you don't want."
- [21:13](https://youtu.be/XnIWJyBB0EM?t=1273) In the endgame, a team with a few extra dollars can snipe your $1 nominations, so keep flexible lists with large groups of targets.
  > "lists and and larger size groupings of guys that you want cuz there's always going to be somebody"
- [23:20](https://youtu.be/XnIWJyBB0EM?t=1400) Vary your bidding style (quick bids, draining the timer, pulling out) so opponents cannot predict you. Predictability is your downfall against sharp drafters.
  > "you want to vary the style that you that you bid in cuz you don't want predictability."
- [25:32](https://youtu.be/XnIWJyBB0EM?t=1532) Use price enforcement to make opponents pay up for players they want. Be prepared to get stuck with the player, and know when to stop.
  > "There's also that idea of your price enforcement, making them pay up."
- [27:50](https://youtu.be/XnIWJyBB0EM?t=1670) Stars and scrubs (two top 10 players for half to three quarters of your budget, then cheap players) gets less viable the deeper the league, meaning more teams or bigger rosters.
  > "the deeper your league gets, by the way, the less viable this strategy becomes."
- [28:28](https://youtu.be/XnIWJyBB0EM?t=1708) Hitting on $1 players who become $10 to $15 players has only about a 10% chance. In stars and scrubs, losing a star to injury ruins the team.
  > "those $1 guys turning into $10 or $15 players, that's like a 10% chance."
- [29:53](https://youtu.be/XnIWJyBB0EM?t=1793) A balanced build avoids projected top 20 players and puts the 11 core players within roughly ranks 25 to 75. It has a lower ceiling but is much safer.
  > "So, you probably want your 11 guys within the top 75."
- [30:09](https://youtu.be/XnIWJyBB0EM?t=1809) Losing your best player hurts less in a balanced build, because replacing the 30th best player from waivers is much easier than replacing Jokic.
  > "Because losing the 30th best player in the league, who's your best player, replacing that through waiver wire streaming"
- [30:41](https://youtu.be/XnIWJyBB0EM?t=1841) In deeper formats like 14 teams, stars go for much more, and the $1 players get much worse.
  > "you go to 14 teams, you'll see guys like Jokic go for 90 bucks."
- [39:25](https://youtu.be/XnIWJyBB0EM?t=2365) At least one manager will usually go balanced and bid up mid-round bargains, which weakens stars and scrubs.
  > "is that at least one person is going to push him to 12 or to 13."
- [40:04](https://youtu.be/XnIWJyBB0EM?t=2404) League size guidance: in 8-team leagues go stars and scrubs, in 10-team leagues it can work, and in anything bigger go balanced.
  > "Now, if you your league is eight-man, go stars and scrubs. If it's 10, you can go stars."
- [40:14](https://youtu.be/XnIWJyBB0EM?t=2414) Always adapt to value. If a star falls well below his price because the room is going balanced, take him.
  > "if you're going to a draft and everyone's doing balance, and Jokic is sitting there at 55 bucks, take him."

## 2026-09-29 [Dallas Mavericks Fantasy Basketball Preview [26/27 NBA Season]](videos/2026-09-29-XSPJL_mlFXo.md)

- [7:24](https://youtu.be/XSPJL_mlFXo?t=444) Projections are about what can happen, not only about what a player did the year before.
  > "looking at what happened the year before. We're looking at what can happen. And that's what projections is"
- [8:46](https://youtu.be/XSPJL_mlFXo?t=526) Top rookies often start slow, with poor efficiency for the first two months, and then ramp up in the second half of the season.
  > "first two months with bad efficiency problems and then he was going to ramp up and roll top"
- [14:54](https://youtu.be/XSPJL_mlFXo?t=894) The same draft slot means different things in different league sizes. Take a low-upside player like Washington at 120 in a 14 or 16 team league, but not in a 10 team league. In 12 team leagues, prefer upside for the later picks.
  > "If I'm in a 14-man league and I'm drafting at 120, that's like my eighth best player"
- [15:58](https://youtu.be/XSPJL_mlFXo?t=958) Rankings and projections are interesting, but where you draft a player depends on context.
  > "So rankings are cool. They're not, but they're sort of cool. They're interesting. Projections are interesting, but it's contextual."
- [22:56](https://youtu.be/XSPJL_mlFXo?t=1376) In a 12 team league, average means roughly the 75th ranked player. A player who is close to average in every category can end up around 100th.
  > "And remember in a 12man league average means 75th. So his contributions like it that's why he was"
- [4:19](https://youtu.be/XSPJL_mlFXo?t=259) Lineup choices trickle down. Playing small cuts center minutes and opens wing minutes. Playing big squeezes the forwards.
  > "if they play small ball, it reduces what Lively and Gaffford and that does and that opens up minutes"
- [17:23](https://youtu.be/XSPJL_mlFXo?t=1043) An unproven player with upside is a better late swing than a proven player with a known, limited ceiling.
  > "But the difference between say him and PJ is that we've seen PJ. We haven't seen Merez"
- [19:20](https://youtu.be/XSPJL_mlFXo?t=1160) A low-usage scorer who does nothing else only matters in very deep leagues when injuries free up usage.
  > "because again he doesn't do anything else except score, nothing else."
- [30:19](https://youtu.be/XSPJL_mlFXo?t=1819) Under a new coach, preseason starting lineups are less reliable signals than they were under a coach whose habits you know.
  > "We don't know how Dusty May is going to handle that and we're going to find out coming up"
- [31:46](https://youtu.be/XSPJL_mlFXo?t=1906) Josh recommends March 28 as the fantasy regular season end date. Look at fantasy playoff weeks and back-to-back counts when you judge a team's schedule.
  > "lockdown fantasy basketball, sorry, JLFB, Josh Lloyd fantasy basketball bowls is March the 28th"
- [32:10](https://youtu.be/XSPJL_mlFXo?t=1930) Players coming back from injury may sit back-to-backs, so teams with many back-to-backs hurt those players more.
  > "they have the league maximum 16 back to backs, which impacts Derek Lively"

## 2026-09-29 [Cleveland Cavaliers Fantasy Basketball Preview [26/27 NBA Season]](videos/2026-09-29-NmdNvAz08oE.md)

- [5:17](https://youtu.be/NmdNvAz08oE?t=317) Big men who split time between power forward and center usually put up better fantasy numbers at center: more blocks, more rebounds and a higher field goal percentage.
  > "if you are a big man and you're playing power forward and center, your fantasy numbers improve when you play center"
- [5:44](https://youtu.be/NmdNvAz08oE?t=344) At power forward, a big man plays further out on the perimeter, relies more on his shooting and is not the only source of rim protection.
  > "If you're the four you're further out on the perimeter. You rely have to rely on your shooting"
- [30:48](https://youtu.be/NmdNvAz08oE?t=1848) The fantasy playoff schedule matters most for early picks. He does not want his best player to have a two-game week in the semifinals or championship.
  > "your best player will have a two-game week in your championship or semi-finals. And that is a no-go for me."
- [31:19](https://youtu.be/NmdNvAz08oE?t=1879) Schedule matters less for mid and late picks. He does not worry much about it when taking chances on later players.
  > "I don't care that much if I'm taking chances on Jarrett Allen or Jalen Tyson or Peyton Watson."
- [30:22](https://youtu.be/NmdNvAz08oE?t=1822) He recommends that fantasy leagues end on March 28th.
  > "If you play a league that ends on March 28th, my recommended end date, they play four games"
- [14:30](https://youtu.be/NmdNvAz08oE?t=870) He calls some players nine-cat fluffies: the traditional Z-score method that includes turnovers makes them look better than they really are.
  > "where the traditional Z score method including turnovers makes this player look good. And I would posit that he's not."
- [29:08](https://youtu.be/NmdNvAz08oE?t=1748) In stash formats (roto, weekly, deep bench, games-cap leagues), players who are bad in real life can still have fantasy value when their team's depth is poor.
  > "Shout out to Mo Bamba and Bol Bol. But he puts up fantasy value. Because the depth is horrible."
- [19:01](https://youtu.be/NmdNvAz08oE?t=1141) Upside that depends on injuries to other players is not something you want to rely on.
  > "the upside I think only really comes through here for Payton in a situation where there are injuries to other people"
- [26:26](https://youtu.be/NmdNvAz08oE?t=1586) Whether to fade a player depends on his price. He would fade a player at a high rank but might take him later.
  > "Am I fading him at 49 where he's ranked on ESPN? Yeah, like yes. No question about that."
- [23:23](https://youtu.be/NmdNvAz08oE?t=1403) Bench players on teams with poor depth become streaming targets during heavy schedule stretches when starters rest.
  > "So, he'll be a really key streaming target and a deeper league, deeper bench type player"

## 2026-09-28 [Chicago Bulls Fantasy Basketball Preview [26/27 NBA Season]](videos/2026-09-28-3Qm5wLjhvTw.md)

- [6:41](https://youtu.be/3Qm5wLjhvTw?t=401) Points, rebounds and assists count the same as other categories, but they vary less from game to game and season to season. That makes them more reliable to build a team around.
  > "percentages, but you should treat them slightly differently because of the game-to-ame and season to season variance"
- [7:36](https://youtu.be/3Qm5wLjhvTw?t=456) A reliable points, rebounds and assists player is better than a player whose value comes from steals, blocks and percentages, because the production repeats more reliably.
  > "Like versus being a steals, blocks, and free throw guy or a steals, blocks, and field goal guy"
- [9:26](https://youtu.be/3Qm5wLjhvTw?t=566) No player is a must grab. Do not reach. Value comes from the gap between where you draft a player and where he finishes. Getting about 40 spots of value is almost a league winner.
  > "Nobody is the must grab player, right? So, if you think, well, I've got to get Balis."
- [18:33](https://youtu.be/3Qm5wLjhvTw?t=1113) Rankings differ a lot between Yahoo, ESPN and Fantrax, so whether a player is a bust or a steal depends on your platform and format.
  > "This is where the difference in platforms is important. He's been aggressively ranked up on Yahoo."
- [23:34](https://youtu.be/3Qm5wLjhvTw?t=1414) A 12 team league has about 120 starting level players. A 16 team league drafts about 200 players.
  > "A 12 team league is 120 players who were starters."
- [25:07](https://youtu.be/3Qm5wLjhvTw?t=1507) Do not value a player based on whether he won or ruined your league last season. Last season will not repeat.
  > "reassess everything that you're doing because that's not how any of this works. We're not repeating last season."
- [25:42](https://youtu.be/3Qm5wLjhvTw?t=1542) Your last pick or last few picks should be upside flyers.
  > "your last pick and last couple of picks should probably just be an upside flyer"
- [29:04](https://youtu.be/3Qm5wLjhvTw?t=1744) Two threes per game is league average in fantasy, so a shooter who only hits two threes is nothing special.
  > "he's hitting two threes a game, remember two threes is league average for fantasy"
- [34:14](https://youtu.be/3Qm5wLjhvTw?t=2054) Leaving out teams with two game playoff weeks, fantasy schedules are mostly comparable and should not change player valuations much. The recommended season end date is March 28. The Yahoo default end date is April 4.
  > "most team schedules outside of teams that have two game playoff weeks, they're all relatively comparable"

## 2026-09-27 [Charlotte Hornets Fantasy Basketball Preview [26/27 NBA Season]](videos/2026-09-27-CRLSsoGhb2w.md)

- [9:21](https://youtu.be/CRLSsoGhb2w?t=561) Avoid drafting players who start the season injured, but the season is 25 weeks long. Do not drop a player with a short-term injury too far.
  > "But the season is 25 weeks long. So, how you valued Kniple before, don't drop it too far down."
- [9:27](https://youtu.be/CRLSsoGhb2w?t=567) Hamstring injuries tend to happen again. A long ruling at the start can mean the team is being careful or that the injury is serious.
  > "Now, hamstrings are prone to re-injury."
- [16:37](https://youtu.be/CRLSsoGhb2w?t=997) Do not judge a player only by last season's rank. Look at the context, such as injuries, minutes limits and role.
  > "take off the single season blinkers because there are plenty of reasons for this."
- [20:16](https://youtu.be/CRLSsoGhb2w?t=1216) Do not boost a fill-in starter much because of a short injury to a starter. The injury may last only a few games or none.
  > "just because Knippel may miss one or two games, I don't think you need to go crazy on grabbing Grayson Allen."
- [26:34](https://youtu.be/CRLSsoGhb2w?t=1594) Players on teams nobody pays attention to often get overlooked in drafts and can be good value.
  > "because they're the Hornets and no one cares about them is that a lot of their players slip through the cracks."
- [27:38](https://youtu.be/CRLSsoGhb2w?t=1658) Stash candidates fit weekly lock leagues, games-cap formats and deep-bench leagues. In 16-team leagues, draft promising rookies.
  > "If I'm in a deep league that goes to 16 teams, I'm drafting him."
- [30:03](https://youtu.be/CRLSsoGhb2w?t=1803) The number of back-to-backs barely matters. The gap between 13 and 16 is about one game every two months.
  > "the difference between 13 back-to-backs and 16 back-to-backs over the course of a season is three."
- [32:14](https://youtu.be/CRLSsoGhb2w?t=1934) Be careful with auction mock drafts. The information from them can mislead more than it helps.
  > "it has a lot of information that can be misleading versus being helpful."

## 2026-09-26 [Brooklyn Nets Fantasy Basketball Preview [26/27 NBA Season]](videos/2026-09-26-3UGI05PDvrE.md)

- [2:20](https://youtu.be/3UGI05PDvrE?t=140) The new anti-tanking lottery reforms should make March basketball more competitive across most of the league.
  > "I think it's going to create more competitive basketball in March."
- [3:40](https://youtu.be/3UGI05PDvrE?t=220) A team with no reason to lose and no reason to win in March can cut veteran minutes to develop young players. Factor that into the value of its veterans.
  > "The incentive is not there to lose, but for them, the incentive is not there to win either."
- [9:45](https://youtu.be/3UGI05PDvrE?t=585) A player moving from a good team to a bad team does not automatically put up bigger numbers. His usage can rise while his playing time falls.
  > "I don't think it's as simple as from good team to bad team, all of his numbers will rise"
- [13:54](https://youtu.be/3UGI05PDvrE?t=834) Some players are worth very different amounts in points leagues and category leagues, so judge their price separately for each format.
  > "But for points leagues, it's too high. And that's the difference. Sharp's value differs between the two"
- [17:33](https://youtu.be/3UGI05PDvrE?t=1053) Rounds 10 to 13 are the place to take flyers on upside players.
  > "when we're talking about what we do in round 10, 11, 12 of a"
- [17:41](https://youtu.be/3UGI05PDvrE?t=1061) Rookie point guards are usually bad, especially for their first two to three months. If you draft one who starts, hold him until about Thanksgiving before judging. Some, like De'Aaron Fox and Darius Garland, were never worth rostering as rookies.
  > "But historically, rookie point guards are bad, especially for the first two to three months."
- [23:51](https://youtu.be/3UGI05PDvrE?t=1431) Take late flyers knowing you can drop them if things are not working after a few weeks.
  > "we take that flyer in the last rounds understanding that we can be ready to move on"
- [24:05](https://youtu.be/3UGI05PDvrE?t=1445) Stash candidates matter most in roto, games-cap head-to-head, deep-bench and weekly-lock leagues.
  > "as a stash option in stashable formats roto games cap head-to-head games cap deep bench leagues and weekly lock leagues"
- [28:50](https://youtu.be/3UGI05PDvrE?t=1730) Auction values depend on the total money available, the number of teams and each team's budget. Enter your budget in your league settings to get correct values.
  > "the prices depend on how much money is available, how many teams are in the league"
- [29:54](https://youtu.be/3UGI05PDvrE?t=1794) Auction mock drafts do not carry over to real drafts. Once one player goes well under his expected price, everyone's thinking changes and the rest of the draft shifts.
  > "as soon as one player goes $10 under their budget, every mindset changes in the draft."
- [30:14](https://youtu.be/3UGI05PDvrE?t=1814) Auction prices change with league size and bench size, so prices from one league mean little in another. A snake draft keeps roughly the same order across leagues.
  > "all the prices are irrelevant anyway. Whereas in a snake draft, there can be slight differences"

## 2026-09-25 [Boston Celtics Fantasy Preview | Can Jayson Tatum & Paul George DESTROY ADP?](videos/2026-09-25-Bi1cEM03k9Y.md)

- [33:22](https://youtu.be/Bi1cEM03k9Y?t=2002) In drafts, value generally beats positional need. Do not go in with a fixed plan to take a certain position in a certain round.
  > "But as a general rule, value just trumps whatever it is you're looking for"
- [34:33](https://youtu.be/Bi1cEM03k9Y?t=2073) Use mock drafts to practice being flexible and trying different paths, not to repeat the same pattern. Muscle memory from mocks can make you panic in a real draft.
  > "Have a mockdraft to be flexible, not to repeat the same pattern"
- [31:25](https://youtu.be/Bi1cEM03k9Y?t=1885) Back-to-back counts matter only a little. The gap between the best and worst team is about three back-to-backs over a 25-week season.
  > "between the best backto-back team and the worst is three backto-backs over the course of a season"
- [31:09](https://youtu.be/Bi1cEM03k9Y?t=1869) The quality games cutoff should be at least 10 games on a day, and the difference over a season is only about six games.
  > "the cut off for quality games should be at least 10 games played on a day"
- [6:24](https://youtu.be/Bi1cEM03k9Y?t=384) Starting usually means more minutes, so a starting role helps a player's fantasy value.
  > "starting inherently gives you a better run at more minutes"
- [4:55](https://youtu.be/Bi1cEM03k9Y?t=295) Do not lean on stats from when one star was off the court if the roster has since added other high-usage players. That data does not fit the new situation.
  > "none of that data accounts for having Paul George there"
- [10:00](https://youtu.be/Bi1cEM03k9Y?t=600) ADPs tend to just follow what happened last season.
  > "the ADPs just seem to follow on exactly what happened last season"
- [29:50](https://youtu.be/Bi1cEM03k9Y?t=1790) Players who play limited games and minutes waste a roster spot in leagues where you must always use the slot. They are easier to hold in stash-friendly formats like weekly lock, roto, or deep leagues with games caps.
  > "in 22 minutes, and that's a bit of a waste of that roster spot"

## 2026-09-25 [The Atlanta Hawks Starter I’m Targeting Every Draft](videos/2026-09-25-4gw4W4RTolY.md)

- [1:37](https://youtu.be/4gw4W4RTolY?t=97) Avoid heavy mock drafting early in September. Injury news, preseason and media day change a lot of draft opinions.
  > "And it's why I don't like to go really heavy mock drafting early in September"
- [6:04](https://youtu.be/4gw4W4RTolY?t=364) Drafting several players from the same NBA team is fine, probably up to three. It is more acceptable if the team has no two-game weeks in the fantasy playoffs. Five is too many.
  > "I have no problem with drafting multiple players from the same team. Probably up to three"
- [13:58](https://youtu.be/4gw4W4RTolY?t=838) Nine-cat rankings can inflate some players. If you use a nine-cat ranking to value a player, you have to accept every result that ranking produces. If you don't believe those results, don't rely on the numbers.
  > "if you want to quote a nine cat ranking in your evaluation of a player then you have to stand on business"
- [10:14](https://youtu.be/4gw4W4RTolY?t=614) Taking a player a few spots too early costs little. If you draft someone at 10 and he finishes 17th, it is not the end of the world.
  > "If you take Jayen at 10, he finishes 17th, oh well,"
- [9:27](https://youtu.be/4gw4W4RTolY?t=567) A player can be fine to draft at a given spot in points leagues but too early in category leagues. Value each format separately.
  > "He's going at like 8 n 10, that sort of range, which for points leagues, totally okay."
- [16:31](https://youtu.be/4gw4W4RTolY?t=991) Extreme hot shooting stretches, like elite true shooting over two months, usually do not stick. Expect them to regress.
  > "There is a lot that happened with him last season though, second half of the year in particular that will not stick."
- [18:28](https://youtu.be/4gw4W4RTolY?t=1108) Don't value players on a single season. Elite skills like steals can bounce back after a down year (elastic band theory).
  > "If we're going to talk elastic band theory on the on the steels, he's that good at it."
- [26:33](https://youtu.be/4gw4W4RTolY?t=1593) A backup point guard is not automatically a handcuff when the team has several ball handlers. Wings can absorb the role instead.
  > "So, it's not the traditional backup point guard sort of scenario that we often sort of like in a fantasy situation."
- [31:32](https://youtu.be/4gw4W4RTolY?t=1892) The best stash is a clear one-for-one backup who would start and play 30-plus minutes if the starter got hurt.
  > "Now, he is not a fantastic permanent producer, but that is a clear one for one."
- [32:01](https://youtu.be/4gw4W4RTolY?t=1921) Only stash players in stash-friendly formats like roto, weekly, deep bench or games-cap leagues. Don't do it in standard daily leagues with small benches.
  > "you're in a regular league that has daily changes with 10 starters and three bench or four bench, don't do it."
- [28:53](https://youtu.be/4gw4W4RTolY?t=1733) His recommended fantasy season end date is March 28. He thinks leagues can go one week later because of the lottery reforms.
  > "but I'm going to go with March 28th because I do think that we can push an extra week given the lottery reforms."
- [34:45](https://youtu.be/4gw4W4RTolY?t=2085) Now that Yahoo has removed IL+, convert the old IL+ spots into regular IL spots rather than bench spots. If you had five injury spots before, keep five.
  > "If you had five total injury spots before, have five now."
- [34:04](https://youtu.be/4gw4W4RTolY?t=2044) Turning IL spots into bench spots hurts teams with many injuries. It makes good teams better and bad teams worse, which causes earlier disengagement.
  > "You don't want the good teams getting better and the bad teams getting worse because then you have disengagement"
- [25:20](https://youtu.be/4gw4W4RTolY?t=1520) Yahoo is a bad platform for dynasty leagues.
  > "If you are in a dynasty league on Yahoo, number one, you should not be because they are bad for that format"

## 2026-09-24 [Fantasy Basketball Mock Draft - Pick 8 In A 9 Cat H2H Draft](videos/2026-09-24-_vbAP5y182A.md)

- [9:21](https://youtu.be/_vbAP5y182A?t=561) When punting free throws around Giannis, you still need to get assists or threes in the early rounds. You do not need to chase low free throw guys.
  > "You got to get you got to get assists or threes in these earlier rounds."
- [12:03](https://youtu.be/_vbAP5y182A?t=723) Do not worry about a team tanking when drafting a good player from that team.
  > "I'm not concerned with tanking and you shouldn't be either."
- [10:54](https://youtu.be/_vbAP5y182A?t=654) Pairing two injury-risk stars (like Anthony Davis and Kawhi Leonard) on one team is very risky.
  > "We can talk about value but pairing Anthony Davis and Kawhi Leonard is very risky."
- [14:24](https://youtu.be/_vbAP5y182A?t=864) When your team is weak in a category like assists, do not overindex on chasing it.
  > "So, I'm not going to overindex on chasing assists."
- [15:47](https://youtu.be/_vbAP5y182A?t=947) Drafts vary a lot because many players have similar value. Stay adaptable instead of planning a perfect build.
  > "There's so much variance with the similarities between players and overall value that you it's hard"
- [18:13](https://youtu.be/_vbAP5y182A?t=1093) In 9-cat, do not draft players whose value comes mostly from points too early. This is not a points league.
  > "Well, that is incredibly early on Steph Castle. This is not a points league, guys."
- [8:38](https://youtu.be/_vbAP5y182A?t=518) Players coming back from Achilles injuries carry a risk of compensation injuries elsewhere in the body.
  > "I'm just I'm a little cautious of compensation injuries, like a hamstring that caused him to miss a week and a half"
- [22:33](https://youtu.be/_vbAP5y182A?t=1353) Avoid big reaches. A swing is fine, but a pick the player has almost no chance to beat is a mistake.
  > "That's when I talk about don't make mistakes. Don't take trips on treacherous roads"
- [22:23](https://youtu.be/_vbAP5y182A?t=1343) When you take a risky player, check how many other big risks are already on your roster. Do not stack risks.
  > "Now, whenever you're taking a risky sort of option like Edy, is there any other big risks there?"
- [37:06](https://youtu.be/_vbAP5y182A?t=2226) Drafting a backup center and waiting for the starter to be traded is usually a waste, especially if he is not a strong per-minute producer.
  > "That's like a backup center that you're waiting for Sabonis to be traded. It may never happen"
- [38:10](https://youtu.be/_vbAP5y182A?t=2290) Do not draft safe, low-upside veterans just to win the projected standings in the draft room.
  > "sometimes they feel like they're used by people to try and win the projected standings in a draft"
- [38:42](https://youtu.be/_vbAP5y182A?t=2322) In late rounds, ask whether a player is a starter or could become one.
  > "Are they starters or can they be starters?"
- [41:57](https://youtu.be/_vbAP5y182A?t=2517) Late-round fliers are often drops. You take them to see what their role turns out to be.
  > "probably going to be drops, honestly. But we just want to see what their role turns out to be."
- [38:58](https://youtu.be/_vbAP5y182A?t=2338) Players who only pay off if someone else gets hurt are poor late picks.
  > "Colin Gillespie, you're waiting on injuries for that to pay off cuz without injuries it won't."

## 2026-09-23 [Fantasy Basketball Punting: Not as Complicated as You Think](videos/2026-09-23-C4vlgpJ62NI.md)

- [1:09](https://youtu.be/C4vlgpJ62NI?t=69) Punting does not apply in points leagues. It is only for category leagues.
  > "Punting is not a thing in points leagues. I've had many people over the years ask me that."
- [2:32](https://youtu.be/C4vlgpJ62NI?t=152) Punting means ignoring one or more categories and acting as if they do not exist.
  > "Punting is ignoring a category/categories. That's all. It's just ignoring a"
- [4:00](https://youtu.be/C4vlgpJ62NI?t=240) Fantasy value is finite. Spreading it over fewer categories raises your strength in each one, so punting simplifies decisions.
  > "You have a finite amount of value that's sitting around in a fantasy league. So if you can pump it"
- [6:29](https://youtu.be/C4vlgpJ62NI?t=389) Punting is not trying to be bad. You target the other categories and accept whatever happens in the punted one. You can still win it sometimes.
  > "You're not trying to make the category bad. You can punt a category, turnovers, for example, and you can win them."
- [8:44](https://youtu.be/C4vlgpJ62NI?t=524) Do not fill your team with bad free throw players after taking Giannis. Your targets are still every player.
  > "You do not need to accumulate all bad free throw centers with Giannis. If you get a player with good free throws, that's okay."
- [7:34](https://youtu.be/C4vlgpJ62NI?t=454) Head-to-head playoffs need only 5 category wins, so even balanced teams end up punting something in the playoffs.
  > "in the head-to-head playoffs? You've got to win five. So, how do you win five? Well, by not paying as much attention"
- [8:09](https://youtu.be/C4vlgpJ62NI?t=489) Punting is not the only way to win. You win fantasy with big value picks and smart waiver moves.
  > "the way to win fantasy is big value picks and smart wave wire moves."
- [9:09](https://youtu.be/C4vlgpJ62NI?t=549) Lloyd ignores turnovers in every head-to-head league.
  > "This is how I approach every head league. I don't even care that turnovers exist."
- [9:48](https://youtu.be/C4vlgpJ62NI?t=588) Watch category correlations. High assists go with high turnovers. Low turnovers go with low points and assists. High blocks go with high rebounds and FG%.
  > "a player that gets high assists will get high turnovers. A player that has low turnovers will have low points and low assists."
- [10:20](https://youtu.be/C4vlgpJ62NI?t=620) If you chase low-block players when punting blocks, your rebounds and FG% will suffer too.
  > "that almost assuredly means your rebounds are going to be below par and you're going to struggle in field goal percentage."
- [10:30](https://youtu.be/C4vlgpJ62NI?t=630) When you punt assists, check your threes, steals and FT%, because low-assist players often struggle there. Punting assists also brings turnovers down automatically.
  > "am I getting enough threes? Are my steals okay? What's my free throw percentage looking like?"
- [11:49](https://youtu.be/C4vlgpJ62NI?t=709) Punt rankings lie, because they remove only your weak category and not everyone else's. Lloyd's DURANT ranking tries to correct for this.
  > "What if you take the other person's worst category out, where do they go? And that's what Durant"
- [12:36](https://youtu.be/C4vlgpJ62NI?t=756) Do not avoid the punted category's player types. If you punt a guard stat (for example FT% with Giannis), draft guards in two of the next three rounds. Otherwise you slide into a 4 or 5 category punt.
  > "If you're punting assists and guard stats, free throw percentage, for example, with Giannis, draft guards in round two and three"
- [13:19](https://youtu.be/C4vlgpJ62NI?t=799) You can change your punt at any time: mid draft, mid season or mid week.
  > "you can change your punt mid draft, mid-season, midweek, whenever."
- [17:42](https://youtu.be/C4vlgpJ62NI?t=1062) First and second round pairing is nonsense. Any sensible first round pick plus a second round value can win. You only go wrong by reaching for a lesser player.
  > "second round player in round two. Guess what? You're on the way. You're going to win."
- [19:16](https://youtu.be/C4vlgpJ62NI?t=1156) What matters is your 7 or 8 man core, not the two-player pair.
  > "What is important is what is your seven or eightman core. That is what is important"
- [18:48](https://youtu.be/C4vlgpJ62NI?t=1128) Treat best player available as a group of roughly equal options and take one of them. There is no single true best option.
  > "There might be six different guys to pick from and generally if you're okay in that area, take one"
- [24:32](https://youtu.be/C4vlgpJ62NI?t=1472) FG% and FT% vary a lot game to game, so punting one of them works well in head-to-head.
  > "So, the idea of punting a variable category is pretty useful in a head-to-head format."
- [25:12](https://youtu.be/C4vlgpJ62NI?t=1512) Threes are easy to find on the waiver wire.
  > "So now you're in a threes hole but we also know we can get threes off the wire."
- [30:22](https://youtu.be/C4vlgpJ62NI?t=1822) Points, assists and FT% are the scarcest categories later in drafts. If you don't get them early, you can just punt them.
  > "Points become the hardest. They are the most scarce. assists, free throw percentage, they're the most scarce categories."
- [37:00](https://youtu.be/C4vlgpJ62NI?t=2220) Assists, rebounds and points are the most stable categories year to year and game to game.
  > "that's useful in fantasy because they are the most stable categories year on year and game by game"
- [31:25](https://youtu.be/C4vlgpJ62NI?t=1885) Stay flexible in drafts. If someone takes your target, take the next player rather than locking into a planned pair.
  > "I just grab the next guy and we'll be fine. We'll figure it out. Be malleable. Be flexible."
- [39:39](https://youtu.be/C4vlgpJ62NI?t=2379) Do not push up players who gain value in punt rankings, such as bad FT% players, just to secure them.
  > "doesn't mean you need to push him up because I got to secure all the bad free throw guys. You don't."
- [39:04](https://youtu.be/C4vlgpJ62NI?t=2344) Your first four picks and then your first eight picks need to make sense together.
  > "is your first four picks and then your first eight picks. They have to make sense."
- [35:41](https://youtu.be/C4vlgpJ62NI?t=2141) First round players all have high turnovers, because turnovers are a third of the usage formula.
  > "The first round of players all have bad turnovers. Giannis might have more than somebody, but it's not that big of a deal."
- [41:51](https://youtu.be/C4vlgpJ62NI?t=2511) Use at least three of your last four picks on upside flyers who could beat their draft spot by 40 to 50 places.
  > "What I want to do in the last four rounds in at least three of them is take upside flyers."
- [42:21](https://youtu.be/C4vlgpJ62NI?t=2541) Don't set rigid stat or position targets by round. Plans break once picks start, especially in auctions. Fill positions, and get the early-scarce stats only if you want them.
  > "no matter what draft you're in, go doubly for auction. As soon as something happens in a draft, your plan's gone."

## 2026-09-22 [The Points League Bust You Can’t Ignore](videos/2026-09-22-QbdrhJd7LiA.md)

- [1:13](https://youtu.be/QbdrhJd7LiA?t=73) Calling a player a bust does not mean you should never draft him. It means the market is valuing him wrongly at his current price.
  > "What does a bust mean? Does it mean you don't draft them? No, that's not what it means."
- [2:34](https://youtu.be/QbdrhJd7LiA?t=154) Yahoo rankings are format agnostic, so they do not fit any one format, and ADP tends to follow them. Do not trust them for points leagues.
  > "Yahoo's rankings are format agnostic. They throw an X rank out there. What does it mean?"
- [3:42](https://youtu.be/QbdrhJd7LiA?t=222) Format matters. A player who is good value in category leagues can be a bust in points leagues.
  > "in a points league. And this is where again format is important in a points league."
- [7:55](https://youtu.be/QbdrhJd7LiA?t=475) Players whose Yahoo ranks are boosted by 9-category value are hard to value correctly for points leagues.
  > "these are the guys again that get real nine cap fluffed which creates issues with trying to assign their value for points leagues"
- [15:55](https://youtu.be/QbdrhJd7LiA?t=955) Not every drafter knows why a player is ranked where he is, so many people get fooled by bad ranks.
  > "not everyone knows why players are in certain positions. So they can get fooled."
- [16:27](https://youtu.be/QbdrhJd7LiA?t=987) In points leagues, minutes drive usage, usage drives scoring and scoring drives fantasy points. A player who only scores needs big volume to pay off.
  > "minutes begets usage, usage begets scoring, scoring begets fantasy points."
- [17:37](https://youtu.be/QbdrhJd7LiA?t=1057) Play the prediction game. Project a realistic stat line for a player and ask whether it would really justify his draft spot.
  > "play the prediction game. What do you think a reasonable predicted stat line is"
- [19:25](https://youtu.be/QbdrhJd7LiA?t=1165) Avoid single-season myopia. Look at more than one past season, for example when comparing games played.
  > "I want you to really be cautious of single season myopia."
- [22:30](https://youtu.be/QbdrhJd7LiA?t=1350) Last season's finish is not the final word, but it shows how much a player has to improve to justify his rank.
  > "it's a good indication to see how much someone needs to maybe improve to hit this number."
- [20:41](https://youtu.be/QbdrhJd7LiA?t=1241) ESPN default points scoring penalizes missed shots, so inefficient shooters lose value there.
  > "ESPN default scoring penalizes missed shots."
- [22:02](https://youtu.be/QbdrhJd7LiA?t=1322) ESPN gives separate points league ranks, but its ADP mixes formats together and does not mean much.
  > "ESPN splits them up. They go, "Here's your points league ranks." Now, they're ADPs."
- [33:03](https://youtu.be/QbdrhJd7LiA?t=1983) Playoff schedules are the least important factor at draft time. Use them only as a tiebreaker between equal players. Do not take a worse player for a better playoff schedule.
  > "Hey, should I take a worse player who's got a better playoff schedule?" No, you shouldn't."
- [33:13](https://youtu.be/QbdrhJd7LiA?t=1993) Later in the season, playoff schedules matter through smart streaming and avoiding two-game weeks.
  > "it becomes more important about maxing out through smart streaming, avoiding a twoame week if it's close"
- [33:46](https://youtu.be/QbdrhJd7LiA?t=2026) Hitting on value picks in the draft is probably the biggest factor in winning a league.
  > "Drafting and nailing the value picks is probably the number one thing that contributes to winning."
- [34:28](https://youtu.be/QbdrhJd7LiA?t=2068) The waiver wire matters as much as the draft. Grab hot players who stay hot, and stream to get a games-played edge in head-to-head.
  > "using it to max out your games in certain spots and taking that games played advantage in a head-to-head format."
- [34:37](https://youtu.be/QbdrhJd7LiA?t=2077) Overall, the name of the game is value: from the draft, streaming, hot waiver pickups and short-term injury replacements.
  > "the name of the game is value. get value through streaming, hot wave wide pickups, short-term injury replacements"

## 2026-09-21 [Fantasy Basketball Points League Sleepers - All The Yahoo & ESPN Values](videos/2026-09-21-egRrai3Ax38.md)

- [4:52](https://youtu.be/egRrai3Ax38?t=292) Yahoo removed IL+. Players tagged out or injured can now go on IL right away. Questionable, doubtful and probable players cannot.
  > "I plus no longer exists the rules for IIL are different out tags now qualify"
- [3:22](https://youtu.be/egRrai3Ax38?t=202) The old trick of stashing questionable players on IL gave only a small edge. Streaming through the open spot gave more flexibility.
  > "I think just in general streaming through the spot gave you more flexibility"
- [4:07](https://youtu.be/egRrai3Ax38?t=247) He is not sure injury prone players should drop further because of the IL change. They can now go on IL as soon as they are ruled out, without waiting.
  > "now as soon as he misses a game, as soon as he's ruled out, you"
- [5:14](https://youtu.be/egRrai3Ax38?t=314) How much the IL change matters depends on how fast Yahoo updates player statuses to out.
  > "how quickly Yahoo making those updates to player statuses. That will be the big tell"
- [5:45](https://youtu.be/egRrai3Ax38?t=345) Yahoo ranks and ADPs are the same for every format. They do not change based on your league settings.
  > "Remember, Yahoo's rankings and ADPs are format agnostic. There's no, it doesn't matter what format it is"
- [12:13](https://youtu.be/egRrai3Ax38?t=733) Know both your league settings and the site's settings. Yahoo ranks some players for category leagues and others for points leagues.
  > "Cuz some of them they're ranking for category leagues, some of them they're ranking for points leagues"
- [7:36](https://youtu.be/egRrai3Ax38?t=456) Players with a big gap between their points and category value can be mispriced. Target them when the site ranks or drafts them for the other format.
  > "Paulo has a discrepancy in value between points and category leagues and the Yahoo ranks"
- [20:09](https://youtu.be/egRrai3Ax38?t=1209) ESPN ADPs will not be fixed later. They update every day from real draft data, so you will see the current ADPs in your draft room.
  > "They update them every day based on the data they receive from drafts"
- [13:42](https://youtu.be/egRrai3Ax38?t=822) When some drafters believe a player might lose his starting job or share minutes, his price drops. That creates value if you think he starts.
  > "But the fact that that exists in multiple places that means that white's value is suppressed"
- [21:22](https://youtu.be/egRrai3Ax38?t=1282) ESPN points scoring gives 4 points per steal, so steals-heavy players are worth more there.
  > "Remember, steals are worth four a game over there"
- [20:58](https://youtu.be/egRrai3Ax38?t=1258) Drafters are too scared of players coming back from injuries that cost them last season. You can be more confident than their ADPs suggest.
  > "so people are rightfully scared. You shouldn't be that scared, though. You don't need to be that scared"
- [35:41](https://youtu.be/egRrai3Ax38?t=2141) He now suggests ending head-to-head fantasy playoffs on March 28 instead of March 21. He thinks the new lottery rules will make late March games more competitive.
  > "I feel like the changes to lottery rules will make those March games more competitive"
- [36:09](https://youtu.be/egRrai3Ax38?t=2169) In roto leagues, play to the end of the NBA season with a games cap.
  > "Roto, just go to the end of the season. Put a games cap on"
- [17:16](https://youtu.be/egRrai3Ax38?t=1036) A per game rank earned in limited minutes suggests upside if the player's minutes or role grow.
  > "having him at four when he only played 29 minutes a game suggests to me"

## 2026-09-19 [The Overhyped Fantasy Draft Values I’m Steering Clear Of](videos/2026-09-19-uarqbNA2dFk.md)

- [1:18](https://youtu.be/uarqbNA2dFk?t=78) Rank and ADP are the only large-scale guides to what drafters do. How much they matter depends on your league: some leagues follow ranks closely, others follow ADP, and some go rogue.
  > "In some leagues, rank will be very highly adhered to. In some leagues, people will really, really pay attention to ADP"
- [10:16](https://youtu.be/uarqbNA2dFk?t=616) Reaching for a player to fill a category need is acceptable if it fits your build. You do not have to be rigid about value.
  > "Like we don't have to be as strict and rigid as it sometimes feels like we are."
- [13:37](https://youtu.be/uarqbNA2dFk?t=817) Yahoo ADP mixes points and category drafts. Players valued in points leagues can show up high in category draft rooms and at the top of autodraft queues.
  > "So if you or a league mate sorts the draft room by ADP, he'll come up at 56."
- [4:00](https://youtu.be/uarqbNA2dFk?t=240) Seasons put up while key teammates were injured are hard to repeat once those teammates return.
  > "he played the majority of the season without either Embiid or Paul George and a chunk of the season"
- [15:30](https://youtu.be/uarqbNA2dFk?t=930) Playing every game does not add value if the player's per-game production is unrosterable.
  > "So I don't care that he plays every game. At some point he won't, by the way"
- [23:45](https://youtu.be/uarqbNA2dFk?t=1425) The consensus labels a player injury-prone or healthy after just one season. The speaker disagrees with this but says it affects market perception.
  > "All it takes in in the in the bulk consensus idea for someone to stay healthy or to be injuryprone is one season."
- [31:12](https://youtu.be/uarqbNA2dFk?t=1872) ADPs are not assigned by a person. They update every day from the drafts that actually happen, so do not wait for a site to 'fix' them.
  > "The ADPs update every single day based on the data from drafts that happen. ADPs are not a number that someone just assigns."
- [19:05](https://youtu.be/uarqbNA2dFk?t=1145) A points-only scorer needs a lot of usage to return value. Usage gets harder to find when there is competition for touches.
  > "He'll be a points guy. And to get a lot of points, you need a lot of usage."
- [8:23](https://youtu.be/uarqbNA2dFk?t=503) Do not reach for centers out of fear of a shortage. It is better to find centers later than to take one about 60 spots too early.
  > "I'd rather have no centers to pick from than someone take someone 60 spots too high and I can find some guys later"

## 2026-09-17 [Fantasy Basketball 'SLEEPERS' - Undervalued Picks On Yahoo, ESPN, & Fantrax](videos/2026-09-17-ahNxsoU8Hx4.md)

- [1:50](https://youtu.be/ahNxsoU8Hx4?t=110) The main way to win fantasy is getting value picks, meaning drafting players who finish well above where they were taken, plus active waiver-wire streaming. Builds and pairings matter much less.
  > "It's drafting someone at pick 80 who ends up the 40th best player. It's not builds, it's not pairings"
- [4:10](https://youtu.be/ahNxsoU8Hx4?t=250) The gap between rank and expected finish needed to count as value gets wider as you go further down the draft board.
  > "So, the gap that's needed to create value widens as you go down a draft board."
- [5:03](https://youtu.be/ahNxsoU8Hx4?t=303) Turnovers should be punted by anyone drafting high-usage, high-value players because you cannot avoid them.
  > "Turnovers should just be punted anyway by anyone who's paying any attention to any sort of fantasy"
- [5:23](https://youtu.be/ahNxsoU8Hx4?t=323) If you draft a bad free throw shooter like Giannis, punt FT% but get guard stats (assists, threes, steals) early. Do not draft only players who shoot free throws badly.
  > "got to make sure that you're getting guard stats somewhat early. Getting your assists, getting threes, getting steals"
- [8:19](https://youtu.be/ahNxsoU8Hx4?t=499) Rank and ADP affect each other. When Yahoo moves a player's rank back, his ADP tends to drift later too.
  > "often if Yahoo moves a rank back like they did with Davis here, that ADP is going to drift out."
- [9:35](https://youtu.be/ahNxsoU8Hx4?t=575) ADP is an average, not a median. A player with ADP 50 is going after pick 50 in roughly half of drafts.
  > "So, let's just roughly say 50% of people are drafting him after pick 50."
- [16:42](https://youtu.be/ahNxsoU8Hx4?t=1002) Steals are variable in both directions. Do not pay for a career-high steal rate, but a player whose steals dropped can bounce back.
  > "I told you like that steals are variable. There was very little chance that he would hit three steals a game."
- [22:41](https://youtu.be/ahNxsoU8Hx4?t=1361) Late in drafts, target players with top-30 upside even when they carry injury risk. If they miss long stretches, move on.
  > "when we're drafting in this area. Who else has got top 30 upside? And that's what wins you a league."
- [30:44](https://youtu.be/ahNxsoU8Hx4?t=1844) The best value is usually found between picks 51 and 100, where players can beat their ADP by 10 to 40 spots.
  > "But the real value of where you hit it is between 51 and 100."
- [27:03](https://youtu.be/ahNxsoU8Hx4?t=1623) Do not trust traditional 9-cat total rankings for valuing players. They produce absurd results, such as making Giannis 69th per game.
  > "The traditional NAT rankings like I will tell you again if you want to debate the status of Jaylen Brown"
- [36:38](https://youtu.be/ahNxsoU8Hx4?t=2198) Games-played totals mean nothing without context. Games missed because of team tanking should not count as injury risk.
  > "minimum 40% of the games that he missed due to the ankle problems were tanking related. So games totals without context are meaningless."
- [42:10](https://youtu.be/ahNxsoU8Hx4?t=2530) When a player's ESPN ADP is far later than his rank, people are passing on him round after round. Grab him when that happens in your draft.
  > "if you ever see a discrepancy like that, that means that people are in a draft and they're seeing the ranking list"
- [37:51](https://youtu.be/ahNxsoU8Hx4?t=2271) ESPN's default leagues use 10 teams and 8 categories, so convert ESPN ranks before comparing them to a 12-team 9-cat format.
  > "31 on ESPN, by the way, whose default is 10-man leagues, that's fourth round."

## 2026-09-17 [NBA Fantasy Basketball Rankings Best & Worst Case Scenarios for Every Round [2026/27]](videos/2026-09-17-DubdKKhMWHo.md)

- [0:58](https://youtu.be/DubdKKhMWHo?t=58) Fantasy leagues are small samples. Do not treat a player's average as something that will repeat exactly.
  > "we deal with small sample sizes in most fantasy leagues, roto excluded."
- [1:28](https://youtu.be/DubdKKhMWHo?t=88) Putting too much of your team into high-variance categories leaves you open to strange losses.
  > "putting all your eggs into a high variance basket leads you susceptible to weird losses."
- [3:06](https://youtu.be/DubdKKhMWHo?t=186) Pick between upside and safety based on your roster. If you have already taken several risky swings, lean toward players with a narrower range.
  > "I've done a lot of cracks, so therefore maybe I want to get a guy where the range is narrower"
- [13:14](https://youtu.be/DubdKKhMWHo?t=794) Steals are a highly variable category. Even elite steals players can drop to 0.7 or 0.8 per game in a season.
  > "We know that steals are a highly variant category and he's terrible at them."
- [14:11](https://youtu.be/DubdKKhMWHo?t=851) Further down the board, ranks are packed tightly. A small drop in one stat can cost a player 10 or more spots.
  > "instead of 6.7 assists you average 6.4 four and you fell 12 spots. Everything is incredibly tight"
- [23:30](https://youtu.be/DubdKKhMWHo?t=1410) In later rounds (9 and 10), the downside of most players is just being useless. Take upside flyers on players who could reach the top 50.
  > "can anyone be top 50 here? Have a look"
- [25:28](https://youtu.be/DubdKKhMWHo?t=1528) Base fantasy value on each player's current situation, not on how much you like them as a player.
  > "everything in how I look at at fantasy is about what's the current situation."
- [29:42](https://youtu.be/DubdKKhMWHo?t=1782) Whether you choose an upside pick or a safe pick depends on what the rest of your team looks like.
  > "that is depending on what sort of player you want, what's your team looking like?"
- [34:36](https://youtu.be/DubdKKhMWHo?t=2076) Tiny changes move ranks a lot. One extra steal a week (about 0.3 per game) can be worth around 15 spots, and one extra made basket per game around 10 spots.
  > "your steals go up by.3 and your fantasy rank improves by 15 spots."
- [36:09](https://youtu.be/DubdKKhMWHo?t=2169) Nothing in a projection is guaranteed. Understand which categories are more variable and decide when you are drafting for safety and when for a big upside hit.
  > "Work out when you're drafting for safety and when you're drafting for that big dinger."

## 2026-09-16 [The TOP 25 Players In Fantasy Basketball [Cats & Points]](videos/2026-09-16-2A2JbUN-kc0.md)

- [2:05](https://youtu.be/2A2JbUN-kc0?t=125) Differences between first-round players are marginal. Picking order in round one rarely wins or loses a league. Unexpected injuries do.
  > "It's not it's not the thing that wins or loses. Unexpected injuries that'll lose your league."
- [3:11](https://youtu.be/2A2JbUN-kc0?t=191) A pick is only clearly too early when six or seven players who fit that spot better are still available.
  > "if I see six, seven players that I think might be better suited than that player in that area"
- [12:16](https://youtu.be/2A2JbUN-kc0?t=736) In points leagues, the biggest drivers of fantasy points are usage and minutes.
  > "because the biggest driver of fantasy points is usage and minutes."
- [25:13](https://youtu.be/2A2JbUN-kc0?t=1513) Over five seasons, about 37% of the qualified 9-cat top 25 changed from one year to the next. About 16 of 25 repeat.
  > "On average, we have 37% turnover."
- [26:29](https://youtu.be/2A2JbUN-kc0?t=1589) 75% of top 10 players stay inside the top 25 the next year. Players who stay in the top 25 move about five spots on average, with a median of four.
  > "The top 10 players, 75% of those guys remain as top 25 players."
- [27:28](https://youtu.be/2A2JbUN-kc0?t=1648) 54% of top 25 exits came from players missing the 50 game or 1500 minute threshold because of injury, not from playing worse. Availability is the biggest threat.
  > "54% of them in fact were not due to them being bad."
- [28:04](https://youtu.be/2A2JbUN-kc0?t=1684) Every top 25 player who stayed eligible but dropped out of the top 25 still finished top 50. Healthy top 25 players do not bottom out.
  > "every player who remained eligible but did drop out of the top 25, they still were top 50 players."
- [29:04](https://youtu.be/2A2JbUN-kc0?t=1744) In head-to-head, efficiency is the most variable category week to week. He prefers consistent volume over a small efficiency edge.
  > "efficiency is the most variable thing week on week, game by game."
- [31:21](https://youtu.be/2A2JbUN-kc0?t=1881) Usage strongly correlates with points-league value but correlates much less with category-league success.
  > "usage doesn't correlate to fantasy category success as much as it does in points leagues."
- [36:00](https://youtu.be/2A2JbUN-kc0?t=2160) A star joining a new team tends to lose some value.
  > "Big Star joining a new team is an impact thing. It it does have a it does have a decrease in value."
- [37:46](https://youtu.be/2A2JbUN-kc0?t=2266) Draft players knowing their strengths and weaknesses. A weak category like free throws is acceptable.
  > "You know, when you draft what a player's strengths and weaknesses are. That's okay."
- [39:41](https://youtu.be/2A2JbUN-kc0?t=2381) In competitive roto, you can win while punting a category. Punting becomes more viable with more teams, more categories and deeper leagues.
  > "The more competitive, the more teams, the more categories, the more viable punting a category is."
- [40:04](https://youtu.be/2A2JbUN-kc0?t=2404) Injuries matter less in roto than in head-to-head.
  > "At number 11, injuries don't factor as much in this format."
- [41:12](https://youtu.be/2A2JbUN-kc0?t=2472) Rankings are ordinal, not value gaps. Number 6 is not much better than 8 or 12. Adjust picks based on your earlier picks.
  > "Six is not that much better than 8, not that much better than 12th"

## 2026-09-15 [14 Team Fantasy Basketball Mock Draft [9 Cat Mock Draft]](videos/2026-09-15-KPdD91Oo8-U.md)

- [1:07](https://youtu.be/KPdD91Oo8-U?t=67) In deeper leagues, steady low-upside players like Aaron Gordon, Tobias Harris and Andrew Wiggins become key parts of your main roster instead of streaming spots.
  > "the guys that you would pass over Aaron Gordon Tobias Harris Andrew Wiggins maybe they become key parts"
- [1:22](https://youtu.be/KPdD91Oo8-U?t=82) In a 14-team league, do not start taking flyers too early, for example in round 8. Picks around 110 to 130 are active starters, not flyer picks.
  > "Do they start the flyers early and miss out on some solid picks? They start grabbing guys in round eight."
- [1:40](https://youtu.be/KPdD91Oo8-U?t=100) Players who are not worth rostering in 10 or 12 team leagues become your eighth or ninth best player in deeper leagues and gain value.
  > "They become your eighth best player, your ninth best player instead of being your 11th best player."
- [9:27](https://youtu.be/KPdD91Oo8-U?t=567) Standard score valuations depend on the mean and standard deviation of the player pool. As the pool grows from about 156 to 200, values shift and a player might move up around 10 spots.
  > "So it might not be big differences, but you might see someone push up 10 spots just due to player pool expanding."
- [12:19](https://youtu.be/KPdD91Oo8-U?t=739) The later you pick in a snake draft, the more risk you should accept, because the top of the draft has a built-in advantage.
  > "you got to increase your risk tolerance the further down the draft board you get because there is an inherent advantage"
- [12:25](https://youtu.be/KPdD91Oo8-U?t=745) Auction drafts are the best way to even out draft position. In snake formats, all-round reversal is the fairest: the first pick picks last in every other round.
  > "the best way to even it out obviously is an auction draft obviously."
- [14:20](https://youtu.be/KPdD91Oo8-U?t=860) Do not lock onto must-have players and reach for them. Make the best pick available and build around value.
  > "I can build a team around value, not hyperfocused targets."
- [19:26](https://youtu.be/KPdD91Oo8-U?t=1166) Do not draft a one-category specialist to fix a category that is already too weak to recover.
  > "his strength is steals. My steals are putrid. I wouldn't have recovered them from there."
- [27:53](https://youtu.be/KPdD91Oo8-U?t=1673) In a deep league, an injury-prone player taken around pick 110 is a big risk. When he misses games, a much worse replacement player has to start for you.
  > "when Porzingis misses, it means that my 11th best guy, which would be like the 170th, 180th best player, has to jump into my starting group."
- [28:51](https://youtu.be/KPdD91Oo8-U?t=1731) Picking first gives a safe core, so that manager can afford riskier picks later.
  > "you've got the security that you pick. So, you can take some risks. That's also the benefit of picking up at number one."
- [33:02](https://youtu.be/KPdD91Oo8-U?t=1982) Change your draft strategy based on how deep your league is.
  > "I think you should you should be changing your strategies in drafts depending on how deep your league actually is."
- [46:57](https://youtu.be/KPdD91Oo8-U?t=2817) Late in deep drafts, low-ceiling veterans are all upside at their price. Minutes upside drives value.
  > "I'm just give me minutes upside which is what Hunter has. Is he good? Of course not. But minutes will drive"

## 2026-09-14 [Fantasy Basketball Center Tier Rankings [NBA]](videos/2026-09-14-t4n9MAP2_14.md)

- [1:03](https://youtu.be/t4n9MAP2_14?t=63) Tiers are a guide only. Do not treat them as a drafting bible.
  > "you treat this as some sort of drafting bible. It is not is not."
- [9:53](https://youtu.be/t4n9MAP2_14?t=593) Rankings are fluid. The speaker changes his opinion daily as new information comes in, and you should debate your own rankings while staying uncertain.
  > "So doubting and debating with yourself and with others while being uncertain of how things play out"
- [13:33](https://youtu.be/t4n9MAP2_14?t=813) His head-to-head ranking system pushes centers down. In H2H you want to max out games played, so low turnovers matter less, and traditional box score values overrate blocks, steals and some percentages.
  > "because in head-to-head leagues, you are trying to max out games played, meaning the impact of low turnovers"
- [19:47](https://youtu.be/t4n9MAP2_14?t=1187) Standard 9-cat rankings ('fluff') inflate some players, and those players get overdrafted. Be aware of that.
  > "Tier seven has a lot of the guys that are going to be overdrafted thanks to nine capat fluffery."
- [18:15](https://youtu.be/t4n9MAP2_14?t=1095) Roto and head-to-head are very different. Injury-risk stars like Embiid were worth taking in roto, but less so in H2H.
  > "But Roto is very different to headto-head."
- [18:58](https://youtu.be/t4n9MAP2_14?t=1138) Only take a high-injury-risk player late if you have not already taken anything super risky earlier in the draft.
  > "take a you can take a chance if you haven't done anything super risky earlier on."
- [30:55](https://youtu.be/t4n9MAP2_14?t=1855) Prefer a player with top 50 upside over a safe, boring player with a capped ceiling at the same draft spot.
  > "The answer is you want the bloke who could be top 50."
- [36:22](https://youtu.be/t4n9MAP2_14?t=2182) Do not draft or stash a long-term injured player. Only keep him in an empty injured slot and drop him once you need the spot.
  > "If you have Mark Williams and you got no one else in your injured slot, hold him there"
- [37:23](https://youtu.be/t4n9MAP2_14?t=2243) Several late-tier centers are only worth looking at in 14-team leagues, not in 12-team leagues.
  > "make sure you're looking at them in 14 cuz in a 12 team, I don't know what the point would be"
- [22:13](https://youtu.be/t4n9MAP2_14?t=1333) Players with similar category profiles (rebounds, blocks, FG%) should be drafted around the same area. Huge ADP gaps between them are market inefficiencies.
  > "is ridiculous to me when they all should be around the same area."

## 2026-09-14 [Fantasy Basketball Power Forward Tier Rankings [NBA]](videos/2026-09-14-LM0cRCGoAUQ.md)

- [1:38](https://youtu.be/LM0cRCGoAUQ?t=98) Tiers do not translate well from fantasy football or baseball to basketball. Basketball positions are fluid and players at the same position do very different things.
  > "In basketball, the positions are a little bit more fluid, but also what the players do"
- [1:03](https://youtu.be/LM0cRCGoAUQ?t=63) Do not use positional tiers as the basis of drafting.
  > "do not use this as the basis of drafting. You see tiers, and there are things"
- [4:16](https://youtu.be/LM0cRCGoAUQ?t=256) Straight nine-cat rankings are a bad way to value players. If a player needs a 50-spot adjustment to reflect his real value, the ranking system is wrong.
  > "If you have to make adjustments that are 50 spots to get relative value of a player, then the ranking system is wrong"
- [14:42](https://youtu.be/LM0cRCGoAUQ?t=882) A low nine-cat ranking can wrongly suggest a useful player belongs on the waiver wire or bench. Paolo Banchero is the example.
  > "that would suggest to you that in a 10-man league, they are a player you leave on the waiver wire"
- [15:34](https://youtu.be/LM0cRCGoAUQ?t=934) Yahoo ranks and ADPs can be skewed by points league value. Check which format a rank reflects before using it.
  > "So, his ADP's and ranks you got to sort of work out what it is."
- [4:47](https://youtu.be/LM0cRCGoAUQ?t=287) A player joining a new team can have growing pains.
  > "My only hesitation on it is that on a new team, there can be some growing pains."
- [20:14](https://youtu.be/LM0cRCGoAUQ?t=1214) Players with heavy injury risk can be fine in roto leagues but should be pushed down in head-to-head formats. Kawhi Leonard is the example.
  > "In a roto league, if you want to do round three, go for it. But in any head-to-head format"
- [25:32](https://youtu.be/LM0cRCGoAUQ?t=1532) Teams coming off long playoff or championship runs may be cautious with their main players' minutes the next season.
  > "I'm a little bit worried they just be somewhat cautious on him. Like they were with all of their main guys"
- [26:00](https://youtu.be/LM0cRCGoAUQ?t=1560) Rookies are usually drafted around pick 100 and play that way early, then improve as the season goes on.
  > "like all rookies, I'm almost certain that he will be around pick 100 for the first 2 months"
- [27:42](https://youtu.be/LM0cRCGoAUQ?t=1662) A team that does not own its draft pick has less reason to fake injuries. But it may still give minutes to young players to see what they have.
  > "Brooklyn being a team without their pick means that they don't have to avoid relegation zone."
- [32:28](https://youtu.be/LM0cRCGoAUQ?t=1948) A big man moving from center to more power forward minutes usually loses field goal percentage, blocks and rebounds.
  > "playing more power forward, as we know, means usually lower field goal percentage, lower blocks, lower rebounds."
- [37:22](https://youtu.be/LM0cRCGoAUQ?t=2242) In the late rounds, hunt upside over stable low-upside players. Stable players are worth more in deeper leagues.
  > "Stable enough to be your round 11 pick, but in a lot of cases, we want to hunt upside there"
- [29:05](https://youtu.be/LM0cRCGoAUQ?t=1745) Do not bank on a shooting improvement. Treat it as a bonus.
  > "If he gets a shooting improvement, great. Just don't bank on it."
- [35:36](https://youtu.be/LM0cRCGoAUQ?t=2136) Summer League three-point shooting numbers should not be trusted.
  > "I think the three-point shooting numbers from Summer League are iffy and do not buy them"

## 2026-09-10 [Fantasy Basketball Small Forward Tier Rankings [NBA]](videos/2026-09-10-dlo7L8Ru91A.md)

- [15:00](https://youtu.be/dlo7L8Ru91A?t=900) Tiers have limited use in category leagues and even points leagues. Players in the same tier can give completely different category profiles, so draft for the categories you need.
  > "the utility of tier tiers for category leagues, even points leagues, is not really that high"
- [5:14](https://youtu.be/dlo7L8Ru91A?t=314) A player being healthy last season does not mean he will be healthy this season.
