  > "because he was healthy last season, he will be healthy this season. That would be antithetical"
- [24:52](https://youtu.be/dlo7L8Ru91A?t=1492) Availability is not the best ability. Many low-value players played 82 games, so games played alone should not push a player up the draft board.
  > "availability is the best ability. It's actually not. The best ability is ability."
- [13:37](https://youtu.be/dlo7L8Ru91A?t=817) When a team adds high-usage players (for example several new guards or scorers), the existing star's usage and assist upside drops, even if his minutes stay the same.
  > "the usage and passing upside for Denny I think is dropped down and those guys will miss time"
- [13:42](https://youtu.be/dlo7L8Ru91A?t=822) Even if new teammates miss games, they still play more than zero games, so the player still loses some production compared to last season.
  > "unless they're playing zero games that means they're doing more than last season"
- [19:05](https://youtu.be/dlo7L8Ru91A?t=1145) Look at the context behind a breakout season, such as which teammates were out. Big numbers posted while key teammates were missing should be scaled back.
  > "Bane did a lot of his damage on insane shooting stuff when Vagnner was out"
- [31:15](https://youtu.be/dlo7L8Ru91A?t=1875) Late-season numbers on tanking teams can be fake because everyone is out and no one is trying.
  > "his numbers down the stretch were fake because everyone was out and no one was trying"
- [29:59](https://youtu.be/dlo7L8Ru91A?t=1799) Late-draft hedge strategy: draft both candidates in a starting-job battle, see which one wins it, and cut the other.
  > "you take him and Yakul Linderborg. You see which one wins the starting job and you cut"
- [31:37](https://youtu.be/dlo7L8Ru91A?t=1897) In deeper leagues such as 14 teams, late-round players become close to starters and are worth more.
  > "if we're heading more into like 14 team leagues where players in this range become close enough"
- [15:33](https://youtu.be/dlo7L8Ru91A?t=933) Players with injury risk get pushed down a tier or more. He will not draft Kawhi Leonard before pick 40 or in round two.
  > "Kawhai would be like a tier 2 player if I didn't have any worries about his injuries"
- [4:45](https://youtu.be/dlo7L8Ru91A?t=285) Some players are worth very different amounts in points leagues and category leagues, so rank them separately for each format.
  > "There is a big difference between Durant in category leagues and points leagues."
- [18:10](https://youtu.be/dlo7L8Ru91A?t=1090) When public perception of an injured player drops a lot but your valuation stays the same, you can get value by drafting him.
  > "public perception has changed a lot where I'd be very happy to be drafting uh Jaylen Williams"

## 2026-09-10 [Fantasy Basketball Shooting Guard Tier Rankings [NBA]](videos/2026-09-10-W-R1dzem32s.md)

- [2:32](https://youtu.be/W-R1dzem32s?t=152) Positional tiers are fluid. Cutoffs shift between positions, so a player changing tiers from one position list to another should not be overread.
  > "That's why some of these positional tier things I think can be"
- [7:21](https://youtu.be/W-R1dzem32s?t=441) Avoid single season myopia. Do not assume last season's result is what always happens. Look at a player's career range and at what changed around him.
  > "single season myopia, where people just look back at what happened last season and that's it."
- [9:35](https://youtu.be/W-R1dzem32s?t=575) Use past production as a base, then adjust for changed factors like new teammates and lost teammates.
  > "I look at the production and and what did happen as a basis of what could happen, but factors need to be considered."
- [8:51](https://youtu.be/W-R1dzem32s?t=531) Projected usage and minutes drive rankings. If you expect different usage or minutes, adjust the player's position yourself.
  > "if you think that his usage will be higher or his minutes will be lower, then take that into consideration"
- [3:39](https://youtu.be/W-R1dzem32s?t=219) Injuries are largely unpredictable. A player seen as injury prone can stay healthy, and a durable player can get hurt.
  > "players can stay healthy or players can get hurt. There's not a lot you can do about it."
- [13:15](https://youtu.be/W-R1dzem32s?t=795) Leaning too hard on 9-cat formula rankings ('nine cat fluffery') can mislead player evaluation in both directions.
  > "rooted in nine cap fluffery and that can lead to problems I think in evaluating players."
- [19:29](https://youtu.be/W-R1dzem32s?t=1169) Defensive stat differences are small in weekly terms. Going from 0.7 to 1 steal is about one extra steal per week, which is easy to flip.
  > "going from 7 steals to one steal is one extra steal per week. It's so inconsequential."
- [18:40](https://youtu.be/W-R1dzem32s?t=1120) Good efficiency on low volume does not matter much.
  > "good efficiency guy on lower volume is not that important."
- [24:54](https://youtu.be/W-R1dzem32s?t=1494) Be wary of players whose value came from teammates being absent. When those teammates return, their production drops.
  > "really making hay while BS while BS have been out and then when they come back he disappears."
- [32:14](https://youtu.be/W-R1dzem32s?t=1934) The 240 game: every team game has 240 minutes to split among about 10 players. Use it to test whether a team's minutes projections are realistic.
  > "10-man rotation. Some play 11, maybe one team will play nine, but you've got to fit 240 minutes for 10 players."
- [29:44](https://youtu.be/W-R1dzem32s?t=1784) High usage rookies nearly always post bad percentages.
  > "pretty bad percentages as nearly every high usage rookie does"
- [26:42](https://youtu.be/W-R1dzem32s?t=1602) Expect second year players to take a jump forward.
  > "we talked about secondyear players and big jumps jumps that they take forward."
- [30:47](https://youtu.be/W-R1dzem32s?t=1847) If you took injury risk or flyer picks earlier, balance them later with safe, steady players.
  > "If you've taken flyer picks earlier, injury risk picks earlier, Wiggo is just solid here."
- [34:19](https://youtu.be/W-R1dzem32s?t=2059) Players at the bottom tier are deep league (14 team) picks or streamers who move on and off rosters.
  > "you're picking them in 14 teamers and they're going to be on and off rosters of streamers throughout the year."
- [10:24](https://youtu.be/W-R1dzem32s?t=624) Some players are much better in points leagues than in category leagues, so tiers differ by format.
  > "you can see some differences who's better in category leagues who's better in points leagues"

## 2026-09-09 [Fantasy Basketball Point Guard Tier Rankings [NBA]](videos/2026-09-09-7BllEsdNLoM.md)

- [1:48](https://youtu.be/7BllEsdNLoM?t=108) Positional tiers can mislead in fantasy basketball. Unlike fantasy football, you do not need to fill positional groups early. Your build changes throughout the draft.
  > "In fantasy basketball, outside of just making sure you've got enough positional cover across your roster, you don't have to do it that way"
- [3:12](https://youtu.be/7BllEsdNLoM?t=192) When drafting, look for statistics or statistical shapes, not positions. Positions only become a focus around round 8 or 9.
  > "The position part comes a focus maybe round eight, round nine, you go, "Oh, got to make sure"
- [3:44](https://youtu.be/7BllEsdNLoM?t=224) Do not use tier lists as the foundation of your draft. Do not reach for a position because of a drop-off between tiers.
  > "Well, I've got to get a tier one player and now it's a big drop-off, so I've got to target other positions."
- [7:00](https://youtu.be/7BllEsdNLoM?t=420) Use projected usage and minutes as the levers. If you see a player's usage or minutes differently, adjust his ranking to match.
  > "if you disagree with the positioning of a player, you go, "Well, I think he's going to get more usage.""
- [9:26](https://youtu.be/7BllEsdNLoM?t=566) Drafting players on the basis that they will not get hurt does not work. Injuries are hard to predict.
  > "if you are drafting someone on the basis of not being hurt, you will get it wrong."
- [27:17](https://youtu.be/7BllEsdNLoM?t=1637) He moves players with injury concerns down his rankings even when their per game numbers say they belong higher.
  > "So, with a lot of these injury concern guys, I bump them down. Even though their per game numbers suggest they should be higher."
- [27:32](https://youtu.be/7BllEsdNLoM?t=1652) In head-to-head, a player who only plays about two games a week can cost you, even when his per game numbers are good.
  > "picking up Dejounte Murray last season actually cost you leagues. Cuz he literally played two games a week."
- [30:03](https://youtu.be/7BllEsdNLoM?t=1803) Do not value players only from last season's ranks. Look at the reasons behind the numbers, such as injuries, limited minutes or a role change.
  > "And this is where if you just base stuff off last season you might as well stick your head up"
- [34:26](https://youtu.be/7BllEsdNLoM?t=2066) Value a player relative to his draft cost and the players around him. A player you don't like can still be a good pick if he is cheap enough.
  > "Everything in fantasy is about evaluating a player, but then evaluating them in the in the context of everyone else around them."
- [19:54](https://youtu.be/7BllEsdNLoM?t=1194) Stats from a team's tanking stretch can understate a player's real value.
  > "some of his numbers last season are hurt by the fact that in the tanking portion of the season"
- [26:05](https://youtu.be/7BllEsdNLoM?t=1565) Teams coming off a Finals run may have a hangover. Their players are unlikely to repeat the same production.
  > "this is a finals I'll say hangover team. Not necessarily they're going to be bad, but they played two months extra"
- [37:19](https://youtu.be/7BllEsdNLoM?t=2239) Players can share a tier on median outcome but have very different ceilings. Pick the safe floor or the upside depending on your build.
  > "But based on my median expectation of these players, they're all in the same grouping."
- [41:02](https://youtu.be/7BllEsdNLoM?t=2462) Do not let strong steals alone inflate a player's value.
  > "He's going to be very good at steals, so don't let that over inflate his value. Don't get fluffed by it."
- [43:49](https://youtu.be/7BllEsdNLoM?t=2629) Draft for value based on ADP, team shape and the risks you have already taken. If you have taken no risks early, take a flyer later.
  > "Hit value based on ADP, based on team shape, based on what you're building. Based on what risks you've taken early."
- [43:57](https://youtu.be/7BllEsdNLoM?t=2637) Leagues are won by getting value, like a late pick who outperforms his draft spot.
  > "What wins a league is just getting value. The guy picked 90 becomes the 40th best player."

## 2026-09-07 [Is Year 3 The Prime Breakout Time In The NBA? [Breakout Fantasy Basketball Players]](videos/2026-09-07-gJUBAJaHzlU.md)

- [2:19](https://youtu.be/gJUBAJaHzlU?t=139) In recent years the big breakouts have moved more to year two. Players who did not take a step in year two are the ones who tend to break out in year three.
  > "over the last couple of years, we're getting more of the big improvements in year two"
- [2:37](https://youtu.be/gJUBAJaHzlU?t=157) Big jumps in year four are unlikely for players who have shown nothing in their first three years.
  > "a lot of those guys they haven't shown anything in the first three years. It is unlikely"
- [6:00](https://youtu.be/gJUBAJaHzlU?t=360) Category-league breakouts are driven by efficiency at volume, a higher free throw attempt rate and a higher assist rate. Points leagues reflect these less.
  > "can you get me 20% extra in terms of free throw attempts? And can you get me 25% extra on assist rate?"
- [7:22](https://youtu.be/gJUBAJaHzlU?t=442) Third-year players drafted inside the top 50 have not busted badly. Third-year players drafted between 101 and 150 made the top 100 only 13% of the time.
  > "Only 13% of those guys drafted late as third round players made it into the top 100."
- [7:44](https://youtu.be/gJUBAJaHzlU?t=464) Third-year players with no ADP almost never become top 100 players.
  > "There's 157 of those guys. Less than 1% of them became top"
- [8:01](https://youtu.be/gJUBAJaHzlU?t=481) For late-round flyers, look at opportunity and situation, and lean toward second-year players over third-year players.
  > "lean more secondy year players because a flyer on a thirdyear guy towards the end of the draft"
- [14:56](https://youtu.be/gJUBAJaHzlU?t=896) Beware of nine-cat fluffing. Straight nine-cat total rankings overrate players who are strong in only a few categories.
  > "it's when you look at a straight nine capat ranking that tells you Jiannis is ranked 50th"
- [15:34](https://youtu.be/gJUBAJaHzlU?t=934) ADP is an average, not a median. A player can often go earlier than his ADP number suggests.
  > "Remember an ADP of 39 and a half means that he is going earlier than that pro"
- [16:00](https://youtu.be/gJUBAJaHzlU?t=960) Taking a two-category player early leaves holes in your team that you then have to fix.
  > "So it puts me in so many holes, giggity, that I have to get myself out"
- [16:38](https://youtu.be/gJUBAJaHzlU?t=998) Yahoo auction price data currently differs a lot from snake-draft ADP data, so treat the two separately.
  > "The data that Yahoo is giving at the moment is very different from snake draft ADAP data"
- [29:02](https://youtu.be/gJUBAJaHzlU?t=1742) Check the context behind stats. Numbers can be inflated when teammates are injured.
  > "It was inflated by the fact that at the start of the year the Bronco was out"
- [33:01](https://youtu.be/gJUBAJaHzlU?t=1981) Some Yahoo ADPs are distorted by dynasty leagues where a player is drafted in only a small share of leagues. Ignore those.
  > "Sometimes they're a little bit distorted by someone that gets drafted in like 2% of leagues"

## 2026-09-07 [Fantasy Basketball Mock Draft - It's Giannis Time [9 Cat 12 Teams Pick 5]](videos/2026-09-07-E-KmhvyZ2CU.md)

- [9:28](https://youtu.be/E-KmhvyZ2CU?t=568) In a punt free throw build, do not draft only bad free throw shooters. Free throws are linked to points, threes and assists, so doing that effectively punts four categories.
  > "free throws are linked heavily to points, threes, and assists. And if you just draft guys with bad free throws"
- [13:11](https://youtu.be/E-KmhvyZ2CU?t=791) When punting a category you are not trying to be bad in it. You just stop caring about it and move resources to other categories.
  > "when you're drafting a punt, whatever team, you're not I'm not trying to make it bad. I just don't care."
- [13:19](https://youtu.be/E-KmhvyZ2CU?t=799) Points and assists are very hard to find in good volume later in drafts, so secure them early.
  > "points and assists are very hard, almost impossible to get in good volume later on"
- [12:19](https://youtu.be/E-KmhvyZ2CU?t=739) Do not let fantasy rankings drag you along. Target the individual categories and stats your team needs.
  > "do not have the leash of fantasy rankings dragging you along like the nine cat sub that you are"
- [23:14](https://youtu.be/E-KmhvyZ2CU?t=1394) Heavy punting leads to low volume and more variance, which can cost you a playoff spot depending on the format.
  > "it leads to variance issues with volume And depending on your playoff format and how many teams make it"
- [22:46](https://youtu.be/E-KmhvyZ2CU?t=1366) Value wins leagues. Take players you think will consistently return more than the spot where you drafted them.
  > "What wins a fantasy league is value. who is going to consistently in your opinion"
- [32:14](https://youtu.be/E-KmhvyZ2CU?t=1934) Late-round flyers: take two upside players in a similar situation to improve the chance that at least one hits.
  > "if you take both of those guys again, Yakel and Santos, I think your chance of hitting one"
- [40:14](https://youtu.be/E-KmhvyZ2CU?t=2414) Late-round upside: a player drafted around 160 who might finish around 120 has upside. Drafting someone at 120 hoping he finishes at 120 has none.
  > "I wouldn't take him at 120 hoping he finishes at 120. There's no upside in that"
- [37:22](https://youtu.be/E-KmhvyZ2CU?t=2242) Stashing is risky in leagues with daily changes and short benches. Deep benches and games limits reward speculation.
  > "stashing in a daily Changes league is fraught with danger."
- [37:07](https://youtu.be/E-KmhvyZ2CU?t=2227) For long-term injured players like Jimmy Butler, use the IL slot if you have it, but cut them once you need the spot after the first two weeks.
  > "But as soon as you need that spot outside of the first two weeks, move on."
- [18:11](https://youtu.be/E-KmhvyZ2CU?t=1091) Mock drafts this early are of limited use, because media day and preseason news will make many results irrelevant.
  > "we're going to see media day and preseason. And all this is going to become relatively irrelevant."
- [14:28](https://youtu.be/E-KmhvyZ2CU?t=868) Draft-room psychology: you can take one player and try to get another on the turn, but you may guess wrong about what other managers want.
  > "I'm going to take Deonte and try and sneak Jaylen Brown. Now, that's a calculated risk."

## 2026-09-04 [Second Year Fantasy Basketball Breakouts](videos/2026-09-04-gerS7ibpaJo.md)

- [2:24](https://youtu.be/gerS7ibpaJo?t=144) Second-year players are much more fantasy relevant than rookies. Over six years, top 50 category players went from 3 as rookies to 8 in year two, top 100 from 11 to 31, and top 150 from 20 to 54.
  > "We had three players as rookies be top 50 guys for category leagues."
- [4:50](https://youtu.be/gerS7ibpaJo?t=290) Across all rookies, 60% improved in year two, and 41% improved by at least 50 ranking slots.
  > "41% of all rookies improve by at least 50 ranking slots in year two."
- [5:36](https://youtu.be/gerS7ibpaJo?t=336) Rookie rank and sophomore rank have a correlation of about 0.61. Most players who are relevant in year two were already somewhat relevant in year one. Only 30 players in six years jumped from outside the top 150 to inside it.
  > "Only 30 of those players over that six year period were not top 150 relevant as rookies"
- [6:32](https://youtu.be/gerS7ibpaJo?t=392) ADP is good with second-year players at the top end. All seven with a top 50 ADP finished top 100. Of those with an ADP of 51 to 100, 72% finished top 100.
  > "Only 72% of those finish in the top 100 and 94% of those finish in the top 150."
- [7:03](https://youtu.be/gerS7ibpaJo?t=423) Second-year flyers with an ADP of 101 to 150 hit only 13% of the time for top 100 and 33% for top 150. Undrafted sophomores almost never become relevant.
  > "So a 13% hit rate on secondyear flyers. 33% of them did end up as top 150 players."
- [7:59](https://youtu.be/gerS7ibpaJo?t=479) Late flyers usually do not work out. That is accepted as part of the cost of drafting in that area.
  > "We know that when we're drafting them late that that's that's part of the cost of doing business"
- [13:00](https://youtu.be/gerS7ibpaJo?t=780) In auctions, people tend to overpay for top-end players and underpay for players in the middle range.
  > "I think that in general people do overpric topend players and underpric the middle range like a lot."
- [14:04](https://youtu.be/gerS7ibpaJo?t=844) If a pick finishes a few spots below where you took it, that barely matters. A big miss, like 11th to 30th, does matter.
  > "But a four or five spot difference, which is probably half a fantasy point or, you know, 0.1 steals, doesn't matter."
- [21:44](https://youtu.be/gerS7ibpaJo?t=1304) Be wary of unsustainable shooting splits, such as very high percentages on twos and threes. They tend to regress.
  > "Bro's hitting 75 on his twos. He's at 50 on his threes. That's just not going to happen, is it?"
- [22:26](https://youtu.be/gerS7ibpaJo?t=1346) Steals and free throw percentage are the two categories that vary most from year to year.
  > "Free throw percentage in steals the two most variable year on year."
- [27:28](https://youtu.be/gerS7ibpaJo?t=1648) Backup bigs who would become must-rosters if the starter misses games are worth drafting in games cap, limited transaction, roto and weekly lock formats. They are harder to justify in daily leagues where you use your bench all the time.
  > "So in games cap formats, in limited transaction formats, in roto leagues, in weekly lock leagues, he has to be drafted"

## 2026-09-03 [Assessing The Fantasy Basketball Production Of NBA Rookies](videos/2026-09-03-OBwWCxG9SqM.md)

- [4:24](https://youtu.be/OBwWCxG9SqM?t=264) Be cautious about investing in rookies in fantasy drafts.
  > "when we're talking about rookies in fantasy, we have to be very cautious about how we invest in them"
- [7:09](https://youtu.be/OBwWCxG9SqM?t=429) The number of relevant rookies goes up in the second half of the season and fantasy playoffs. The causes are tanking, injuries and rookies improving.
  > "the last half of the season in your fantasy playoffs, the number of relevant rookies increases,"
- [7:53](https://youtu.be/OBwWCxG9SqM?t=473) The rookie wall and the sophomore slump are lazy narratives. He says most rookies and second-year players get better, so do not treat these as general rules.
  > "season goes on. Oh, sophomore slump. Yeah, except again 90% of second year players get better."
- [10:56](https://youtu.be/OBwWCxG9SqM?t=656) With less tanking expected this season, the late-season jump in rookie relevance may be smaller than usual.
  > "we get double the amount of rookies becoming relevant, I I don't think it's going to be as extreme"
- [13:57](https://youtu.be/OBwWCxG9SqM?t=837) ADP overrates rookies mostly in the late flyer range. Drafters take far too many rookies near the end of drafts, when most classes give only about three or four relevant players.
  > "we take too many rookies towards the end of a draft when in reality where there's probably going to be"
- [19:58](https://youtu.be/OBwWCxG9SqM?t=1198) Rookies, especially rookie guards, usually shoot badly for the first two to three months and then improve.
  > "He will have bad shooting numbers for two to three months, but it will trend up and get better."
- [21:55](https://youtu.be/OBwWCxG9SqM?t=1315) Judge a rookie by situation, minutes, usage and non-scoring stats, not by draft position.
  > "look at the situation on the team. Where is he going to slide in usage-wise, minutes wise?"
- [23:17](https://youtu.be/OBwWCxG9SqM?t=1397) Projections have to assume trade candidates stay all season. This can understate the rookies behind them.
  > "you sort of do have to project it out assuming that Sabonis and Lavine are going to be there all season"
- [24:08](https://youtu.be/OBwWCxG9SqM?t=1448) If a drafted rookie starts with real usage but hurts your efficiency, hold him until about Thanksgiving before giving up.
  > "if you draft rookies, especially rookie guards, give them until Thanksgiving. If they're starting and they got a usage role"
- [28:01](https://youtu.be/OBwWCxG9SqM?t=1681) Do not hold several inefficient rookie flyers at once while waiting for them to improve. Pick which ones to keep and drop the rest quickly.
  > "you can't hold all of them through to Thanksgiving or else you'll be, you know, six weeks in"
- [30:07](https://youtu.be/OBwWCxG9SqM?t=1807) Late-round rookie picks are for chasing upside, but be quick to move on when they do not pan out.
  > "those late picks they don't work out to use them by all means. We're hunting upside. But be quick to move on."

## 2026-09-01 [How To Win Your Fantasy Basketball League](videos/2026-09-01-skKXe2CRl8Q.md)

- [2:16](https://youtu.be/skKXe2CRl8Q?t=136) Know your scoring system and format: categories or points, head-to-head or roto. If you don't know it, you have no chance.
  > "If you don't know your scoring system, you're done. you just have no chance of winning"
- [3:25](https://youtu.be/skKXe2CRl8Q?t=205) Know your transaction rules: daily or weekly lineups, weekly add limits, trade caps, games caps. They change how you value players. With unlimited moves the end of your roster should be churning all the time. With two pickups a week, use them all.
  > "If you can do two pickups a week, you've got to max out those spots."
- [3:50](https://youtu.be/skKXe2CRl8Q?t=230) Injury-prone stars can be taken a bit earlier in roto than in head-to-head. In head-to-head with limited streaming, avoid players who miss games often.
  > "In a roto league, there's a little bit more value in the often guys like Embiid and Kawaii"
- [4:41](https://youtu.be/skKXe2CRl8Q?t=281) Know your playoff format. If the top six make it, you can punt more heavily. If only the top four of 12 make it, punting four categories may keep you out.
  > "If you're in top six, then you can lean a little heavier into punting because you're not"
- [5:36](https://youtu.be/skKXe2CRl8Q?t=336) Information hierarchy for evaluating players: minutes, then role, then usage and opportunity, then production, with narrative and hype last.
  > "What are the minutes the player is getting? That's one of your number one things you're looking at."
- [6:47](https://youtu.be/skKXe2CRl8Q?t=407) Last season's production is overvalued. Production follows minutes, role and opportunity, and those can change.
  > "Production's important, but it sort of goes, it gets dragged along by minutes, roll, and opportunity."
- [7:32](https://youtu.be/skKXe2CRl8Q?t=452) Don't fall for narrative, hype or highlight-reel bias. Ask why something happened and whether it can happen again.
  > "if you just get sucked into highlight real bias narrative and hype without looking at why did it happen"
- [9:39](https://youtu.be/skKXe2CRl8Q?t=579) Rankings and projections tell you a player's quality. ADP is the market price and tells you when he will likely be available. If you rank a player 30th and his ADP is 70th, draft him in the 50s.
  > "If you have a player 30th, his 8 AP is 70th. What I like to do in those"
- [10:26](https://youtu.be/skKXe2CRl8Q?t=626) Draft for flexibility and categorical shape. Think about what your team needs and which categories are about to run out in the draft.
  > "rebounds are about to run out. I better get someone with that now. Can I afford the free throw hit?"
- [11:02](https://youtu.be/skKXe2CRl8Q?t=662) Cover every position with at least two to three eligible players, even when punting. Otherwise you give up games during the week.
  > "Make sure you can cover each position with two to three eligible players at least."
- [11:20](https://youtu.be/skKXe2CRl8Q?t=680) Streaming lower-ranked players (170 to 190) for more games beats holding a 130th-ranked player who sits on your bench all season.
  > "In most cases, you should be streaming. And having a player that's 130th versus streaming in seven games"
- [13:45](https://youtu.be/skKXe2CRl8Q?t=825) Don't use late picks on players just because they have good week one schedules. Use the first two weeks to evaluate and be patient. Losing week one is fine.
  > "I like to use the first two weeks to make sure I'm evaluating what's happening and being patient."
- [14:59](https://youtu.be/skKXe2CRl8Q?t=899) Early in the season, watch for unexpected minutes, new starters, depth chart changes and players doing more. Coaches do weird things in weeks one and two.
  > "Coaches do weird things in week one or two all the time. All the time they do weird things."
- [17:00](https://youtu.be/skKXe2CRl8Q?t=1020) React quickly to rotation changes, unexpected starters and bigger minutes, such as a 28-minute starting role. Don't react to bad shooting nights if role, minutes and usage haven't changed.
  > "Jump on those immediately cuz we want sustainability. We want to go that's a roll. That's a 28 minute starting roll."
- [17:32](https://youtu.be/skKXe2CRl8Q?t=1052) Stats are volatile. No player matches his averages every game, so don't overreact to hot or cold stretches.
  > "Stats are volatile. They're variable. They No one is going to get their averages every game."
- [19:17](https://youtu.be/skKXe2CRl8Q?t=1157) Rule for drafted rookies: if their role is okay or trending up, give them until Thanksgiving. If they aren't playing at all, cut them after two weeks.
  > "I like to have the idea if I've drafted a rookie, I give them until Thanksgiving."
- [19:41](https://youtu.be/skKXe2CRl8Q?t=1181) The better your team is, the longer you can hold struggling or injured players.
  > "the better my team is, the longer I can hold on to guys."
- [19:58](https://youtu.be/skKXe2CRl8Q?t=1198) A streaming spot is worth about as much as the 100th-ranked player. Holding long-term injured players costs you that production.
  > "the value of streaming in a spot is basically equivalent to the hundth ranked player."
- [22:55](https://youtu.be/skKXe2CRl8Q?t=1375) Make trades for the long term. Buy low and sell high, and accept short-term pain for long-term gain.
  > "generally want to make a trade for the long term. You're probably going to get some sort of a short-term"
- [23:28](https://youtu.be/skKXe2CRl8Q?t=1408) Trades that improve your schedule, such as extra games in the fantasy playoffs, are worth considering as the season goes on, but not at the draft.
  > "Can I squeeze two extra games out in my fantasy playoffs finals week? I wouldn't care too much about that during a draft"
- [23:41](https://youtu.be/skKXe2CRl8Q?t=1421) Look to make 2-for-1 trades where you send out two players. The open roster spot turns into a streaming slot worth top-100 value, so it nearly always works out.
  > "You're looking to make two for one deals. I send out two, I get back one because we never"
- [24:44](https://youtu.be/skKXe2CRl8Q?t=1484) Start from an internal default of no on every trade offer, then convince yourself whether it is worth doing.
  > "I look at a trade, it comes in, I go, I'm not doing that. That's my that's my baseline."
- [25:40](https://youtu.be/skKXe2CRl8Q?t=1540) Be careful accepting 2-for-1 trades where you get two players back. They take away your streaming slot and your flexibility.
  > "Be careful accepting two for ones because you reduce your flexibility. Your streaming slot disappears."
- [26:03](https://youtu.be/skKXe2CRl8Q?t=1563) It is okay to switch your team's category profile during the season through trades. Make sure a trade doesn't leave you short at a position.
  > "Now, it's okay to switch your team profile during the course of a season."
- [28:32](https://youtu.be/skKXe2CRl8Q?t=1712) The season has three phases. Discovery comes early, then optimizing, then maximizing near the end and in the playoffs, when you drop stashed or injured players and stream as much as you can.
  > "You drop those players. You cut them. You stream your ass off."
- [29:23](https://youtu.be/skKXe2CRl8Q?t=1763) Draft opportunistically instead of locking into punt builds or category pairings. If a player is falling well below his value, take him and adjust your build later.
  > "Draft opportunistically. Huh? I think this guy might be a top 40 player. I'm sitting here at 65."
- [29:51](https://youtu.be/skKXe2CRl8Q?t=1791) The number one way to win is to get value relative to where you drafted or picked up a player.
  > "one way, the number one way to win fantasy. Get value. You draft someone at 100 and"
- [30:47](https://youtu.be/skKXe2CRl8Q?t=1847) React correctly. Don't drop proven players, and don't chase unsustainable hot streaks that will normalize.
  > "You have to react correctly. Don't drop proven players. Don't take trips on treacherous roads."
- [32:15](https://youtu.be/skKXe2CRl8Q?t=1935) Maximize your assets: players, roster spots, weekly moves, IR slots, streaming slots, knowledge of the rules, and league mates you can take advantage of.
  > "Your weekly waiver moves are your assets. Your injured reserve slots are your assets."

## 2026-09-01 [Fantasy Basketball Mock Draft [ESPN Points Scoring Format] - Pick 10](videos/2026-09-01-80kfLVnFQ_s.md)

- [8:17](https://youtu.be/80kfLVnFQ_s?t=497) Know the scoring system and league structure before you draft. Many picks are only too early or too late because of the format.
  > "there is importance in knowing what your structure is and what what the idea of this draft is"
- [21:31](https://youtu.be/80kfLVnFQ_s?t=1291) In a 10-team league the waiver wire is deeper. You can take more risk and draft late-round flyers, because a failed pick is easy to replace by streaming.
  > "this is a 10 team league. So the waiver wire is going to be more chockers. So feel free to take flyers"
- [24:34](https://youtu.be/80kfLVnFQ_s?t=1474) In shallow leagues, be risk forward and flyer forward in the late rounds because of how the league is set up.
  > "I'm happy to be risk forward, flyer forward in this sort of scenario because"
- [17:25](https://youtu.be/80kfLVnFQ_s?t=1045) Be careful about stacking too many older or previously injured players on one roster, even when each one looks like good value.
  > "that's a lot of like older guys, a lot of previously injured guys"
- [25:54](https://youtu.be/80kfLVnFQ_s?t=1554) Rookies often get their fantasy value from defensive stats. Those count less in points leagues.
  > "his value for a rookie in fantasy is going to come from defensive stats, and that's not going to count"
- [27:26](https://youtu.be/80kfLVnFQ_s?t=1646) Inefficient scorers get penalized in ESPN points scoring.
  > "he will get a penalty in this format because of inefficiency"
- [33:20](https://youtu.be/80kfLVnFQ_s?t=2000) Drafts with an odd number of rounds give the first pick one more first-in-round pick than the last pick. He prefers 14 rounds with four bench spots.
  > "Why would you have odd number of rounds so that the team that picks first gets"
- [1:16](https://youtu.be/80kfLVnFQ_s?t=76) Very early in the preseason (50+ days out), there is no need to run many mock drafts in every format because a lot will change.
  > "We are 50 plus days away from the start of the season. I don't think it's necessary"
- [25:05](https://youtu.be/80kfLVnFQ_s?t=1505) Health-risk players like Kristaps Porzingis are worth a pick in the late-middle rounds. The upside is high and the cost is low by then.
  > "if Pzingus is playing, you're maybe getting a top 60 guy. Now, he might not play, but who cares"

## 2026-08-30 [The Big Differences Between Category & Points Leagues [Fantasy Basketball]](videos/2026-08-30-Alwse2uXzD4.md)

- [1:18](https://youtu.be/Alwse2uXzD4?t=78) Rankings without a format attached are useless. Value differs across head-to-head categories, roto, Yahoo points, ESPN points and Sleeper.
  > "Oh, he's ranked here. Is he? But like in what format? head-to-head categories, Yahoo points, rotisserie, ESPN points"
- [2:08](https://youtu.be/Alwse2uXzD4?t=128) The Yahoo X rank (expert rank) does not clearly reflect points value or category value. It often floats somewhere in between.
  > "list that says X rank X, that stands for expert. Wow, these guys are experts."
- [3:27](https://youtu.be/Alwse2uXzD4?t=207) Don't follow a prescribed pick list. Every draft decision depends on who is still available, so build understanding instead.
  > "Because if the second guy that I told you to take, what if there's four other players"
- [4:37](https://youtu.be/Alwse2uXzD4?t=277) No scoring format captures true universal value.
  > "You You don't because there's no such thing as true universal value."
- [5:39](https://youtu.be/Alwse2uXzD4?t=339) In a standard 150-player league, the average player gives about 18 fantasy points from scoring, 5.2 from assists, 3 from steals and about 2 from blocks. Scoring dominates points leagues.
  > "So an average player in scoring gets you 18 fantasy points through their scoring. An average player in assists get you five."
- [7:07](https://youtu.be/Alwse2uXzD4?t=427) Usage, minutes and scoring drive points leagues, so volume is key. Defense is downplayed.
  > "Usage, minutes, and scoring drive points leagues. Again, this is I don't I don't I don't think"
- [9:05](https://youtu.be/Alwse2uXzD4?t=545) Yahoo default points scoring has no penalty for missed shots. ESPN gives -1 per field goal and free throw attempt, gives 4 points per steal or block instead of 3, and adds a bonus for threes. A made three is worth 5 points on ESPN.
  > "Every shot that you attempt is a negative one. Every free throw you attempt is a negative one."
- [10:57](https://youtu.be/Alwse2uXzD4?t=657) In points leagues, you just need the player who scores the most fantasy points. It doesn't matter how he gets them, so don't chase specific skills like assists.
  > "It literally does not matter how they get their points."
- [11:18](https://youtu.be/Alwse2uXzD4?t=678) Fantasy points built mostly on defensive stats are less reliable than points built on scoring. Scoring repeats more consistently game to game.
  > "is worse than a player that gets 20 fantasy points based 60% on their scoring because scoring is more repeatable"
- [12:21](https://youtu.be/Alwse2uXzD4?t=741) The speaker dislikes Sleeper's default scoring. It includes binary double-double and triple-double bonuses, a 40-point bonus and penalties for technicals and flagrants, which are unprojectable.
  > "I don't like having categories that or even scoring things that are binary like double doubles and triple doubles"
- [18:32](https://youtu.be/Alwse2uXzD4?t=1112) ADP often mixes owners drafting for points with owners drafting for categories. In category leagues, players whose ADP leans toward their points value can be targets.
  > "I guess half the people are drafting like it's a points league and half are drafting like it's a category league."
- [20:35](https://youtu.be/Alwse2uXzD4?t=1235) Players whose main contribution is scoring, with weak defensive stats and lower efficiency, are better in points leagues than category leagues.
  > "If you score as your main thing and have troubles with low defensive stats and"
- [20:47](https://youtu.be/Alwse2uXzD4?t=1247) Default rule: rookie guards and wings are better in points leagues.
  > "if it's guards and they're rookies or wings, an easy default rule is better in points leagues."
- [30:46](https://youtu.be/Alwse2uXzD4?t=1846) Inefficient, defense-light scorers are worth relatively more in Yahoo points leagues than in ESPN points leagues, because ESPN penalizes misses and values defense more.
  > "given ESPN has penalties for miss shots and values defensive stats more"
- [35:54](https://youtu.be/Alwse2uXzD4?t=2154) Labels like overrated, sleeper or bust mean nothing unless you know which format they come from.

## 2026-08-26 [Biggest Fantasy Basketball Risers & Fallers | Usage & Minutes Changes for 2026](videos/2026-08-26-sTtFUy7IoJI.md)

- [1:40](https://youtu.be/sTtFUy7IoJI?t=100) Usage and minutes are the two stats most closely tied to fantasy value. Projecting changes in them gives a starting point for valuing players.
  > "usage and minutes are the two biggest correlations of stats for fantasy value"
- [4:59](https://youtu.be/sTtFUy7IoJI?t=299) Look at context behind last season's numbers, such as injuries, minutes limits or a tanking team, before projecting a player forward.
  > "But context around it is important. So, Jaylen Green played 25.9 minutes per game last season."
- [7:03](https://youtu.be/sTtFUy7IoJI?t=423) For uncertain young players with upside, take a flier with your last pick and cut him if it does not work out.
  > "you just take a fly with the last pick and just see what happens. And then you cut him."
- [9:02](https://youtu.be/sTtFUy7IoJI?t=542) A backup big's upside often depends on an injury to the starter, so he is mainly worth it if you have room to stash him.
  > "But the upside only is there if you've got stash ability waiting for a go bear injury"
- [11:24](https://youtu.be/sTtFUy7IoJI?t=684) In points leagues, a scorer who does little else needs both minutes and shot volume to succeed.
  > "And to be successful there, you need the minutes, which he's going to get, but then you also need volume."
- [15:38](https://youtu.be/sTtFUy7IoJI?t=938) He advises against being okay with injury risk when drafting injury-prone players.
  > "player if you're okay with injury risk, which I don't think you should be"
- [16:56](https://youtu.be/sTtFUy7IoJI?t=1016) A recurring back injury during a season can improve with a full offseason of rest. Worry again only if it flares up in training camp.
  > "But you have four months off and then theoretically like hopefully your back is okay."
- [37:35](https://youtu.be/sTtFUy7IoJI?t=2255) When high-usage players join the same team, last season's numbers cannot all hold. Expect each player's usage to drop.
  > "If you just put everyone's numbers from the year before, the last time they played together, they're going"
- [32:55](https://youtu.be/sTtFUy7IoJI?t=1975) A player losing about 25% of his usage cannot keep his fantasy output, even if his minutes stay high.
  > "if you are losing a chunk like that 25% of your usage not 25 percentage points"
- [33:54](https://youtu.be/sTtFUy7IoJI?t=2034) General rules like third-year breakouts are a good baseline, but each player should then be judged on his own situation.
  > "you look at things generally to start off to set a baseline what's the expectation"

## 2026-08-25 [Are You Sleeping on the Atlanta Hawks? [BEST Hawks Outlook]](videos/2026-08-25-H9q2FT3LhNw.md)

- [2:59](https://youtu.be/H9q2FT3LhNw?t=179) This season the East is stronger and fewer bottom teams are tanking, so a team can get better and still win fewer games. Do not read fewer wins as a worse team.
  > "you can be a better team and win fewer games and that's okay as long as we're just understanding"
- [10:01](https://youtu.be/H9q2FT3LhNw?t=601) When a player has an extreme hot stretch, such as a post All-Star run, use the earlier part of his season as the baseline and expect the shooting to come down.
  > "So there's going to be a bit of usage and ball handling changes plus that insane shooting is going to come down."
- [23:20](https://youtu.be/H9q2FT3LhNw?t=1400) To judge a player's production and minutes, look at who was around him, who was out, and how he gets used when the team is healthy. Big games that came while a teammate was out may not carry over.
  > "who was around, who wasn't around, and how were they used and how do they get used when the team looks whole?"
- [28:25](https://youtu.be/H9q2FT3LhNw?t=1705) Players who go for more blocks commit more fouls. As players age and their minutes go up, their block and foul rates tend to drop. Starters playing big minutes cannot risk foul trouble.
  > "when you go for more blocks, you commit more fouls. And when you're every player, like as they get older, block rate down"
- [26:54](https://youtu.be/H9q2FT3LhNw?t=1614) A center who takes more threes plays farther from the rim. His offensive rebounds and rim finishing tend to drop, while assists and three-point attempts go up.
  > "when you're out there taking more threes, you're in a different position. So you're working not exactly under the rim."

## 2026-08-24 [Cleveland Cavaliers - I Think This Is Their BEST Chance [NBA]](videos/2026-08-24-rnq3118kfhY.md)

## 2026-08-24 [Points Mock Draft [YAHOO] | 2026/27 NBA Fantasy Basketball](videos/2026-08-24-g31YlwRe0XQ.md)

- [4:26](https://youtu.be/g31YlwRe0XQ?t=266) Points league and category league values differ a lot. Know your format, because drafting from category rankings in a points league can hurt you badly.
  > "this is not a category league and we'll see how players and managers approach this draft"
- [25:17](https://youtu.be/g31YlwRe0XQ?t=1517) Scoring is the number one contributor to fantasy points in points leagues, so high-usage scorers gain value there.
  > "the number one contributor to fantasy points is scoring and he's going to have a lot of usage"
- [22:56](https://youtu.be/g31YlwRe0XQ?t=1376) A reach costs more early than late. Twenty spots too high in round 3 is bad. Fifteen spots too high in round 6 hardly matters.
  > "if it's 20 spots too high in round three, bad, right? If it's 15 spots too high"
- [9:55](https://youtu.be/g31YlwRe0XQ?t=595) On the turn, reaching for a player you really want can be justified, because he will not come back to you.
  > "on the turn, you can always make arguments cuz if Harden's the guy you want, you're not going to get him"
- [38:05](https://youtu.be/g31YlwRe0XQ?t=2285) In late rounds (13 and 14), take upside swings over boring veterans. Boring players can be found later, and they become value picks outside the top 150.
  > "Let's hit some of these upside guys that might be the 90th best player, but might be 180th"
- [38:39](https://youtu.be/g31YlwRe0XQ?t=2319) Boring veterans are fine late but bad picks in early or middle rounds. Take them when they fall past their value.
  > "But if you take him at in round 10, it's just nothing. It's boring. It's not interesting."
- [39:48](https://youtu.be/g31YlwRe0XQ?t=2388) Hedge strategy: draft two players fighting for the same minutes, then drop whichever one loses the role.
  > "Do I take Yaxle and then take Santos and whoever gets the bulk of those minutes is good"
- [45:00](https://youtu.be/g31YlwRe0XQ?t=2700) A fantasy basketball handcuff, unlike one in fantasy football, must have value on his own, with big upside if the starter gets hurt.
  > "a fantasy basketball handcuff has to have value on his own with huge upside"
- [21:51](https://youtu.be/g31YlwRe0XQ?t=1311) Players with health uncertainty can be strong per game, but it is better to wait a few rounds on them.
  > "Pzingis probably per game is better than this, but I'd like to wait a few more rounds given this the health uncertainty"

## 2026-08-23 [Phoenix Suns 2026/27 NBA Season Preview](videos/2026-08-23-hm5-fiCa5S4.md)

  > "when everyone gets hot it's all celebrated and everyone thinks well this"
- [12:14](https://youtu.be/hm5-fiCa5S4?t=734) Teams usually try the option that protects ego, salary, draft pedigree or trade capital first. They only make harder rotation changes after it clearly fails.
  > "draft pedigree which holds a lot or you know trade capital invested in players that requires"
- [36:56](https://youtu.be/hm5-fiCa5S4?t=2216) Bench players who put up numbers in big minutes during injuries should be valued closer to their healthy-team role. Expect a rank around 150th unless something changes.

- [37:28](https://youtu.be/hm5-fiCa5S4?t=2248) Taking flyers on players with an uncertain role is fine. Know what has to happen for them to pay off, and drop them at the right time.

- [28:09](https://youtu.be/hm5-fiCa5S4?t=1689) Players who put up big scoring numbers only when injuries push their usage up tend to produce much less when asked to scale back.

## 2026-08-19 [Exposing The Initial Yahoo Fantasy Basketball Rankings For Fantasy Basketball](videos/2026-08-19-J1Eg3uaAICU.md)

- [1:22](https://youtu.be/J1Eg3uaAICU?t=82) Yahoo rankings matter because Yahoo is the most-used platform and its rankings drive ADP in mock and real drafts. Use them as a baseline for where players will go.
  > "And the rankings influence the ADP. So you go into a mockdraft, you go into a real draft"
- [3:47](https://youtu.be/J1Eg3uaAICU?t=227) Yahoo's X-rank is a vibes-based list that ignores your league format. The draft room defaults to it. The separate 'rank' column is built from statistical projections and changes with your league settings.
  > "X-rank is the vibes based ranking. rank is based on what their statistical projections are"
- [3:47](https://youtu.be/J1Eg3uaAICU?t=227) Ranking players by nine-cat totals is the worst way to rank them.
  > "because they base it on, you know, the worst way to rank players, nine cat totals."
- [4:42](https://youtu.be/J1Eg3uaAICU?t=282) Yahoo's default roster uses two centers. You should always change it. Yahoo also still has no third round reversal option.
  > "they still have two centers as their default, which you should always change"
- [4:25](https://youtu.be/J1Eg3uaAICU?t=265) This season Yahoo correctly combines weeks seven and eight into one matchup for the NBA Cup.
  > "They have combined weeks seven and eight into one matchup to become week seven, which is correct."
- [6:56](https://youtu.be/J1Eg3uaAICU?t=416) Watch out for players whose team has a two-game fantasy playoff week. It can be a tiebreaker but should not override a clear talent gap.
  > "the twoame playoff week wouldn't change my opinion on that"
- [8:22](https://youtu.be/J1Eg3uaAICU?t=502) Avoid one-year blindness. Do not let one season flip a long-term narrative such as a player being injury prone or reliable.
  > "people have one year blindness or one year narrow focus, one year tunnels."
- [16:47](https://youtu.be/J1Eg3uaAICU?t=1007) The further down the draft board you go, the less the gaps between slots matter. A gap between picks 1 and 20 is huge. A gap between 50 and 70 is small.
  > "the further down we get the draft board, the differences in positions become less important."
- [17:11](https://youtu.be/J1Eg3uaAICU?t=1031) Points league and category league values can differ a lot. Use rankings that match your format.
  > "this one is dependent on on format. This is why why I talk about coherence."
- [18:02](https://youtu.be/J1Eg3uaAICU?t=1082) Players often slow down the year after a long championship run because they are exhausted.
  > "Many of these guys slow down in the year after the championship. They have to pull back"
- [21:32](https://youtu.be/J1Eg3uaAICU?t=1292) Steals swing from year to year. A drop from three to two steals cuts a third of a player's value in that category, and it can bounce back.
  > "steals change all the time." He went from three steals to two steals, losing 33% of his value"
- [21:18](https://youtu.be/J1Eg3uaAICU?t=1278) Value is relative to where a player is drafted. Fading or buying a player depends on his price, not on liking or disliking him.
  > "It's all about relativity because last season there were times when Dyson Daniels was being discussed"
- [29:46](https://youtu.be/J1Eg3uaAICU?t=1786) Think about team build when choosing between players: positional need, which centers are left, and how much injury risk you already have.
  > "there's team build ideas. Do I need a center? What other centers are available?"
- [29:56](https://youtu.be/J1Eg3uaAICU?t=1796) Winning fantasy leagues comes down to finding players who can jump 40 spots above their draft position.
  > "winning fantasy leagues, if you want to boil it down to one thing, it's finding someone who can jump 40 spots."

## 2026-08-16 [Breaking Down The NBA Schedule For Fantasy Basketball](videos/2026-08-16-gf_6GveiAls.md)

- [1:28](https://youtu.be/gf_6GveiAls?t=88) Before you look at any schedule, check your league settings and playoff dates.
  > "That's the number one thing with any any question that you're doing in any fantasy league."
- [2:30](https://youtu.be/gf_6GveiAls?t=150) The playoff schedule should only break ties between similar players. It should not drive your draft philosophy.
  > "And if you are talking just tie breakers behind between players, then sure, no problem."
- [3:07](https://youtu.be/gf_6GveiAls?t=187) Player value is uncertain. Players picked around 100 often finish around 30, and players picked around 20 can finish around 60. Don't stack your roster based on playoff game counts.
  > "every year a player that was picked 100th becomes 30th. Player that was picked 20th becomes"
- [4:55](https://youtu.be/gf_6GveiAls?t=295) In roto leagues, play to the end of the season. Fantasy playoff schedule details don't matter there.
  > "If you're playing in a roto league, none of this fantasy playoff stuff matters to you at all."
- [6:12](https://youtu.be/gf_6GveiAls?t=372) Because of the tanking rule changes and lottery reform, the speaker expects less resting late in the season, so leagues can end a week later than before.
  > "given the the change in the tanking rules and the lottery reform, I actually think we could push it back a week."
- [7:15](https://youtu.be/gf_6GveiAls?t=435) His recommended end date for fantasy playoffs is March 28 (matchup 21), with a standard 3-week playoff.
  > "is to end on March the 28th. So, I am pushing it back a week."
- [9:26](https://youtu.be/gf_6GveiAls?t=566) Merge the two NBA Cup half weeks (November 30 to December 13) into one 14-day matchup. Also merge the All-Star weeks.
  > "That'll start week seven and I think that should be combined into one matchup over 14 days."
- [13:31](https://youtu.be/gf_6GveiAls?t=811) The difference in total back-to-backs between teams is small (16 at most, 13 at fewest), so don't overweight it.
  > "The difference in backto-backs is 16 for the most and 13 for the fewest."
- [14:53](https://youtu.be/gf_6GveiAls?t=893) Back-to-backs during the fantasy playoffs matter more than the season total.
  > "And what is more important is playoff backto-backs."
- [17:38](https://youtu.be/gf_6GveiAls?t=1058) Most back-to-back problems come from players returning from in-season injuries, and nobody can predict those.
  > "if someone gets hurt in season and comes back, they sit a few back tobacks."
- [21:26](https://youtu.be/gf_6GveiAls?t=1286) Two-game weeks in the fantasy playoffs are bad. This is the schedule factor that actually matters.
  > "Two game weeks, they are bad. That there is in the fantasy playoffs, two game weeks are bad."
- [22:41](https://youtu.be/gf_6GveiAls?t=1361) A top-two seed with a first-round bye can absorb an early two-game playoff week.
  > "So, if you are hyper confident you're going to be a top two seed and your league has a buy"
- [25:22](https://youtu.be/gf_6GveiAls?t=1522) If an early pick with a two-game playoff week falls late enough with no better option, take him. Don't reach for him early.
  > "But if you're debating it at six, seven, don't do it."
- [27:45](https://youtu.be/gf_6GveiAls?t=1665) In head-to-head leagues, categories or points, a two-game playoff week should drop a player down your board.
  > "If you're playing head-to-head leagues, doesn't matter if it's categories or points, it doesn't matter. The twoame week has to drop somebody down."
- [28:43](https://youtu.be/gf_6GveiAls?t=1723) A quality game is one played on a day with few games, so you don't face start/sit decisions. The cutoff should be 11 games (or 10), not Basketball Monster's default of 5.
  > "The cutoff should be either 11 or 10. I actually think 11 is probably right."
- [29:07](https://youtu.be/gf_6GveiAls?t=1747) Quality game totals vary too little between teams to affect draft decisions.
  > "the range of games here if I use 11 as a cut off is between 65 and 70."
- [29:57](https://youtu.be/gf_6GveiAls?t=1797) Schedule quirks (back-to-backs, playoff games, two-game weeks) only matter for your first three rounds of players.
  > "unless it's your first three round players. That's it. So, like I said,"
- [31:29](https://youtu.be/gf_6GveiAls?t=1889) Injuries peak early in the season because preseason and training camp are short. They drop off by mid-December. The late-season spike should be smaller this year because there should be fewer fake injuries.
  > "So, you will get peak injuries. By the time you hit mid December, it all drops"
- [32:38](https://youtu.be/gf_6GveiAls?t=1958) Don't agonize over 12 versus 11 playoff games because too much can change.
  > "Don't agonize over 12 games versus 11 games in your fantasy playoffs because so many things can change."

## 2026-08-11 [The FIRST Fantasy Basketball Mock Draft Of The Year - Jokic Or Wemby At 1?](videos/2026-08-11-OdDkXFhoKsc.md)

- [1:50](https://youtu.be/OdDkXFhoKsc?t=110) The mock league format is 9-category, 12 teams, 14 roster spots, 10 starters, 4 bench, with a third round reversal.
  > "It's a nine category league. 12 teams, 14 roster spots, 10 starters, four bench, third round reversal."
- [8:26](https://youtu.be/OdDkXFhoKsc?t=506) Low-scoring players are harder to build around unless you are comfortable punting points.
  > "the low scoring can be harder to build around unless you're very comfortable just punting that category"
- [8:39](https://youtu.be/OdDkXFhoKsc?t=519) He avoids stacking old players with repeated lower body injuries early in the draft.
  > "So that's a lot of old and a lot of injury, just repeated lower body stuff, which is not what I love to do."
- [11:54](https://youtu.be/OdDkXFhoKsc?t=714) Free throws are the most variable fantasy category. Draft a poor shooter expecting bad free throws, so any improvement is a bonus.
  > "We know that free throws are the most highly variable fantasy category, but if it you at least go in"
- [13:49](https://youtu.be/OdDkXFhoKsc?t=829) A straight 9-cat ranking can be misleading. He uses other measures to judge value.
  > "if you look at a straight NAT ranking, it's going to tell you some stuff that is um not super accurate"
- [17:05](https://youtu.be/OdDkXFhoKsc?t=1025) Players coming off a long Finals run often start slow, with production dips and fatigue.
  > "He's off a finals run. So the these guys often start slow and can see some of their production dip"
- [21:18](https://youtu.be/OdDkXFhoKsc?t=1278) Drafting injury-prone stars like Kawhi and Embiid worked in a large roto league, but head-to-head is a lot different.
  > "by drafting Kawawaii and Embiid in that in that league. So it was Roto and it worked fine for me."
- [22:56](https://youtu.be/OdDkXFhoKsc?t=1376) People overindex on punting. Punting wins leagues, but early in the draft focus on value and lean into a punt later if one appears.
  > "People overindex on punting a lot. I I believe punting is a strong thing. It's a very good thing"
- [36:30](https://youtu.be/OdDkXFhoKsc?t=2190) Take upside flyers from round 10 on. Leagues are won by players who beat their draft slot by a lot. A safe pick that finishes at his draft slot means nothing.
  > "you get a guy at 100 and he's the 40th best player. You you you're there."
- [36:41](https://youtu.be/OdDkXFhoKsc?t=2201) Don't play it safe in round 10. Go for upside.
  > "If you get a guy at 100 and he ends up 100th, it means nothing. So don't go safe in round 10"
- [49:44](https://youtu.be/OdDkXFhoKsc?t=2984) An injured star is fine as a last-round pick to stash in an IL spot. Drop him for a waiver player if the IL spots fill up.
  > "I don't hate him as a last round pick because my last round guy you he goes in my I'll add someone off waiverss"
- [26:07](https://youtu.be/OdDkXFhoKsc?t=1567) A backup big with strong per-minute production behind a starter is worth drafting because he becomes valuable if the starter misses time.
  > "if Duran misses time, Paul Reed's going to be a top 50 player. He's definitely he definitely has to be"

## 2026-08-09 [Why Health Is Hard to Predict: What Stats Stay Stable Year After Year?](videos/2026-08-09-8d--aL_xxwE.md)

- [3:24](https://youtu.be/8d--aL_xxwE?t=204) Correlation scale used: above 0.8 is very strong, 0.6 to 0.79 strong, 0.4 to 0.59 moderate, 0.2 to 0.39 weak, below 0.2 very weak.
  > "between 6 and 79 is a strong correlation between 04 and 0 59 is moderate"
- [5:09](https://youtu.be/8d--aL_xxwE?t=309) Shot profile is very sticky. Three-point attempt rate correlates at 0.92 year to year, and two-point, free throw and field goal attempts are also sticky.
  > "correlation of three-point attempt rate year on year over a fiveyear sample was 0.92"
- [6:08](https://youtu.be/8d--aL_xxwE?t=368) Points, rebounds and assists are the most stable counting stats at 0.89. They also have less game-to-game variance, so they are the most predictable categories for drafts.
  > "0.89 for points, rebounds, and assists, the big three, which is great for us from a fantasy"
- [7:16](https://youtu.be/8d--aL_xxwE?t=436) Season busts and breakouts mostly come from injuries (to the player or someone ahead of him) and random shooting seasons, not from changes in counting stats.
  > "There's probably two to three major reasons why it happens. Injury a guy got injured."
- [8:54](https://youtu.be/8d--aL_xxwE?t=534) Usage is stable at 0.83 and minutes per game at 0.78. To find breakouts, look for role changes such as an injury, trade or free agency departure that frees up shots.
  > "player usage has a pretty stable correlation at 0.83. Again, when we're trying to target sleeper guys"
- [13:58](https://youtu.be/8d--aL_xxwE?t=838) Games played has a correlation of only about 0.3, so it cannot be predicted. Totals rankings and totals projections are garbage, and so is labeling players injury-prone or iron men.
  > "the R number is 0.3. We have no way of predicting how many games somebody will play. None."
- [14:33](https://youtu.be/8d--aL_xxwE?t=873) Injury rule: be cautious with players who have repeated injuries or surgeries to the same lower-body part, especially knees, or an ongoing mystery illness. Hand, finger, shoulder and oblique injuries do not matter much. Concussions matter a little.
  > "if you have had multiple injuries to the same lower body part, particularly knees, including surgeries"
- [17:34](https://youtu.be/8d--aL_xxwE?t=1054) Using two years of history only raised the games-played correlation from 0.3 to 0.35. Limiting the sample to the top 250 minutes players dropped it to 0.2.
  > "the top 250 highest minutes players each season, the correlation went to 0.2."
- [18:05](https://youtu.be/8d--aL_xxwE?t=1085) Assists, points, rebounds, blocks, threes and turnovers all correlate between 0.86 and 0.89.
  > "assists, points, rebounds, blocks, threes, and turnovers. They are all at least 0.86 up to a maximum of 0.89."
- [19:04](https://youtu.be/8d--aL_xxwE?t=1144) Steals (0.74), field goal percentage (0.75) and assist-to-turnover ratio (0.7) are strong but more variable.
  > "74. That's not bad. Field goal percentage 75, assist to turnover ratio 7"
- [20:31](https://youtu.be/8d--aL_xxwE?t=1231) Regress shooting percentages in projections. Two-point percentage correlates at 0.53, true shooting 0.52, free throw percentage 0.49 and three-point percentage 0.45. Free throw percentage is now the least stable standard fantasy category.
  > "the things that need regression, it's shooting percentages. Two point percentage correlation 53."
- [21:14](https://youtu.be/8d--aL_xxwE?t=1274) Do not decide to punt free throws based on one bad season. Free throw percentage swings a lot in both directions.
  > "if you go, "This guy is killing me. I have to punt free throws.""
- [22:24](https://youtu.be/8d--aL_xxwE?t=1344) Turning contested shots at the rim into blocks is very sticky (0.82). Turning potential assists into assists (0.27) and deflections into steals (0.32) is not.
  > "the ability to convert shots contested at the rim into blocks was incredibly sticky. 0.82."
- [25:21](https://youtu.be/8d--aL_xxwE?t=1521) Volume is predictable but accuracy is not. Three-point attempts per game correlate at 0.88 and threes made at 0.86, but three-point percentage only at 0.45.
  > "You can predict taking them, but you can't really predict making them."
- [24:38](https://youtu.be/8d--aL_xxwE?t=1478) Buy-low and sell-high calls often come from three-point percentage swings. A buy-low player has usually had a cold streak from three. A sell-high player has shot something like 60% from three early in the season.
  > "A player who's a buy low usually has had like a two of 20 streak from three."
- [26:16](https://youtu.be/8d--aL_xxwE?t=1576) Using multi-year history does not predict better than using last season alone.
  > "It doesn't actually benefit us really at all versus just looking at last season."
- [26:58](https://youtu.be/8d--aL_xxwE?t=1618) Projection order: minutes per game first, then usage and role, then shot diet, then category production, then efficiency, and games played last.
  > "I first go in and project minutes per game. That's what I try to do first."
- [29:29](https://youtu.be/8d--aL_xxwE?t=1769) As a general rule, do not stack up several players you have injury worries about.
  > "As a general rule, you don't want to just stack up guys that you're a bit worried about."

## 2026-08-03 [New Orleans Pelicans Season Preview - A Team With No Direction](videos/2026-08-03-5QU-jta-lWM.md)

- [32:47](https://youtu.be/5QU-jta-lWM?t=1967) A player on a cheap contract is worth the most in trades early in the deal. His trade value drops as his next contract gets closer.
  > "the closer you get to having to pay him his next deal, the value goes down."

  > "So, I do think scheme can maybe help him a little bit"
- [30:23](https://youtu.be/5QU-jta-lWM?t=1823) Teams that keep competing late in the season can pile up wins in March and April against teams that are tanking.
  > "they were able to rack up those wins in that period of the year when everyone else was trying to lose"

## 2026-08-02 [Re-Ranking The 2026 NBA Draft Class | Dynasty Rookie Ranks](videos/2026-08-02-TOn-D1SV7a8.md)

- [0:38](https://youtu.be/TOn-D1SV7a8?t=38) Do not overreact to Summer League, but still react with some ranking moves.
  > "it's important not to overreact to summer league. I think you all know that. But you should react."
- [3:37](https://youtu.be/TOn-D1SV7a8?t=217) Older prospects who miss their rookie year to injury get bumped down.
  > "I'm an older player, missing his first year, so I bumped him down."
- [11:09](https://youtu.be/TOn-D1SV7a8?t=669) How soon a player can earn a role matters in dynasty rookie rankings. A great prospect in a crowded rotation gets ranked lower.
  > "part of it is where is the immediiacy in role and it's not there."
- [12:56](https://youtu.be/TOn-D1SV7a8?t=776) Summer League production from Lakers players tends to be overrated.
  > "it was also, as happens to Lakers players, overrated because you"
- [15:58](https://youtu.be/TOn-D1SV7a8?t=958) Older rookies are not more NBA ready, but they reach their peak sooner. That makes them more useful for older, contending dynasty teams.
  > "the fact that he is 24 means he will hit his peak sooner."
- [24:18](https://youtu.be/TOn-D1SV7a8?t=1458) Three-point attempt volume is the most translatable Summer League stat for rookies. Shooting percentages are not.
  > "the most translatable part of some league stats for rookies is what his volume was shooting."
- [23:04](https://youtu.be/TOn-D1SV7a8?t=1384) Players in the same tier are close to interchangeable. Pick between them based on your own team.
  > "this is where you have to look at these things and look at tiers and look at ranks and look at your team."
- [21:26](https://youtu.be/TOn-D1SV7a8?t=1286) Even strong draft classes have two or three top-10 picks who bust badly.

- [17:46](https://youtu.be/FEcNjVRlj-U?t=1066) Injuries that come from a player's style of play are more likely to happen again than random contact injuries. Expect more missed games from players who play all out.

## 2026-07-31 [Sacramento Kings 2026-27 NBA Season Preview - Avoid Relegation](videos/2026-07-31-oEywzBZfAvY.md)

- [5:19](https://youtu.be/oEywzBZfAvY?t=319) Don't judge rookies on Summer League. They play next to other fringe players, and opposing defenses go all out to disrupt them.
  > "when at Summer League, it it's not a good representation of who you're going to be on the court"
- [14:17](https://youtu.be/oEywzBZfAvY?t=857) A player's numbers depend on who is around him. Taking away ball-dominant teammates can raise a player's usage and production.

- [13:32](https://youtu.be/oEywzBZfAvY?t=812) Under the new lottery relegation zone, being one of the three worst teams is a penalty, so bottom teams have a reason to try to win games.

- [40:57](https://youtu.be/oEywzBZfAvY?t=2457) When one team in a weak group loses a key player to injury, it can lose several wins. Other bad teams can then pick up those extra wins.

- [34:33](https://youtu.be/oEywzBZfAvY?t=2073) A coach fighting for his job may lean on veterans to win games instead of developing young players.

## 2026-07-31 [Denver Nuggets 2026/27 Preview: Are They Still a Title Threat?](videos/2026-07-31-keNupMSHp1Y.md)

- [22:03](https://youtu.be/keNupMSHp1Y?t=1323) Rest for injury-prone players should be planned before the season from the schedule, not decided game by game. Reactive rest leads to blown minutes limits and players pushing through bad rest spots.
  > "You go into the season and you look at the schedule and you go"
- [23:41](https://youtu.be/keNupMSHp1Y?t=1421) Cutting a player's minutes in a game is not real rest. Real rest means sitting the whole game, because warm-ups, travel and pre-game also add to the workload.
  > "they need to be like no you're out for the game like I'll see you later like take 48 hours off"
- [23:53](https://youtu.be/keNupMSHp1Y?t=1433) Workload is not just the 48 minutes on the court. Travel and the full day around the game add to fatigue.
  > "the game is not the 48 minutes the game is the 24 hours of the day"
- [29:09](https://youtu.be/keNupMSHp1Y?t=1749) Win totals for good teams may need to come down because there may be less late-season (March-April) tanking to pad records. A 55-win team might be a 51-win team at the same quality.
  > "we have to reassess our ideas on good teams and win totals given the potential reduction in the March-April inflation"
- [5:29](https://youtu.be/keNupMSHp1Y?t=329) Defensive wings who come to the NBA from overseas leagues at an older age can make an impact, but it often doesn't last long and the drop-off can be quick.
  > "It doesn't always last a huge amount of time, but for the time where they bring them over"
- [1:52](https://youtu.be/keNupMSHp1Y?t=112) Restricted free agency standoffs usually get resolved in the first week of September.
  > "that's usually the first week in September is when these things get resolved"

## 2026-07-30 [Boston Celtics 2026/27 Season Outlook - No Jaylen Brown, Still A Contender?](videos/2026-07-30-TiiaNZCJNs8.md)

- [13:03](https://youtu.be/TiiaNZCJNs8?t=783) Before expecting a breakout, check the usage picture. When more high-usage stars are on the roster, there are fewer chances for role players, not more.
  > "the whole usage calculation is actually more crowded because you've got Tatum and George versus Brown"
- [13:57](https://youtu.be/TiiaNZCJNs8?t=837) Age matters for breakout talk. A player who has been in the league a long time and is turning 29 is probably who he is, not someone due for a breakout.
  > "He's going to be 29. He kind of is who he is."
- [17:10](https://youtu.be/TiiaNZCJNs8?t=1030) A player's best breakout chance is the season with the most opening. When stars return, expect some step back rather than growth.
  > "That That was last season. I would expect somewhat of a ramp backwards."
- [25:24](https://youtu.be/TiiaNZCJNs8?t=1524) After major lower-body surgery, soreness on the other side from compensating is common. It does not by itself make a player injury-prone.
  > "people can question whether that injury is now is injury-prone. Like that's just a really common impact"
- [36:54](https://youtu.be/TiiaNZCJNs8?t=2214) Late-season games in March and April are skewed by teams tanking. Fewer tanking teams this season means good teams win fewer games and bad teams win more.
  > "whatever happens in March and April is basically fake. You know, 80% of the games"
- [29:50](https://youtu.be/TiiaNZCJNs8?t=1790) Starting a poor free throw shooter can protect him from hack-a-player tactics, because there are no team fouls early in the game.
  > "there are no team fouls at the beginning of a game and you can't play the hack-a-Mitch"

## 2026-07-27 [Dallas Mavericks 2026/27 Season Outlook](videos/2026-07-27-0AptxcRW0RE.md)

- [5:57](https://youtu.be/0AptxcRW0RE?t=357) Overstocked rosters limit minutes. Coaches do not play 12 or more players, so not every rotation candidate gets minutes unless injuries open them up.
  > "No coach plays 12 players, let alone like 15. Like there's no way that all these guys get minutes."
- [6:03](https://youtu.be/0AptxcRW0RE?t=363) Injuries on a deep team can hand real minutes to fringe players, as they did in Dallas the last couple of years.
  > "injuries have allowed, you know, a Nembhard and a Brandon Williams and and you know, all these others to actually get a bunch of time"
- [14:04](https://youtu.be/0AptxcRW0RE?t=844) Lower body and foot injuries are a bigger concern for big men, who jump, contest and land on bodies. Slow recoveries can push them past opening night.
  > "It's a foot injury for a big, which is kind of a big deal. He's also had a lot of lower body injuries."
- [28:33](https://youtu.be/0AptxcRW0RE?t=1713) When a coach publicly talks up a player, pay attention to it as a signal.
  > "if your coach is talking about you, you got to at least pay attention in that way"
- [24:44](https://youtu.be/0AptxcRW0RE?t=1484) Older players coming back from major injuries will likely sit back-to-backs early in the season. That opens games for backups.
  > "Kyrie is not going to play back-to-back especially early on. Like what do they do?"
- [37:05](https://youtu.be/0AptxcRW0RE?t=2225) Draftability of centers depends on who starts. A starting center is worth drafting.
  > "from a fantasy perspective. If Gafford does start, we draft him."
- [35:00](https://youtu.be/0AptxcRW0RE?t=2100) Lottery reform should cause many teams to make 10 to 20 win jumps, since last season's low win totals were partly deliberate.
  > "15, 20 win jumps just because of a the way that they deliberately kept the win totals low"

## 2026-07-26 [Oklahoma City Thunder 2026/27 Season Outlook](videos/2026-07-26-75Sk_4fkgIM.md)

- [2:44](https://youtu.be/75Sk_4fkgIM?t=164) The number of games played can overstate a player's real healthy sample. Many of Jalen Williams' 40 games were limited-minute games while he recovered from injuries.
  > "it was probably 20 full speed games and that had a huge impact across the team"
- [4:16](https://youtu.be/75Sk_4fkgIM?t=256) Losing depth hurts a team more in the regular season than in the playoffs, because playoff rotations shrink to eight or nine players.
  > "They'll have to shrink their rotation like a normal team would to like nine or eight guys"
- [21:59](https://youtu.be/75Sk_4fkgIM?t=1319) Big men with a history of repeated lower body injuries rarely see those problems go away.
  > "bigs who have constantly had lower body injuries, historically speaking, those don't just up and go away"
- [34:14](https://youtu.be/75Sk_4fkgIM?t=2054) A player's shooting efficiency depends on lineup context. Playing next to stars who draw defenders creates more open looks than playing as the lone creator on a bench unit.
  > "the shots that he's being funneled are generated by Shay and they're generated by these guys who have better gravity"
- [36:07](https://youtu.be/75Sk_4fkgIM?t=2167) A good three-point percentage on low volume does not make a reliable shooter. Volume of around five or six attempts per game, or a high share of shots from three, is needed.
  > "if you are going to be a very good shooter it needs to be more than that"
- [37:38](https://youtu.be/75Sk_4fkgIM?t=2258) Shot quality is player-specific. A contested mid-range shot can be efficient for an elite mid-range shooter and a bad shot for others.

- [36:36](https://youtu.be/UTE0dNIv8nY?t=2196) Players on a team that is trying to win are easier to trust in fantasy than players on a tanking team. Tanking teams pull players after three quarters and sit them for much of March.

  > "maybe he doesn't play 34 minutes maybe he's plays 28 minutes a night early on"
