## 2026-07-23 [Summer League Fact Or Fiction: Recapping The Eastern Conference](videos/2026-07-23-LUTYUdXBG1M.md)

- [1:26](https://youtu.be/LUTYUdXBG1M?t=86) Summer league shooting percentages do not mean much. Look for whether the skills that made the player good showed up.
  > "shooting percentages in the summer league don't really mean anything. What we want to see is the things that made you good."
- [14:37](https://youtu.be/LUTYUdXBG1M?t=877) Summer league percentages have some correlation for rookies, but not for second year players.
  > "when we talk about those correlation numbers, that's on rookies, not on second year guys."
- [1:45](https://youtu.be/LUTYUdXBG1M?t=105) Summer league rules such as 10 fouls and single free throw attempts can distort free throw numbers.
  > "they tried out this new free throw situation where you only get one attempt. So, the percentages can be off."
- [8:12](https://youtu.be/LUTYUdXBG1M?t=492) Judge summer league stats in context. On a team with no other talent, high usage and big scoring should be expected.
  > "Look at who's on this team, and he's still only averaged 13." This Sixers team has nobody."
- [15:21](https://youtu.be/LUTYUdXBG1M?t=921) A summer league team with many main roster players usually means the NBA team will be bad.
  > "a summer league team that's filled with like nine rotation or sorry nine main roster players it probably means that team is going to be bad."
- [39:59](https://youtu.be/LUTYUdXBG1M?t=2399) Second year players should dominate summer league. Ordinary numbers from them are a disappointment.
  > "Like give me 16 and eight as a second year guy that should be cooking two games."
- [22:07](https://youtu.be/LUTYUdXBG1M?t=1327) Two-way players with a 50 game limit can still be worth rostering late in the season when they play.
  > "Slawson was playing with the 50 game limit on the two-way contract, you rosted him."
- [17:18](https://youtu.be/LUTYUdXBG1M?t=1038) A flat stat profile without a standout skill limits fantasy upside, even for a player who performs well.
  > "It was an encouraging summer league, but it was still a lot of, "Oh, your stat profile still feels flat.""

## 2026-07-21 [Summer League Fact Or Fiction: Recapping The Western Conference](videos/2026-07-21-RyzcCGChYgs.md)

- [1:12](https://youtu.be/RyzcCGChYgs?t=72) The summer league stats that carry over for rookies are assists, rebounds, blocks, three-point attempt rate and scoring. Shooting percentages and steals have little correlation.
  > "the things we look at are assists, rebounds, blocks, three-point attempt rate, scoring, percentages, steals don't really matter"
- [1:26](https://youtu.be/RyzcCGChYgs?t=86) Judge summer league numbers by context: the player's role, his usage and who else is on the roster. A player on a thin team gets inflated volume.
  > "What role was a player playing? How did the team want them to perform? And one of the key ones, who else was on their team?"
- [2:10](https://youtu.be/RyzcCGChYgs?t=130) Compare summer league usage with the usage the player will get on the real NBA roster.
  > "All of those things are a part of it versus just looking at raw numbers."
- [4:34](https://youtu.be/RyzcCGChYgs?t=274) Watch out for highlight reel bias. Early big games can create hype that the overall production does not support.
  > "I think that the early hype did not match the overall production."
- [22:06](https://youtu.be/RyzcCGChYgs?t=1326) Experienced or older players should dominate summer league. Mid numbers from a player with NBA experience are a warning sign.
  > "the fact that you put up those mid numbers as a bloke with starting NBA experience is is worrying"
- [20:29](https://youtu.be/RyzcCGChYgs?t=1229) In deeper, weekly, roto or games-cap leagues, draft and stash a backup center whose starter could get hurt. He can also be streamed for blocks.
  > "If you have a league with a slightly deeper bench, a weekly league, a roto league, a games cap league"
- [25:47](https://youtu.be/RyzcCGChYgs?t=1547) Rookies usually start slow and improve toward the end of the season.
  > "like all rookies, it'll be slow to start and he'll come good towards the end."

## 2026-07-21 [Charlotte Hornets 2026/27 Season: Ultimate Preview & Insider Secrets!](videos/2026-07-21-EB1Z_6n56-o.md)

- [20:22](https://youtu.be/EB1Z_6n56-o?t=1222) When a team is out of contention, games a player misses with injuries can look worse than they are. On a good team, the same player may play through those injuries.
  > "when this team is good he'll play through them and yeah, that's what happened"
- [36:43](https://youtu.be/EB1Z_6n56-o?t=2203) With lottery reform, fewer teams will finish with very low win totals. Wins shift away from the middle and top teams, so expect win projections to bunch closer together.
  > "with the lottery reform system, there's not going to be four teams that finish under 25"
- [36:51](https://youtu.be/EB1Z_6n56-o?t=2211) Bad teams that used to win about 17 games may now win about 24, because they will play their regular players late in the season.
  > "These bad 17 win teams might be 24 win teams."
- [6:47](https://youtu.be/EB1Z_6n56-o?t=407) When a player has an outlier shooting season on high volume, expect the volume to come back down toward his career norm.
  > "Grayson, the outlier shooting year for him, just happened this past season and the volume's going to come back down"

## 2026-07-20 [9 Bounceback Candidates For The 2026/27 NBA Season](videos/2026-07-20--KS_AZjZnw4.md)

- [4:44](https://youtu.be/-KS_AZjZnw4?t=284) Do not draft straight off last season's rankings. You will miss the players you should jump to grab and take players everyone else avoids too early because they sit high in the rankings.
  > "And the players who everyone's avoiding, you'll grab too early because they're sitting at the top of the rankings"
- [4:35](https://youtu.be/-KS_AZjZnw4?t=275) Some people say projections are pointless and you can just draft from last season's rankings. The speaker disagrees.
  > "Just look at the rankings from last season and if you draft from there, you'll be fine."
- [2:56](https://youtu.be/-KS_AZjZnw4?t=176) Bounceback candidates come partly from role changes, and partly from injuries and shooting slumps.
  > "when we talk about bounceback candidates for this season, some of it is role based."
- [6:26](https://youtu.be/-KS_AZjZnw4?t=386) Injuries have a hidden cost. Besides the missed games, a player stays on limited minutes while ramping back up, so all of his numbers drop.
  > "that's the hidden impact of um injuries is not only does it mean he only played 32 games"
- [17:51](https://youtu.be/-KS_AZjZnw4?t=1071) Several players had big free throw drops for no clear reason. Treat that as a pattern that likely reverts.
  > "Are you seeing a common pattern here? Why did he go from an 85% free throw guy to a 77?"
- [27:36](https://youtu.be/-KS_AZjZnw4?t=1656) Check the context behind numbers. Stats a wing piled up while playing center may not hold when he moves back to his normal position on a healthy team.
  > "you always have to be careful of it where he had those high block rates, high rebound rates, high field goal percentage rates"
- [21:36](https://youtu.be/-KS_AZjZnw4?t=1296) Under the new tanking rules, teams get no real benefit from sitting players late in the season.
  > "And we all know that with the tanking rules in place, there's no real benefit from teams having to sit guys down."
- [22:01](https://youtu.be/-KS_AZjZnw4?t=1321) Teams that do not control their own draft picks have no reason to finish bottom three, so they keep pushing to win.
  > "But those teams that don't have control of their draft picks, there's no benefit for them to finish in the bottom three."
- [12:49](https://youtu.be/-KS_AZjZnw4?t=769) Past high rankings can be misleading. Turner's top 20 finish was a flaw in the rankings, and Zubac's 9-cat rank did not reflect his real value.
  > "when he was a top 20 player, he really wasn't. That was a rankings flaw."

## 2026-07-17 [Can Analytics Solve Fantasy Basketball?](videos/2026-07-17-NYTH7uQsPCM.md)

- [2:59](https://youtu.be/NYTH7uQsPCM?t=179) Analytics describe what happened. Some models project what may happen, not what will happen. Talk about what a player did, not what he is.
  > "what we should be saying is that player got you a lot of assists, or that player did kill your percentages"
- [4:35](https://youtu.be/NYTH7uQsPCM?t=275) Player values are ranges, not fixed ranks. A strict best player available approach in a draft is flawed.
  > "So a best player available idea in a draft is a pretty flawed argument."
- [4:54](https://youtu.be/NYTH7uQsPCM?t=294) When drafting, ask whether you are paying for a 95th percentile outcome or a 50th percentile one. A player whose floor can't get much worse is a big value.
  > "Am I drafting at 95th percentile outcome? Am I drafting at 50th percent, where it could go up or down?"
- [8:59](https://youtu.be/NYTH7uQsPCM?t=539) Shots defended, especially at the rim, correlate with blocks. League average conversion of rim contests into blocks is 13.5%. Expect very high conversion rates to regress.
  > "how many shots do you contest at the rim that turn into blocks? League average is 13.5."
- [10:07](https://youtu.be/NYTH7uQsPCM?t=607) Elite shot blockers can lose blocks because opponents stop shooting at them. You can't block shots that are never taken.
  > "You can't block a shot if they don't shoot it."
- [12:46](https://youtu.be/NYTH7uQsPCM?t=766) A player's blocks can take a double hit: fewer rim contests (from a role or position change) plus regression in his conversion rate.
  > "there are a couple of things that could have a double negative impact on someone's block numbers."
- [13:34](https://youtu.be/NYTH7uQsPCM?t=814) Compare each player's conversion rates to his own career trends. Expect very high numbers to come down and very low numbers to go up.
  > "so any high-level number maybe expect regression. Any low number maybe it jumps up."
- [15:22](https://youtu.be/NYTH7uQsPCM?t=922) Players with very low block conversion could move a couple of points toward average, which adds about 0.2 to 0.3 blocks per game.
  > "Get closer to average. Meaning that you get an extra 0.2 to 0.3 blocks per game from these players."
- [18:38](https://youtu.be/NYTH7uQsPCM?t=1118) Deflections correlate strongly with steals (0.86), but only 49% of deflections become steals, and luck decides who recovers the ball. Very high conversion rates are likely to regress.
  > "only 49% of all deflections turn into steals. Less than a 50% conversion."
- [20:09](https://youtu.be/NYTH7uQsPCM?t=1209) Steals are one of the most volatile categories from year to year. Don't rely on a player's steals from the previous season.
  > "steals is one of the most volatile categories year on year in fantasy. So, when you're relying upon"
- [25:52](https://youtu.be/NYTH7uQsPCM?t=1552) Potential assists correlate with assists at 0.78, and 58% of potential assists became assists last season. On-ball time correlates very strongly with potential assists (0.9) and assists (0.88).
  > "0.9 of on-ball percentage to potential assists and 0.88 for on-ball percentage to assists."
- [27:07](https://youtu.be/NYTH7uQsPCM?t=1627) When two ball-dominant players share the court, both lose on-ball time, so both should lose assists. More minutes can make up for it.
  > "Because if they have it in their hands less, then almost certainly, not always, but"
- [32:21](https://youtu.be/NYTH7uQsPCM?t=1941) Assist conversion depends on how well teammates finish. When two teammates both convert poorly, the cause is more likely the team than luck. Look for context behind the number.
  > "suggests that it's teammate and structural versus all being luck-based. And that's what I mean about analytics"
- [6:54](https://youtu.be/NYTH7uQsPCM?t=414) DARKO DPM is a next-game predictive tool. It does not project end-of-season impact, which is why rookies start low.
  > "It is at this point a next game predictive tool."
- [33:48](https://youtu.be/NYTH7uQsPCM?t=2028) DARKO has only a moderate link to fantasy rank (0.42). It is a per-possession stat, so high-impact players also need minutes to matter in fantasy.
  > "you need to play minutes in fantasy cuz Darko is a per possession stat."
- [34:57](https://youtu.be/NYTH7uQsPCM?t=2097) On-ball time has no link to offensive impact (0.1) or to fantasy rank. It matters for assists, but it doesn't show who is a good player.
  > "Plenty of bad players have the ball in their hands a lot. Plenty of good players do not."
- [35:59](https://youtu.be/NYTH7uQsPCM?t=2159) Plan to build each player's baseline conversion rates (expected blocks, steals and assists) to spot players who are underperforming because of luck.
  > "through luck under performing what we expect. What is their X assists? What is their X blocks?"

## 2026-07-16 [The Biggest NBA Surprise Shooting Risers & Fallers | Potential Busts Revealed](videos/2026-07-16--y6p5PYLf00.md)

- [1:12](https://youtu.be/-y6p5PYLf00?t=72) Free throw percentage, along with steals, is the most variable category from one year to the next. FG% and 3-point shooting also vary a lot.
  > "the biggest variance category year-on-year is free throw percentage. And field goal percentage and three-point shooting is up there"
- [1:43](https://youtu.be/-y6p5PYLf00?t=103) Shooting categories are rate stats with no floor. A bad shooter can keep dragging your team down, and you can lose a lead in the category on the last day of a matchup.
  > "there's actually no floor to how bad you can be in shooting, which has a really negative impact on your team"
- [2:58](https://youtu.be/-y6p5PYLf00?t=178) Don't label a player a bad shooter as a fixed fact. Frame it as how he shot last season. Only extreme cases like Giannis at the free throw line are near certain.
  > "the way we always should be framing that stuff was or is he was a bad shooter last season"
- [4:09](https://youtu.be/-y6p5PYLf00?t=249) 3-point percentage is a hidden category. It affects 3-pointers made, points and FG%. FG% and FT% each affect two categories.
  > "three-point percentage is the biggest hidden category in in fantasy leagues, whether it's points leagues or category leagues"
- [5:41](https://youtu.be/-y6p5PYLf00?t=341) Check whether a player's value is propped up by very high shooting numbers that may not hold, or whether he has room to improve.
  > "would a player have scope to improve a lot, or has their value been, and I'll say this in American for you guys, buoyed"
- [11:35](https://youtu.be/-y6p5PYLf00?t=695) Players whose fantasy relevance depends on elite shooting are risky because of how much shooting can vary.
  > "when your game is relevant based on how well you shoot, and there's this much variance potential, well, it's a bit ugly"
- [14:30](https://youtu.be/-y6p5PYLf00?t=870) Mid-range shooting is low volume, so it swings a lot. Rim finishing is higher volume and somewhat more predictable, but swings there matter more.
  > "Mid-range shooting volume is low, so there tends to be more variance in the mid-range shooting."
- [18:07](https://youtu.be/-y6p5PYLf00?t=1087) Rim finishing is only one part of FG%. An 11-point drop at the rim might cost about 3 points of overall FG%.
  > "You might be losing three percentage points if you drop 11%, and 60 is still a okay number"
- [20:51](https://youtu.be/-y6p5PYLf00?t=1251) Players coming back from major injuries like ACL or Achilles tears almost always lose efficiency in their first season back.
  > "that recovery from big injuries, ACLs and Achilles, it hurts players' efficiencies almost every time in their first run back"
- [22:14](https://youtu.be/-y6p5PYLf00?t=1334) If a 2-point percentage starts with a 7, expect it to come back down. Be skeptical of 70% field goal shooters in general.
  > "If you see a number from two-point land that begins with a seven just expect it to come back."
- [26:15](https://youtu.be/-y6p5PYLf00?t=1575) Teammates who create shots, like elite passers, can strongly affect a player's finishing and FG%.
  > "Trae Young, one of the top five passers in the league, down to CJ McCollum and Nickeil Alexander-Walker. It's an impact."
- [34:57](https://youtu.be/-y6p5PYLf00?t=2097) Overall 9-cat rankings can mislead. If you punt FT, a player's FT% getting worse barely matters to you, even if his rank falls a lot.
  > "that's why I think your nine-cat rankings and total rankings and the way Yahoo displays it is misleading"
- [36:21](https://youtu.be/-y6p5PYLf00?t=2181) Unexpected free throw swings in either direction usually don't last and drift back toward the player's norm. You cannot predict them.
  > "if someone kills your free throws or saves your free throws, especially if it's unexpectedly, probably not going to be a real thing"

## 2026-07-15 [Fantasy Basketball Statistical Correlations & Why Turnovers Suck](videos/2026-07-15-0geFVzSqOnA.md)

- [6:14](https://youtu.be/0geFVzSqOnA?t=374) In points leagues, minutes and usage are the simplest way to predict fantasy points. Choosing between two players on those two factors gets you about 80% of the way to the right answer.
  > "minutes and which player will have more usage, and you're 80% of the way there"
- [7:50](https://youtu.be/0geFVzSqOnA?t=470) Usage matters more in points leagues than in category leagues, though it helps in both.
  > "usage becomes more important in points leagues than it is in category leagues"
- [8:51](https://youtu.be/0geFVzSqOnA?t=531) Points and assists come together. If you target high-points players, you usually get assists too, and the reverse is also true.
  > "if you go for higher points players, you will usually bring assists along with it"
- [9:12](https://youtu.be/0geFVzSqOnA?t=552) The guard build (points, threes, assists, steals, FT%) is common because its categories reinforce each other.
  > "Points, threes, assists, steals, and free throws is the general guard build."
- [13:39](https://youtu.be/0geFVzSqOnA?t=819) The big man build is harder to execute because only rebounds, blocks and FG% move together.
  > "part of the reason why the the big man build is harder to execute is that that's only three categories"
- [13:59](https://youtu.be/0geFVzSqOnA?t=839) Steals are the swing category. They do not tie strongly into either the guard build or the big man build.
  > "we always talk about steals as being the swing number"
- [14:38](https://youtu.be/0geFVzSqOnA?t=878) A big man build does not naturally bring steals or low turnovers with it. Blocks and turnovers are not correlated.
  > "Steals aren't getting brought along. And low turnovers aren't necessarily getting brought along either."
- [17:11](https://youtu.be/0geFVzSqOnA?t=1031) Threes and FG% pull against each other, so adding threes to a big man build is hard.
  > "more threes means lower field goal percentage. Higher field goal percentage means lower threes."
- [18:24](https://youtu.be/0geFVzSqOnA?t=1104) Winning head-to-head categories takes margin. Being barely above average in categories that are negatively correlated leaves you exposed to schedule and injury swings.
  > "part of having success in head-to-head categories is having margin, then you're cooked"
- [19:14](https://youtu.be/0geFVzSqOnA?t=1154) A small positive z-score in a category (like 0.7) wins only about 55% of the time. A large one (like 2.5) wins about 85%. Build big buffers.
  > "If you get a Z score of 2.5 in your assists, you're going to win 85% of the time"
- [21:04](https://youtu.be/0geFVzSqOnA?t=1264) Being strong in both FG% and FT% is very hard. Barely winning both is fragile, and putting resources into it leaves you short elsewhere.
  > "one less game from your free throw volume at anchor means that now you've lost the category"
- [23:02](https://youtu.be/0geFVzSqOnA?t=1382) Players who combine categories that are not normally correlated (like rebounds and assists) carry extra value.
  > "So, players who do the low correlation things are pretty useful."
- [24:26](https://youtu.be/0geFVzSqOnA?t=1466) A low-volume build of threes, steals, blocks, FG% and FT% is very hard to pull off, because those categories do not drag each other along.
  > "So, going for like a low volume build a threes steals, blocks, field goals, free throws really tough to pull off"
- [25:57](https://youtu.be/0geFVzSqOnA?t=1557) Steals are one of the most abundant categories on the waiver wire, and they create oddities in standard 9-cat rankings.
  > "steals are one of the most abundant categories off the waiver wire"
- [29:25](https://youtu.be/0geFVzSqOnA?t=1765) Maximizing FG% or working hard to keep turnovers low hurts the rest of a fantasy team.
  > "turnovers low, is pretty detrimental to your overall fantasy team. That's what that means."
- [30:57](https://youtu.be/0geFVzSqOnA?t=1857) In head-to-head leagues, the speaker ignores turnovers completely.
  > "Cuz you know when I am talking head-to-head leagues, I am telling you I do not care about turnovers."
- [31:10](https://youtu.be/0geFVzSqOnA?t=1870) Exception: turnovers matter to a degree in roto leagues.
  > "You are playing in a roto league, turnovers are one of the categories. It is important."
- [33:23](https://youtu.be/0geFVzSqOnA?t=2003) Games-capped leagues are a little different, but the correlations still apply.
  > "if I'm playing a games cup league, a little bit different. It's a little bit different."
- [35:19](https://youtu.be/0geFVzSqOnA?t=2119) Turnovers are the only negative counting stat in default fantasy formats. Streaming to max games played naturally raises turnovers, so chasing low turnovers fights the head-to-head game.
  > "That's why we stream. Streaming is anti-turnovers. We want more games played than our opponent"
- [36:48](https://youtu.be/0geFVzSqOnA?t=2208) Injuries and schedule disadvantages automatically lower your turnovers, so you often win turnovers anyway in weeks when you are short on games.
  > "If one of your guys gets injured, he accumulates zero turnovers."
- [37:12](https://youtu.be/0geFVzSqOnA?t=2232) Using turnovers as a tiebreaker between two otherwise identical players is fine.
  > "I got no problem if you want to use turnovers between two identical players"
- [37:51](https://youtu.be/0geFVzSqOnA?t=2271) The speaker's Durant ranking system for head-to-head leagues leaves out turnovers.
  > "I'm not including turnovers in it cuz if you want to win a head-to-head league"

## 2026-07-14 [Can Nickeil Alexander-Walker REPEAT His Fantasy PLAYOFF Heroics Next Year?](videos/2026-07-14-xHRF06_E9HE.md)

- [1:08](https://youtu.be/xHRF06_E9HE?t=68) His second-half splits start the Monday after the trade deadline. That skips the odd stretch right after the deadline when traded players are moving and rosters are thin.
  > "because that gives you that time because there's that weirdness when the trade deadline happens"
- [2:24](https://youtu.be/xHRF06_E9HE?t=144) He expects next season's fantasy playoffs to be less extreme. This season about eight or nine teams were tanking or resting players.
  > "But it won't be as bad as what it was in fantasy playoffs a lot of the time"
- [2:07](https://youtu.be/xHRF06_E9HE?t=127) Teams that don't control their own draft pick may still have reasons to lean on young players and protect injured ones late in the season.
  > "they don't control their pick necessarily. So then they might still have some incentive"
- [5:25](https://youtu.be/xHRF06_E9HE?t=325) Late-season numbers are inflated for two reasons. Teammates sit out, and so do players on opposing teams. Discount late-season shooting numbers for this.
  > "when you're playing against other teams, their guys are out, too. So, we have to cut"
- [15:51](https://youtu.be/xHRF06_E9HE?t=951) Yahoo's full-season total rankings can mislead. Players who played a lot of games, like Reed Sheppard with 82, get ranked far too high.
  > "So the metrics tell you again poorly executed and wrongly interpreted metrics. we'll list him as 30th."
- [14:58](https://youtu.be/xHRF06_E9HE?t=898) Don't treat post-deadline numbers as all fake or all real. Check each case for whether the conditions behind the rise will still exist.
  > "either write them all off or say well this is a great indicator for moving forward. That's stupid."
- [16:20](https://youtu.be/xHRF06_E9HE?t=980) Any big ranking jump into top 50 numbers needs a closer look at why and how it happened.
  > "having a rise that big and posting those top 50 type numbers requires investigation."
- [20:32](https://youtu.be/xHRF06_E9HE?t=1232) Be very skeptical of late-season production from Sacramento.
  > "if you ever see something from Sacramento, especially late in the season, your instinct should be a probably terrible"
- [11:28](https://youtu.be/xHRF06_E9HE?t=688) Injury risk works both ways. If a player's injury history worries you, remember his injury-prone teammates will also miss games, and that can open up more usage for him.
  > "if we can be worried about Garland being hurt, we should be equally worried about Ingram not being there."

## 2026-07-13 [The Top 9 Fantasy Basketball Players On New Teams For 2026/27](videos/2026-07-13-Rqb5GdrSweY.md)

- [4:46](https://youtu.be/Rqb5GdrSweY?t=286) When a good player moves to a new team, his production usually dips. There are also ripple effects on his new teammates and on the team he left.
  > "generally a good player moving to a new team, there is some sort of a dip in production"
- [4:35](https://youtu.be/Rqb5GdrSweY?t=275) The 2027 draft looks weak. Combined with the lottery changes, he expects less extreme tanking than usual.
  > "I don't think we're going to have as much egregiousness with tanking"
- [22:13](https://youtu.be/Rqb5GdrSweY?t=1333) Teams that don't own their draft pick have no reason to tank or push for wins. Watch them for players being rested late in the season. Brooklyn and Milwaukee are the main examples.
  > "if I'm worried about any teams, it is Brooklyn and Milwaukee,"
- [9:52](https://youtu.be/Rqb5GdrSweY?t=592) With top-protected picks under the new lottery odds, finishing in the bottom three can give a team a worse chance at a top two pick than finishing 4th to 10th. So teams like Dallas may push harder to win.
  > "Dallas probably has to push a little bit more, I would guess, to increase their odds of keeping a top two pick"
- [6:59](https://youtu.be/Rqb5GdrSweY?t=419) In leagues with a games cap, move injury-prone players up the board because missed games matter less.
  > "Games Cap leagues, you move him up around. Last season, he was 50s, 40s for Games Cap."
- [15:26](https://youtu.be/Rqb5GdrSweY?t=926) Category leagues and points leagues value players differently. A high-usage scorer with few other strengths can be top 10 in points leagues but only a third rounder in category leagues.
  > "top six MVP is a third round fantasy guy for category leagues. Even in points like in points less he was 10th"
- [17:13](https://youtu.be/Rqb5GdrSweY?t=1033) Look at the context behind missed games. Games a player sat out because his team was tanking should not count as proof that he is injury-prone.
  > "I would say that over the two previous seasons out of the games that he missed 50 of them conservatively"
- [20:15](https://youtu.be/Rqb5GdrSweY?t=1215) Don't judge a player from surface-level narratives. Look at his actual percentages and category output.
  > "often people just cut the top just the tip, just the top 1% off in terms of what they're looking at"
- [15:36](https://youtu.be/Rqb5GdrSweY?t=936) A player's own usage matters less than his share of usage next to other high-usage teammates. When a dominant player joins a team, the usage of everyone around him drops.
  > "Brown is not likely going to be a 36 usage guy in Philadelphia which means that that comes down maybe to 30 to 28"
- [9:06](https://youtu.be/Rqb5GdrSweY?t=546) With so much movement and so many unknowns this year, every round of the draft will be volatile. Draft carefully.
  > "every round in fantasy this season I think is just going to be crazy because there is so much movement"

## 2026-07-07 [Could LaMelo Crater Ant's Scoring? Looking At Regression Risks For 26/27](videos/2026-07-07-ME-r173X5b0.md)

- [2:02](https://youtu.be/ME-r173X5b0?t=122) Don't assume a player repeats last season. Look at several seasons for context before valuing a stat line.
  > "they'll just go, "Well, he he shot 40%." From three, okay, sick. He did, but he shot 32 and 33"
- [2:40](https://youtu.be/ME-r173X5b0?t=160) Free throw percentage and steals are usually the two categories that change the most from year to year.
  > "the two biggest variance categories is free throw percentage and and steals year on year"
- [3:16](https://youtu.be/ME-r173X5b0?t=196) Fantasy is often won on the margins. Small decisions add up.
  > "A lot of it is winning on the margins. In fantasy, it can be that way too."
- [5:22](https://youtu.be/ME-r173X5b0?t=322) Small changes in counting stats change value a lot. Going from 30 to 28 points loses about 8% of scoring value. Going from 28 to 33 gains about 20%.
  > "you'd go from 30 points a game to 28 points a game, you're losing 8% of your value"
- [5:53](https://youtu.be/ME-r173X5b0?t=353) Two high scorers on the same team rarely both stay top five scorers.
  > "you're playing on the same team, it's almost impossible."
- [6:55](https://youtu.be/ME-r173X5b0?t=415) A low scorer drafted for other stats hurts points a lot, since the average fantasy scorer puts up about 18 points.
  > "you draft someone scoring five points per game when the average of a scorer in a fantasy league is at 18"
- [9:29](https://youtu.be/ME-r173X5b0?t=569) The baseline for threes has gone up. About two threes a game is now average in fantasy, so the same raw volume is worth less than it used to be.
  > "Now, hitting two threes a game is basically average in a fantasy league. It's a big difference."
- [10:36](https://youtu.be/ME-r173X5b0?t=636) Non-shooters aren't hurt much in threes because threes are easy to find and stream off waivers.
  > "threes are just readily available off waiver wires. So, you can find two three-pointer per game guys"
- [17:53](https://youtu.be/ME-r173X5b0?t=1073) Assists are very hard to find on waivers and are an important category.
  > "assists are incredibly hard to find off the waiverwire and they're a really really important fantasy category"
- [18:59](https://youtu.be/ME-r173X5b0?t=1139) Potential assists per 100 possessions can show whether a player has room to gain or lose assists.
  > "I believe the lowest of those players in potential assists was Jokic, meaning there's two ways to look at that."
- [21:24](https://youtu.be/ME-r173X5b0?t=1284) If you draft a low-assist player early, you can fall behind in assists, and big assist guys are rare late in drafts.
  > "You cannot really find many big assist guys later in drafts. Good luck catching up."
- [25:34](https://youtu.be/ME-r173X5b0?t=1534) Steals are very variable and low volume. He weights them down in his rankings and says not to rely on them.
  > "steals get down weighted because when you're looking at them, they are highly variant year on year game by game"
- [27:42](https://youtu.be/ME-r173X5b0?t=1662) Expect few of last season's top five steals players to be back in the top five.
  > "don't expect hardly any of them to be back in the top five next season"
- [29:45](https://youtu.be/ME-r173X5b0?t=1785) Blocks are very variable from year to year.
  > "much like with steals, blocks are incredibly variable. We have seen this year after year"
- [35:07](https://youtu.be/ME-r173X5b0?t=2107) Players with outlier field goal percentages tend to regress, and a small drop can wipe out most of their edge.
  > "you go from outlier good, 100th percentile to 96th percentile, the that advantage you've created is gone"
- [37:45](https://youtu.be/ME-r173X5b0?t=2265) Over the last two seasons, free throw percentage has changed more from year to year than steals, because both makes and attempts move around.
  > "The last two seasons has actually been more variable yearon year than steals."
- [41:35](https://youtu.be/ME-r173X5b0?t=2495) Z-scores are standardized against the league, so fewer free throw attempts league-wide wouldn't shrink the gap between top and bottom players.
  > "the idea of standardization, it doesn't mean that if you reduce the amount of attempts by half"
- [43:31](https://youtu.be/ME-r173X5b0?t=2611) Punting doesn't mean trying to be the worst. It means ignoring the category.
  > "we remember about punting in category leagues, you are not trying to be bad. You are not trying to be the"
- [45:22](https://youtu.be/ME-r173X5b0?t=2722) High-variance categories (steals, blocks, threes, FT%) are better to punt because you still win some by surprise. Stable high-volume categories like points and assists are bad to punt.
  > "Steals, blocks, threes, free throw percentage, higher variance, way more chance to win them, way more success in punting them"
- [46:45](https://youtu.be/ME-r173X5b0?t=2805) Use last season's top and bottom lists as a baseline only, not as a reason to fade or buy.
  > "This is not to suggest that the guys at the top of the list you fade or the guys"

## 2026-07-05 [Explaining My Stupid NBA Nicknames](videos/2026-07-05-4kKINkZhWls.md)

- [1:04:24](https://youtu.be/4kKINkZhWls?t=3864) A shooting guard who only shoots threes and does not rebound or assist is a bad fantasy profile unless he is elite at it.
  > "that stereotypical shooting guard profile, which is horrible for fantasy and honestly has limited appeal"
- [23:57](https://youtu.be/4kKINkZhWls?t=1437) Be skeptical of preseason hype and of 'maybe he gets the minutes' stories. Opportunity and shooting spikes often do not happen.
  > "Oh, look at Eason in the preseason." I'm like, "No, like he's not going to get these opportunities."
- [35:48](https://youtu.be/4kKINkZhWls?t=2148) Do not overreact to the first week or summer league of a player's NBA career.
  > "Like just insane reactions to the first week of someone's NBA career."
- [58:37](https://youtu.be/4kKINkZhWls?t=3517) When a player who is not a real starter is putting up starter numbers, sell him then, because those numbers will not get better.
  > "I was like you got to trade him now. Like he is never going to put up better numbers"

## 2026-07-02 [Jaylen Brown TRADED | Kessler To LA | NBA Free Agency Day 2](videos/2026-07-02-P6TNP-g0wzY.md)

- [9:40](https://youtu.be/P6TNP-g0wzY?t=580) A high-usage scorer who moves next to other high-usage, ball-dominant players will see his usage and on-ball role shrink, which lowers his value.
  > "So even if Embiid is out, Brown gets usage up, but he doesn't get on-ballness up."
- [18:03](https://youtu.be/P6TNP-g0wzY?t=1083) Players who are elite in only three categories (blocks, FG%, rebounds) get overdrafted in category leagues. Don't take them as early as round three.
  > "will be somebody in fantasy drafts I think in category leagues not points leagues in category leagues that will take Kessler"
- [22:14](https://youtu.be/P6TNP-g0wzY?t=1334) A bench player who gets about 27 minutes a night is enough to be a later-round fantasy flyer.
  > "Cuz if he's a 27-minute a night sixth man, then we're in. Like that's that's enough."
- [28:15](https://youtu.be/P6TNP-g0wzY?t=1695) A scorer who only gives points and threes needs high usage (around 28) and about 40% three-point shooting to be fantasy relevant.
  > "he needs to be a 40% three-point shooter and getting 28 usage to be fantasy relevant."
- [39:00](https://youtu.be/P6TNP-g0wzY?t=2340) When a team has too many players at the same positions, the minutes get spread thin and fewer players are draftable. Project the rotation before you reach for anyone.
  > "But, it's just extra depth that does mean that to me I I have to do it. I have to project it out."
- [30:53](https://youtu.be/P6TNP-g0wzY?t=1853) Watch backup center battles behind injury-prone starters, because whoever gets those starts has fantasy value.
  > "Cuz whoever starts would be interesting to us from a fantasy point of view."

## 2026-07-01 [LeBron Leaves Lakers | NBA Free Agency Day 1](videos/2026-07-01-W3THnI7wWdA.md)

- [14:15](https://youtu.be/W3THnI7wWdA?t=855) When a team loses high-usage players and brings in fewer players than it lost, the leftover usage has to go to someone else. That creates fantasy targets.
  > "bringing LaMelo, but like that's two for one, usage needs to flow somewhere else"
- [14:52](https://youtu.be/W3THnI7wWdA?t=892) A player who has been third in line for ball handling next to two stars can jump in value once one of those stars leaves, especially in assist rate. Check his splits from games when he played with only one of them.
  > "You can go look at his numbers when he played either just with LeBron or just with Luka."
- [11:56](https://youtu.be/W3THnI7wWdA?t=716) When fewer players sit ahead of a bench player in the rotation, it takes fewer injuries for his minutes to go up.
  > "So there's just one extra player out of there. So fewer players need to be out for his minutes to push up."
- [19:09](https://youtu.be/W3THnI7wWdA?t=1149) A backup center is not worth rostering until the starter in front of him is out.
  > "At the moment he's a backup and we leave that alone unless Kessler's out."
- [21:05](https://youtu.be/W3THnI7wWdA?t=1265) A big contract tells you the team trusts the player. Treat it as a signal that his role could grow.
  > "they ponied up that money to keep him around means they've got a level of confidence in what he can do"
- [21:59](https://youtu.be/W3THnI7wWdA?t=1319) Be careful with players who produced late in the season only because starters were hurt. Once those starters are back, the player returns to a reserve role.
  > "I know people will be looking at this guy like, "Well, that's great. I'm going to draft him. He was awesome for me down the stretch.""
- [19:02](https://youtu.be/W3THnI7wWdA?t=1142) A deep bench player who needs several teammates hurt to become a must-draft is not a must-draft player.
  > "Champagne needs a couple of guys injured to be a must draft player I think."
- [13:27](https://youtu.be/W3THnI7wWdA?t=807) In very deep dynasty leagues, roster young players who could develop into starters even if they have no role now.
  > "you're talking dynasty leagues, deep dynasty leagues, 400 player deep leagues, he needs to be rostered."
- [7:22](https://youtu.be/W3THnI7wWdA?t=442) Ignore social media narratives that people repeat without checking, such as the claim that the middle class of NBA contracts has disappeared.
  > "there's always people who are uh incredibly reactive on social media"

## 2026-06-30 [Kawhi Leonard Is BACK In Toronto! NBA Blockbuster Trade](videos/2026-06-30-JMSLg6yz-M0.md)

- [5:31](https://youtu.be/JMSLg6yz-M0?t=331) In a one-for-one positional swap, the fantasy analysis is simple. The incoming player takes over the outgoing player's usage, and teammates' usage moves up or down from there.
  > "It's basically a one-for-one, position for position. You're just tweaking up the usage that Ingram would have been getting"
- [4:43](https://youtu.be/JMSLg6yz-M0?t=283) When a high-usage player arrives, the players who rely on usage to produce (like Barrett and Quickley) lose the most. Players who don't depend on usage (like Barnes) are less affected.
  > "Scottie Barnes doesn't get by on usage. He doesn't thrive from usage. RJ Barrett does."
- [6:20](https://youtu.be/JMSLg6yz-M0?t=380) A good season from a player with a degenerative injury does not remove the risk. Price in the chronic injury risk even after a healthy year.
  > "irrespective of how it played out last season with Kawhi and his health, it doesn't mean that I trust his knee."
- [9:07](https://youtu.be/JMSLg6yz-M0?t=547) Repeated surgeries and problems in the same spot make future missed time more likely. Draft those players lower than their per-game value.
  > "all in the same spot over and over and over again, leads you more likely to have problems that it's going to make him miss time."
- [7:36](https://youtu.be/JMSLg6yz-M0?t=456) A player who needs a lot of the ball can put up big numbers without being efficient. Don't judge players by raw counting stats alone.
  > "you give someone enough of the ball and enough shots, they can put up numbers. But is it the best thing for the team"
- [16:22](https://youtu.be/JMSLg6yz-M0?t=982) Don't invest fantasy picks in low-ceiling role players on bad, unsettled teams just because they might start.
  > "we're not interested in investing in these guys. They shouldn't be, and I don't think we should be from a fantasy point of view"

## 2026-06-30 [These NBA Roles Will Decide Fantasy Basketball Drafts](videos/2026-06-30-4GDfg2n2l8o.md)

- [4:18](https://youtu.be/4GDfg2n2l8o?t=258) Two signs of a year three or year four star leap are a higher free throw rate and a higher assist rate, even for players who are not point guards.
  > "increase in assist rate even if you're not a point guard."
- [25:49](https://youtu.be/4GDfg2n2l8o?t=1549) Early in free agency, don't overreact to single moves. More trades can change the picture quickly.
  > "And it's why like overreactions to individual moves, yeah, can often lead you astray."
- [18:25](https://youtu.be/4GDfg2n2l8o?t=1105) Per-minute big men pile up numbers, but they only have fantasy value if they get enough minutes. Watch for spots where a lack of depth forces those minutes on them.
  > "just not good enough to get enough minutes usually. But what if they're in a position"
- [17:55](https://youtu.be/4GDfg2n2l8o?t=1075) A late-round big is only worth drafting if he can reach about 30 minutes. If his minutes get split down to around 22, he is useless.
  > "if he's got 30 minute only upside that can push to 22 because they want to split"

## 2026-06-29 [Ja Morant TRADED To Portland | What Is Going On?!](videos/2026-06-29-bHA-JoW3reE.md)

- [1:15](https://youtu.be/bHA-JoW3reE?t=75) Mock drafts this early in the offseason are mostly pointless because many moves will still change player values.
  > "I don't do mock drafts at that point, because to me, it's relatively pointless."
- [2:57](https://youtu.be/bHA-JoW3reE?t=177) Avoid giving absolute verdicts on a trade while more moves are clearly still coming.
  > "it's going to be foolish to be giving absolutes here. Because there has to be more happening."
- [5:49](https://youtu.be/bHA-JoW3reE?t=349) When a team adds other high-usage, ball-dominant players, a player's baseline value drops. It only recovers when those teammates are out.
  > "It will pick up when guys are out, but the baseline value won't be there."
- [18:01](https://youtu.be/bHA-JoW3reE?t=1081) There is only one ball. You can't add up every player's previous-season numbers on a stacked team. Scale everything back, and that is where you find value or players to fade.
  > "Everything has to be scaled back. And that's why That's where we end up finding value or finding guys to fade"
- [17:42](https://youtu.be/bHA-JoW3reE?t=1062) You need to look at full rosters and project players before deciding what round someone belongs in.
  > "I need to sit down and look at what the rosters look like. And then I need to go and project all the players out"
- [13:25](https://youtu.be/bHA-JoW3reE?t=805) A player who only scores and is weak in steals, blocks and rebounds has too many category holes to be a standard-league target.
  > "there's just too many sort of holes in what he does, plus uncertainty about role"

## 2026-06-28 [Cameron Boozer or AJ Dybantsa? Ranking The 2026 NBA Rookies](videos/2026-06-28-RsjGTgJiKyI.md)

- [1:48](https://youtu.be/RsjGTgJiKyI?t=108) Points league advice can mislead because default scoring differs between platforms. Yahoo default does not penalize missed shots. ESPN boosts threes, takes points off for misses and weights defensive stats more. Sleeper counts ejections and technical fouls.
  > "Do you mean the Yahoo default scoring where shot efficiency doesn't matter? There's no penalty for missed shots."
- [3:12](https://youtu.be/RsjGTgJiKyI?t=192) For dynasty rookie rankings, judge players over roughly a 4 to 6 year window, not 1 year and not 12.
  > "I'm looking at probably a let's say 4-6 year window of like this is the level of production"
- [2:46](https://youtu.be/RsjGTgJiKyI?t=166) His rankings mix statistical translation with scouting, draft capital and age.
  > "It then gets tied into scouting. It gets tied into draft capital. It gets tied into age."
- [9:23](https://youtu.be/RsjGTgJiKyI?t=563) Players in the same tier are close in value, so you can order them however you like. Weigh how likely each one is to become a 30 minute a night player long term, plus his stats and his team.
  > "You got to take how do you view the players, their propensity to be a 30 minute a night guy long term."
- [7:56](https://youtu.be/RsjGTgJiKyI?t=476) Year one and year two playing time adds dynasty value. A rookie who lands somewhere with immediate minutes ranks much higher than one stuck behind a deep rotation.
  > "Because you get year one, year two production."
- [19:20](https://youtu.be/RsjGTgJiKyI?t=1160) Being the number one overall pick does not make a player the top dynasty fantasy asset. Many number one picks have disappointed.
  > "just because he went number one doesn't mean that he has to be the number one or number two fantasy dynasty guy"
- [22:05](https://youtu.be/RsjGTgJiKyI?t=1325) To spot breakouts among non point guards, look for assist rate and free throw rate climbing over the first six years. That is how a player around 40th overall becomes a top 10 player.
  > "can you envisage or or will you see assist rate climbing over the first 6 years?"
- [22:34](https://youtu.be/RsjGTgJiKyI?t=1354) A free throw rate jump from about 4 attempts to 6.5 or 7 per game can move a player from around 25th to around 5th.
  > "six and a half to seven free throw attempts per game instead of four. That's that's the jump from 25 to five."
- [21:34](https://youtu.be/RsjGTgJiKyI?t=1294) Rookie guards usually struggle a lot with efficiency and turnovers early on.
  > "He's going to be like every rookie guard struggle a lot with efficiency and turnovers early on."
- [20:50](https://youtu.be/RsjGTgJiKyI?t=1250) Do not tweak your ranking formula just to match a gut feeling. Present the data, then give your subjective view separately.
  > "I'm not going to go in and adjust the formula that I use to put him clearly sitting in tier one."
- [13:42](https://youtu.be/RsjGTgJiKyI?t=822) High usage, volume scorers are worth more in Yahoo points leagues than in category leagues, where efficiency, assists, steals and blocks matter more.
  > "If you want to take efficiency and you know, big ramp up of assists and block and steal numbers, he's not as effective."

## 2026-06-26 [Dynasty Fantasy Basketball Rookie Ranks For The 2026 NBA Draft Class - Part 1](videos/2026-06-26-CLsUc0Sevos.md)

- [2:11](https://youtu.be/CLsUc0Sevos?t=131) If your dynasty league keeps only about three players, prioritize only the top two to three rookies and almost no others.
  > "If your league keeps three players, you should not realistically be prioritizing nearly any rookie apart from the top two to three guys"
- [2:32](https://youtu.be/CLsUc0Sevos?t=152) Dynasty leagues should be at least 300 players deep.
  > "Dynasty leagues should be 300 deep minimum."
- [2:44](https://youtu.be/CLsUc0Sevos?t=164) Dynasty leagues should run a separate draft for rookies only, not for cut players or existing free agents.
  > "should have a separate draft for rookies. Not players that get cut, not existing NBA free agents, rookies only."
- [3:27](https://youtu.be/CLsUc0Sevos?t=207) The rookie ranking formula combines age, talent, fantasy skill and draft capital invested.
  > "taking age, talent, fantasy skill, draft capital invested to create a ranking formula"
- [3:41](https://youtu.be/CLsUc0Sevos?t=221) Adjust rookie rankings to your league position. Contenders want players who help in years one and two. Rebuilders can wait for players who break out in years four or five.
  > "They'll bump up in years four to five. And depending on where you sit in your dynasty league, you have to make those adjustments."
- [4:26](https://youtu.be/CLsUc0Sevos?t=266) Players in the same tier are close in value and can be swapped for each other.
  > "Anyone that's in a tier, I find them to be pretty close to each other."
- [5:52](https://youtu.be/CLsUc0Sevos?t=352) Contract status changes a lot right after the draft. Exhibit 10 deals can become two-way deals, so check before you draft.
  > "Some of these players that are on exhibit 10s can be turned into two-ways."
- [23:17](https://youtu.be/CLsUc0Sevos?t=1397) Draft-and-stash overseas players lose value because some of them never come over to the NBA.
  > "cuz if you don't come over, there's a chance he never comes over."
- [26:47](https://youtu.be/CLsUc0Sevos?t=1607) A 24-year-old rookie should ideally be starting and producing right away. Older rookies have less upside.
  > "At 24, you generally would want your rookies to be starting and starting to really do stuff."
- [27:33](https://youtu.be/CLsUc0Sevos?t=1653) Draft capital counts in the rankings, but he trusts it less when it comes from a team he doubts, like the Bucks.
  > "But draft capital was invested. All right, put less faith in that because it's the Bucks."

## 2026-06-25 [LaMelo Ball TRADED To Minnesota! Charlotte, What Are You Doing?!](videos/2026-06-25-ya2VYRJ1BN0.md)

- [19:11](https://youtu.be/ya2VYRJ1BN0?t=1151) When a high-usage star leaves, his usage gets spread among the players who remain. Expect bumps for the secondary options and a dip for a bench scorer who moves into a lower priority role.
  > "So, you're losing Ball Diabate and you're replacing it with Reid and White. So, Miller and Knipel will get bumps."
- [7:59](https://youtu.be/ya2VYRJ1BN0?t=479) A third offensive option needs big minutes and very efficient shooting to matter in fantasy. That is not a likely high-upside outcome.
  > "that guy that's going to need 33 minutes and need to have a true shooting of 61% to be relevant for fantasy"
- [17:52](https://youtu.be/ya2VYRJ1BN0?t=1072) Don't be fooled by a player's per-game rank in nine-category leagues being inflated beyond his real value.
  > "He'll also probably be someone who gets night cat fluff to be looking like a top 30 player. Don't fall for that."
- [7:17](https://youtu.be/ya2VYRJ1BN0?t=437) A team that needs to win will play its star more minutes than a cautious, rebuilding team did.
  > "Minnesota is like we we've got to win, man. Like he's going to play big minutes."
- [10:12](https://youtu.be/ya2VYRJ1BN0?t=612) Games a player missed during a tank may not reflect real injury problems.
  > "Half of the games that LaMelo Ball missed in the last two seasons prior to this last one was not because he was injured, it was because they were tanking."
- [8:24](https://youtu.be/ya2VYRJ1BN0?t=504) Some players' usage spikes when a teammate is out. Losing a frontcourt usage player who shared lineups with them helps them.
  > "McDaniels is one of those players who's usage spikes when somebody is out."

## 2026-06-25 [2026 NBA Draft Recap: 7 Rookies To Draft + Winners & Losers](videos/2026-06-25-lOshTzDA4SA.md)

- [2:20](https://youtu.be/lOshTzDA4SA?t=140) Projections must balance across a whole roster. A player's value depends on teammates, usage and minutes, so a team change can move usage a lot (example: Michael Porter Jr. in Brooklyn vs Denver).
  > "Player moves from one team to another, there's fewer players there. Michael Porter goes to the Nets, usage way up."
- [5:15](https://youtu.be/lOshTzDA4SA?t=315) Don't overrate rookies in redraft. At best a class gives one top 50 player and three top 100 players.
  > "At best you'll get one top 50 guy and three top 100 players. At best. So just always be aware of that."
- [4:22](https://youtu.be/lOshTzDA4SA?t=262) Top rookies are usually bad early and then improve. If you draft one early, accept the slow start and don't drop him.
  > "So if you're drafting him early, you're going to have to just cop it early."
- [7:05](https://youtu.be/lOshTzDA4SA?t=425) The rookie wall is a myth. Roughly 90% of rookies get better as the season goes on.
  > "Rookie wall is a myth. Go back and look at nearly every rookie. 90% of them get better."
- [6:54](https://youtu.be/lOshTzDA4SA?t=414) Don't count on late-season shutdowns by tanking teams giving rookies big minutes in March. That may not happen much anymore.
  > ""Well, in March, they'll sit guys down, and this guy will cook." I I don't know if that's going to happen that much."
- [14:27](https://youtu.be/lOshTzDA4SA?t=867) Uncertain rookies belong in the flyer zone, around picks 120 to 130 in a 12-team league, which is the end of the active roster or start of the bench.
  > "We're talking about a 12-man league, you're picking around 120. So, the start of your bench,"
- [20:04](https://youtu.be/lOshTzDA4SA?t=1204) For rookie flyers, use Summer League and preseason. If a player is named a starter, push him higher. If nothing happens in the first two weeks, drop him and maybe pick him up later.
  > "you draft him and then you'd see what happens the first two weeks and"
- [18:09](https://youtu.be/lOshTzDA4SA?t=1089) A big man with blocks, threes, rebounds and good field goal percentage is a fantasy cheat code.
  > "Cuz he will have the the the cheat code. Blocks, threes, rebounds, um field goal percentage for a big man."
- [22:37](https://youtu.be/lOshTzDA4SA?t=1357) Losing even two to three minutes a game limits a player's upside and lowers his draft value.
  > "lose two to three minutes off what he does, and it drops him down. And then your upside becomes limited."
- [33:00](https://youtu.be/lOshTzDA4SA?t=1980) College players who dominate while four or five years older than their competition are a red flag. NBA role players are usually college stars.
  > "I'm with these players who start dominating when they're five, four years older than their competition in college always is a red flag"
- [24:09](https://youtu.be/lOshTzDA4SA?t=1449) Hot starts built on unsustainable numbers, like extreme rim finishing, tend to fade.
  > "When he was like a 95% rim finisher, was a top 40 guy, and ended up outside the top 150."

## 2026-06-23 [Giannis Antetokounmpo TRADED To Miami Heat In NBA Blockbuster! Game Over For The League?](videos/2026-06-23-nnWX_ObljOE.md)

- [6:53](https://youtu.be/nnWX_ObljOE?t=413) Losing a star does not open up value for everyone on the team when it also gets several players and lottery picks back. Count the usage that leaves and the usage that comes in.
  > "This is not you lose Giannis so everything is cleared out for everybody because you've just gained a bunch of players back"
- [6:22](https://youtu.be/nnWX_ObljOE?t=382) To judge a trade's fantasy impact, add up the usage each team loses and gains.
  > "we're losing Giannis and Porter's usage but we're gaining decent usage back anyway."
- [5:24](https://youtu.be/nnWX_ObljOE?t=324) Be wary of a player whose production came mainly when two or three teammates were out. That production may not carry over.
  > "We saw a lot of what he did last season was when two to three guys were out in Miami"
- [17:09](https://youtu.be/nnWX_ObljOE?t=1029) Players who change teams, even stars, often take a hit in their first year while they adjust.
  > "The players changing teams often get a hit in that first year as they try and figure out"
- [16:47](https://youtu.be/nnWX_ObljOE?t=1007) The adjustment-period hit can be offset if the player gets more minutes on the new team.
  > "players, even high-level players, moving to new teams, there is an adjustment period."

## 2026-06-23 [Randle Dumped To Brooklyn! Claxton To Chicago! NBA Trade Madness Starts](videos/2026-06-23-9tb1ARBEmQU.md)

- [4:55](https://youtu.be/9tb1ARBEmQU?t=295) Offensive load is different from usage because it also counts assists and potential assists. When a team loses ball handlers, the remaining players get more load.
  > "offensive load includes assists and potential assists. So it means more and with no DiVincenzo"
- [12:40](https://youtu.be/9tb1ARBEmQU?t=760) Do not make redraft decisions or draft calls this early in the offseason. Early site rankings are unreliable.
  > "making any redraft decisions and draft calls now is asinine. It's ridiculous. It's stupid."
- [15:23](https://youtu.be/9tb1ARBEmQU?t=923) Stats that backups put up in March and April are often not real. Don't trust them once the team adds players ahead of them.
  > "A lot of March and April is completely fake."
- [10:33](https://youtu.be/9tb1ARBEmQU?t=633) Adding a good player to a team that lacks talent cuts the usage of the players who had been carrying the load.
  > "So, Porter saw his usage go through the roof. It doesn't mean Porter's not going to be good still."
- [12:47](https://youtu.be/9tb1ARBEmQU?t=767) Leagues that stay open in the offseason, like Fantrax and ESPN, let you make dynasty and keeper moves.
  > "at least it's open so you can restart your dynasties or keepers if you've got them"

## 2026-06-23 [NBA Draft Superlatives - My Guys, Best Passer, Best Shooter, Most OVERRATED!](videos/2026-06-23--rgXhs5BHiw.md)

- [1:47](https://youtu.be/-rgXhs5BHiw?t=107) Wait until after the draft to value rookies for fantasy. Landing spot matters, and teams with high-usage veterans leave less usage for rookies.
  > "that's why when we talk about the fantasy value of rookies, we need to to wait until the draft"
- [3:08](https://youtu.be/-rgXhs5BHiw?t=188) Consensus draft boards are often wrong. Every year, players picked in the teens, 20s and second round turn out better than their slot.
  > "picked in the teens that should have been in the top five and in the 20s who should have been"
- [15:11](https://youtu.be/-rgXhs5BHiw?t=911) Dynasty rookie value combines the player, age, stats, draft slot and landing spot.
  > "The player, their age, their stats, their draft slot, their landing position. That's all part of it."
- [25:05](https://youtu.be/-rgXhs5BHiw?t=1505) Draft capital is one of the biggest indicators of NBA career length. High picks get chance after chance, while late picks get small contracts, so draft slot matters in dynasty rankings.
  > "draft capital, which is one of the biggest indicators for length of NBA career, which is why when we talk dynasty rankings"
- [10:59](https://youtu.be/-rgXhs5BHiw?t=659) Prospects who are much older, around 24 as rookies, have rarely become NBA success stories. Being older does not make a player immediately NBA ready.
  > "the history of players at this age having any sort of NBA success is it's minuscule"
- [17:27](https://youtu.be/-rgXhs5BHiw?t=1047) Big men can build fantasy value from field goal percentage, blocks and rebounds even without a full offensive game.
  > "So many of these guys are able to do that by translating field goal percentage, blocks, rebounds into fantasy value."
- [18:25](https://youtu.be/-rgXhs5BHiw?t=1105) Players with high steal and block rates translate well to fantasy. In deep dynasty rookie drafts, keep an eye on late picks or undrafted players with interesting stat translations.
  > "When you're in dynasty rookie drafts and you're picking a pick 50 and Castro was undrafted or whatever"
- [19:10](https://youtu.be/-rgXhs5BHiw?t=1150) Defensive stats and rebounding give a rookie a fantasy baseline that can offset weak usage efficiency.
  > "he's going to have the baseline of defensive stats and rebounding to add on to the other things"
- [8:55](https://youtu.be/-rgXhs5BHiw?t=535) Treat college stats with caution when a player came from a strong team with a great coach, because his teammates may have boosted his numbers.
  > "they were on this powerhouse team with an awesome coach, and they all sort of worked off each other"

## 2026-06-22 [2026 NBA Draft MOCK DRAFT | All 60 Draft Picks!](videos/2026-06-22-HxQjagSTTAM.md)

- [1:46](https://youtu.be/HxQjagSTTAM?t=106) Draft position is unreliable. Every year a player outside the lottery becomes a top 10 player in his class, and a top 10 pick disappoints.
  > "There is going to be a player outside the lottery who is a top 10 player in this draft."
- [6:09](https://youtu.be/HxQjagSTTAM?t=369) Players picked in the 20s, such as OG Anunoby, Pascal Siakam and Desmond Bane, have become excellent players. Do not write off a prospect because of a late projection or bench numbers in college.
  > "I love that for OG Anunoby going in the 20s. I love that for Pascal Siakam going in the 20s."
- [19:38](https://youtu.be/HxQjagSTTAM?t=1178) In dynasty, statistical translations rate high field goal percentage, high block rate big men very highly. These players often go 5 to 10 spots earlier in dynasty drafts than their NBA draft slot.
  > "you will most certainly will see him go in dynasty leagues five to 10 slots higher."
- [11:30](https://youtu.be/HxQjagSTTAM?t=690) Age and context matter when judging college stats. Older prospects, and players on dominant teams with other strong frontcourt players, may not carry their numbers over to the NBA.
  > "Yaxel's numbers are great. Like don't get me wrong. steals, good blocks, good threes"
- [10:54](https://youtu.be/HxQjagSTTAM?t=654) Draft picks should not be made only for the current roster fit. Some planning for the future is needed.
  > "can't make it all exclusively for what's going on right now. There's got to be a little bit of forward planning."
- [5:48](https://youtu.be/HxQjagSTTAM?t=348) Offseason trades often happen around draft time, so rankings and outlooks can change quickly.
  > "So, just be aware that I might be recording this right now, and then an hour later another story might come out."
